title: Agave Dijon Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad agave dijon salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (1 batch) equipment vitamix 2 pitchers ingredients 1 ¼ cups apple cider vinegar ½ cup + 2 tbsp dijon mustard ½ cup + 2 tbsp agave 3 ½ cups light olive oil ½ cup water preparation add all ingredients except oil in the vitamix container and mix on low. drizzle oil into the vitamix while mixing. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Alt Moroccan Red Lentil Soup
text: all recipes / soup alt moroccan red lentil soup tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (14–15 qts) equipment 32qt (largest) stock pot with pot-saver under it zester juicer mini cuisinart ingredients ~⅓ cup olive oil (to coat bottom of stock pot) 2 ½ lbs onions, ½” dice 2 lbs carrots, ½” dice 7 stalks celery, ½” dice 20 cloves garlic, chopped in mini-cuis (easier if thawed a bit) 3 tbls + 1 tsp ground coriander (can either toast & grind seeds or use pre-ground) 5 tsp ground cumin (can either toast & grind seeds or use pre-ground) 5 tsp turmeric 2 ½ tsp paprika (not smoked, just regular or "hungarian") 1 ¼ tsp cinnamon 2 ½ tsp salt 1 ¼ tsp pepper 10 qts veg broth (= 1 ¼ jar better than bouillon dissolved in 1 qt hot tea water + 9 qts water) 1 6lb can + 1 28oz can diced tomatoes 10 cups red lentils, rinsed 4 bunches kale, torn into pieces ½ cup + 2 tbsp (=~3) lemons, juiced ... save some zest in case needed ¼ tsp cayenne 1 ¼ cup flat-leaf parsley, chopped (1 cup = after finely chopping) 4 bunches fresh cilantro, roughly chopped, served on the side ~48 oz yogurt, served on the side (ideally greek) preparation prepare ingredients: locate all ingredients. measure out lentils and set aside. dice onions, carrots & celery. kale: remove thick stem from center, tear into large bite-sized pieces. wash lemons. zest 1–2 lemons (=scrape off the thin outermost yellow layer of skin) using either the microplane (sharp!) or box grater (suggest wearing the cut-resistant glove for either). set aside in case needed at the end. juice lemons using electric juicer or wooden reamer. wash parsley, discard main trunk of stems, finely chop the rest. chop garlic in mini cuisinart on chop setting (best if thawed). if preferred: toast and grind cumin & coriander using a small skillet, watching carefully just till fragrant. grind in the black spice grinder, wiping it out before and after. or just use pre-ground. sauté: be sure heat-saver disk (on stove shelf) is placed under the stock pot. coat the bottom of the pot with olive oil to about ⅛” deep. sauté (=fry in a little oil uncovered, stirring occasionally) the onions until they are getting soft. add in the carrots & celery and 2 tsp salt. sauté for 20 minutes or so to develop the flavor. add the garlic, coriander, cumin, turmeric, paprika, cinnamon, salt and pepper and continue cooking for another 2–3 minutes, stirring the whole time. cook lentils: (~2:30) add broth, tomatoes and lentils. stir well and heat to a boil. be sure there is a pot-saver/heat disperser under the pot. let it simmer at least until the lentils are soft (1 hr or more) — fine to leave it on 2 hrs or more, or until it's time to leave for the meeting. stir frequently, add more water if it's getting too thick. add greens: (~4:20) just before going to the orientation meeting, stir in the kale. turn the fire off and put a lid on the pot. final seasoning: (~5:15, leave meeting early) stir in lemon juice, cayenne, and parsley. re-heat ~10 minutes. taste and adjust seasoning (maybe more salt or lemon zest).

title: Steamed Broccoli
text: all recipes / side steamed broccoli tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × you may need to wash the steamer pans used for the tempeh to reuse for the broccoli, or maybe the veggie choppers have set it up already. we're doing a whole case, so you may need to do 2 rounds — it can all be finished a bit early, anytime from 11:30 onward or so, and served room temperature if needed. equipment 2 - 6” hotel pans 2 steamer pans 2 lids ingredients 1 whole case broccoli preparation setup 2 steamer assemblies: get the two 6” deep (deepest) solid pans and fill them with 2” of water. set the water-filled pans across 2 burners each. divide into the 2 perforated pans as much broccoli as will fit with the lid fully closed. set the perforated pans in the water-filled pans and put a lid on each. turn on both burners. let the broccoli steam for about 5 minutes after the water comes to a boil. carefully lift the lid and check on it. when it looks done, remove the perforated pans from the base pans and empty the broccoli into a large metal serving bowl. refill one or both pans with any remaining broccoli and steam for just 2–3 minutes (we may use some of these for further baking, so leave barely done). leave the pans on the counter (out of the water) so we can serve more if needed.

title: Alt Notes on Recipe Polenta
text: all recipes / side alt notes on recipe polenta tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × simplified to be all vegan, no cheese — serve cheese on the side for the whole meal. if making 3 pans: we only have 2 4” deep full pans, so use 2 4” half pans or a 6” deep one for the third and save that one for a supper leftover. yield: ask km how many pans — usually 2 if no supper (or a supper "minestrone" soup is planned), 3 if a supper casserole is planned (only 1 for a group of ~36 with no supper use). quantities below are per full pan. equipment if supper: 3 full pans (serve 2, save the other for supper); if no supper, just 2 full-size pans use the 4” (medium depth) pans so it doesn't slosh when putting in the oven ingredients (per full pan) 5 cups polenta 20 cups = 5 qts water with bouillon (3 t bouillon paste mixed with 1 quart of hot tea-urn water per pan, other 4 quarts water cold) (1 t) additional salt — optional, the bouillon is already salty, taste at the end before adding 2 t olive oil 2 t dried basil 1 t white pepper ½ c?? nutritional yeast — optional, quantity needs to be verified ~¼ cup per pan earth balance — optional, stir in at the end if using preparation mix and bake polenta: preheat oven to 425. spray pans with spray oil. mix polenta and seasonings in each of the pans you are using. leave pans uncovered and put them in the oven about 10:15. set a timer for an hour. stir & maybe cover: about 11:15, carefully with hot pad gloves (and maybe with help) remove the pans and stir. peek every 20 minutes or so — if the top is getting too brown, put the lid on. if done, turn off ovens and leave pans inside to stay warm. maybe stir in some earth balance at the end. stovetop alternate: use 4:1 water to polenta as above, so the equivalent of the standard 2 oven pans would be maybe 40 c (=10 qts) of water to 10 cups polenta. bring 20 c = 5 qts water to a boil. mix polenta with 10 c cold water to make a slurry. add to the boiling water. stir very often, slowly adding the final 10 cups of water as it thickens. use your judgement if more water is needed for a thick but ladle-able consistency. salt to taste. sheet-pan alternate (notes from cook susan black, makes little squares): prepared on the stovetop, using the same amount as the stovetop version above — same amount of bouillon, plus earth balance and whatever herb you like (just not as much as the other recipe, ¼ to half), and no pepper. key is to stir in the earth balance as it is becoming polenta, not into the water — the closer to done you add it, the less you need and it will taste creamier. quantity of earth balance is about ½ cup, then to taste. olive oil gives it a bit of herbaceous taste; you can mix in both. pour into a sheet pan when done, smooth and creamy — it cools quickly and can be cut into triangles or squares. cooking it in two separate pots (1 per sheet pan) means each pan can use half quantities, since one sheet pan can be cut into about 50 medium-to-large slices; grease the sheet pan before pouring. if you make two sheet pans, the extra one can be used the next day or frozen for later (it freezes well); if used the next day it can be fried lightly in earth balance or oil for a crispy texture, or simply brushed with olive oil or melted earth balance on top and baked low (while reheating) to crisp up a bit. the creaminess comes from the earth balance, but olive oil or any vegan fat could be used instead. fancier idea (maybe for a supper leftover portion): pour the polenta over roasted mushrooms (or any roasted vegetable — zucchini, bell pepper, etc.) spread on the sheet pan and let cool, for toasted mushroom (or vegetable) polenta.

title: Alt Portuguese Kale White Bean Soup
text: all recipes / soup alt portuguese kale white bean soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × adapted from moosewood restaurant favorites. yield: ~48 servings (14–15 qts) — this gets eaten, no useful leftovers expected equipment 32qt (largest) stock pot with pot-saver under it zester juicer spice grinder mini cuisinart separate 12 qt pot (to give beans a head-start) ingredients whole lg jar (32-34oz) sun-dried tomatoes, oil-packed, drained (reserve oil for sauté) olive oil, if needed to supplement sun-dried tomato oil for sauté 4 lbs onions, ½” dice 2 lbs carrots, ½” dice ~4-6 bulbs fresh fennel bulbs (quantity depends on size), ½” dice 4 lbs potatoes (ideally yukon gold), ½” dice 14 cloves garlic, chopped in mini-cuisinart 4 ½ tbls fennel seeds, very lightly toasted and ground 4 ½ tbls thyme 2 ½ tsp salt 1 ¼ tsp pepper 7 qts veg broth (= 1 jar better than bouillon dissolved in 1 qt hot tea water + 6 qts water; use the bean cooking water if you did them separately) 1 lg (+ 1 med) canned diced tomatoes (i.e. 1 6lb6oz + 1 28oz, or ~4.5 28oz cans) 2 qts dry, cooked cannellini (white) beans (about 2 qts dry, or ~6-7 28oz cans) 5 bunches kale, torn into pieces (very roughly 2”x2” sized) ~1 cup (=~8) lemons, juiced ... save some zest in case needed / add to taste preparation prep ahead: soak dry cannellini beans overnight — if you forget, try the quick-soak method (see side notice area), or use ~7 x 28oz canned beans instead. cook beans: note: km will have pre-soaked the beans. rinse soaked beans. in a separate 12 qt pot, cover with fresh water, bring to a boil, and immediately turn to a low simmer, skimming if needed; toss in a stalk of fresh rosemary. add to the main soup pot mid-afternoon — they can continue to cook there. locate & prepare ingredients: strain off the oil from the oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, saving the oil to sauté the onions in the step below. set the tomatoes aside. when ready to transfer the beans, use bean broth and/or water as needed to make bouillon with better than bouillon. dice onions, carrots, fresh fennel, and potatoes. kale: remove thick stem from center, tear into large bite-sized pieces. wash lemons. zest 1–2 lemons (=scrape off the thin outermost yellow layer of skin) using either the microplane (sharp!) or box grater (suggest wearing the cut-resistant glove for either). set aside in case needed at the end. juice lemons using juicer (near rice cooker). lightly toast the fennel seeds dry in a small skillet. grind using spice grinder. chop garlic in mini cuisinart on chop setting (best if thawed). sauté: be sure heat-saver disk (on stove shelf) is placed under the stock pot. using the reserved sun-dried tomato oil if you have it, or else olive oil, sauté the onions until they are getting soft. add in chopped garlic and 2 tsp salt. sauté another minute. add the ground fennel and diced fennel and cook for ~10 minutes. stir in the carrots, potatoes, thyme, sun-dried tomatoes and black pepper and cook for ~20 minutes. combine & cook soup: about 2:30-3:00, add tomatoes, bouillon and beans. stir well, bring to a boil and reduce to a simmer. be sure there is a pot-saver/heat disperser under the pot. simmer until potatoes are just tender. add greens: just before going to the orientation meeting, stir in the kale. final seasoning: after the orientation meeting, just before serving, stir in (some) lemon juice & zest to taste and salt to taste.

title: Alt Recipe Pumpkin Cornbread
text: all recipes / side alt recipe pumpkin cornbread tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × note: see the simpler "vegan gf cornbread" recipe — all versions of this one have eggs. decide with km how many gf/df or regular pans to make; typical for a full house would be 3 half-pans regular, 1 half-pan gf/df. or, if too much trouble, you can make it all gf/df. if you have no-egg people, consider making a small sauce pot of polenta on the stove (1 part polenta : 4 parts water) instead. yield: scales for 1–4 half-size (2”) hotel pans; ingredient amounts below are given per pan count (4 pans / 3 pans / 2 pans / 1 pan) equipment 1-4 2” half-sized hotel pans (cooks more reliably in half-pans than whole pans) 2 large bowls maybe 2 smaller bowls for gf/df version ingredients — wet, dairy version canola oil — 4 pans: 2 ½ c · 3 pans: 1 ¾ c + 2 tbls · 2 pans: 1 ¼ c · 1 pan: ½ c + 2 tbls brown sugar — 4 pans: 1 c · 3 pans: ¾ c · 2 pans: ½ c · 1 pan: ¼ c eggs, beaten — 4 pans: 20 · 3 pans: 15 · 2 pans: 10 · 1 pan: 5 yogurt — 4 pans: 7 ½ c · 3 pans: 5c + 2 tbls · 2 pans: 3 ¾ c · 1 pan: 1 ¾ c + 2 tbls pumpkin puree — 4 pans: 5c · 3 pans: 3 ¾ c · 2 pans: 2 ½ c · 1 pan: (n/a) ingredients — wet, no-dairy version canola oil — 4 pans: 2 ½ c · 3 pans: 1 ¾ c + 2 tbls · 2 pans: 1 ¼ c · 1 pan: ½ c + 2 tbls brown sugar — 4 pans: 1 c · 3 pans: ¾ c · 2 pans: ½ c · 1 pan: ¼ c eggs, beaten (or "egg substitute"?) — 4 pans: 20 · 3 pans: 15 · 2 pans: 10 · 1 pan: 5 pumpkin puree (1 box = 2 cups) — 4 pans: 8c · 3 pans: 6c · 2 pans: 4c · 1 pan: 2c rice milk — 4 pans: 4 ½ c · 3 pans: 3 ¼ c + 2 tbls · 2 pans: 2 ¼ c · 1 pan: 1c + 2 tbls ingredients — dry (vary flour type to get regular or gf version) cornmeal (ideally ~⅔ medium grind, ⅓ polenta, but any combo will do including all one or the other) — 4 pans: 10c · 3 pans: 7 ½ c · 2 pans: 5c · 1 pan: 2 ½ c flour (either regular white or bob's 1-1 gluten free) — 4 pans: 10c · 3 pans: 7 ½ c · 2 pans: 5c · 1 pan: 2 ½ c salt — 4 pans: 5 tsp · 3 pans: 3 ¾ tsp · 2 pans: 2 ½ tsp · 1 pan: 1 ¼ tsp baking powder — 4 pans: 10 tbls · 3 pans: 7 ½ t · 2 pans: 5t · 1 pan: 2 ½ t preparation preheat oven to 350. mix the wet ingredients together in one bowl and the dry in a separate bowl (also keeping the different diet versions separate, so perhaps 4 bowls needed). spray all the pans with spray oil. mix the wet and dry together (for each diet version). just lightly until mixed, don't over-stir. fill the pans and bake at 350 for about 45 minutes (range could be 30-60). done when lightly brown, lightly patting the top feels solid, toothpick comes out clean. let it cool a bit and pre-slice with a bread knife into 4x3=12 or 4x4=16 pieces per pan. serve with butter and earth balance.

title: ALT Recipe Quinoa and Vegetable Stew
text: all recipes / entree alt recipe quinoa and vegetable stew tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × this is a hearty, veggie- and quinoa-packed latin stew. it's full of nutritious ingredients and bright, fresh flavors — a healthy soup you'll want all year round! adapted from cookingclassy.com, itself adapted from the cook's country one pan wonders cookbook. yield: original recipe serves 6 (prep 15 min, cook 40 min, total ~55 min). quantities below are given as full-house batch / ~33-serving batch (with 4 qts leftover) / original single recipe. ingredients olive oil — full house: 12 tbsp · original: 2 tbsp onion, chopped — full house: 6 · original: 1 red bell pepper, stemmed, seeded and cut into 1/2-inch pieces — full house: 7 · ~33 servings: 6 · original: 1 garlic, minced — full house: 25 · original: 5 paprika — full house: 7 · ~33 servings: 6t · original: 1 tbsp ground coriander — full house: 4t+2t · ~33 servings: 4t · original: 2 tsp ground cumin — full house: 3.5t · ~33 servings: 3t · original: 1 1/2 tsp vegetable broth, then more as needed — full house: ?10qt · ~33 servings: 36=9qt · original: 6 cups red potatoes, unpeeled, cut into 1/2-inch pieces — full house: 7lb · ~33 servings: 6lb · original: 1 lb prewashed or rinsed quinoa — full house: 7c · ~33 servings: 6c · original: 1 cup fresh or frozen corn — full house: 7c · ~33 servings: 6c · original: 1 cup tomatoes, cored and chopped coarse — full house: 14 · ~33 servings: 12 · original: 2 frozen peas — full house: 7c · ~33 servings: 6c · original: 1 cup salt and pepper queso fresco or feta cheese, crumbled — full house: 28? · ~33 servings: 24oz · original: 4 oz avocado, halved, pitted and diced — full house: 7 · ~33 servings: 6 · original: 1 minced fresh cilantro — full house: 4c · ~33 servings: 3c · original: 1/2 cup preparation heat oil in a dutch oven over medium heat. add onion and bell pepper and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. stir in garlic, paprika, coriander, and cumin and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. stir in broth and potatoes and bring to a boil over high heat. reduce heat to medium-low (covering the pot from this point on works well) and simmer gently for 10 minutes. stir in quinoa and simmer for 8 minutes. stir in corn (can wait to add corn until adding the peas if using frozen corn) and simmer until potatoes and quinoa are just tender, about 5–7 minutes. stir in tomatoes and peas and cook until warmed through, about 2 minutes. remove from heat, season with salt and pepper to taste. (stew can be refrigerated for up to 2 days.) add additional broth as needed to thin the sauce when reheating. sprinkle each serving with queso fresco, avocado and cilantro before serving. note: do not omit the toppings — they are key to the flavor of this soup.

title: Carrot Cashew Soup
text: all recipes / soup carrot cashew soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × (this recipe needs further work — a placeholder version, good enough for now.) yield: ~14 quarts equipment heaviest 32qt stock pot immersion blender ingredients 14 lbs carrots (could pre-slice the day before in the robo coupe) 3 lbs onions, diced 1 lb ginger (optional: <= 5 lbs leftover yams) 3 lbs cashews 2 t 5-spice powder preparation cover cashews with water and soak for 1–2 hours (i.e. do it at the start of veggie chop, leave it till 9:30). dice onions. locate ~14 lbs of carrots & maybe yams: excess already shredded, leftover roasted yams. chop the ginger in batches in the mini-chopper (roughly cut up first, no need to peel if organic). sauté the onions in the large rondo pan until getting soft (20-30 minutes, not till browning). add carrots (and yams) and continue to sauté, stirring often over low heat until some light browning, not too brown. while these sauté: puree the cashews in the vitamix (multiple batches if needed). add ginger and 5-spice powder & sauté another minute or two. add cashew milk and water to bring it up to ~14 qts. bring to a boil, reduce to simmer stirring frequently. after all ingredients are soft, use immersion blender to blend smooth. taste for seasonings and salt, or add more 5-spice as needed, or salt, pepper, lemon juice. aim to have it about 170 degrees by lunch time. then turn off the gas and leave the pot covered on the stove — it should stay above 145 for the afternoon. reheat at 5:00 to bring it back to 165. optional: serve with yogurt if there are still 2x32oz left for final breakfast.

title: Apple Cake Easy
text: all recipes / dessert apple cake easy tags: vegetarian, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × good with non-diet ingredients, so-so with gf flour, rather weird with vegan egg. maybe make it non-diet and offer an oat-crumble or baked apples for diets — so not so "easy" if dietary needs are involved. yield: scales via 4x (2 full pans, original for a full retreat) / ½x (8x8 pan) / 1x (orig, 9x13 pan) ingredients sugar — 4x: 3 c · ½x: ½ c (still too sweet at this amount) · 1x: 1 c (orig recipe called for 1-3/4 cups — deemed too much) vegetable oil — 4x: 4 c · ½x: ½ c · 1x: 1 cup eggs — 4x: 12 · ½x: 1 ½ · 1x: 3 (note: wouldn't work without eggs — make baked apples for a no-egg side?) vanilla extract — 4x: 4 t · ½x: ½ t · 1x: 1 teaspoon all-purpose flour (fine with gf) — 4x: 8 c · ½x: 1 c · 1x: 2 cups baking powder — 4x: 5 t · ½x: ½ + 1/8 tsp · 1x: 1-1/4 teaspoons salt — 4x: 4 t · ½x: ½ t · 1x: 1 teaspoon cinnamon — 4x: 2 t · ½x: 1 t · 1x: ½ t cardamom — 4x: 1 t · ½x: ½ t · 1x: ¼ t nutmeg — 4x: 1 t · ½x: ½ t · 1x: ¼ t baking soda — 4x: 1 t · ½x: 1/8 t · 1x: 1/4 teaspoon granny smith apples, quantity depends on size of apples — 4x: 12-20 · ½x: 2-3 · 1x: 3-5 chopped walnuts or pecans, optional — 4x: 4 · ½x: ½ · 1x: 1 cup whipped topping — 4x: 3 pints · 1x: 1-1/4 cups preparation quarter and core the apples, then use robocoupe to thin-slice the apples. in a large bowl, beat the sugar, oil, eggs and vanilla until well blended. combine the flour, baking powder, salt, cinnamon and baking soda; gradually beat into sugar mixture until blended. fold in apples (and nuts). this is a stiff batter — best to mix using (gloved) hands to get it well-mixed. transfer to a greased pan. bake at 350° for 45-60 minutes or until browning on top & a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean. serve with whipped topping. make cashew cream (recipe in other recipes folder) for non-dairy. source: originally published as "easy apple cake" in light & tasty (tasteofhome.com/recipes/easy-apple-cake).

title: Apple Crisp
text: all recipes / dessert apple crisp tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × below shows quantities for 1 ½ hotel pans with wheat & butter, plus a half-pan with gf flour and earth balance. yield: ~1 ½ full hotel pans (wheat/butter version) plus a half-pan gf/earth balance version (total ~16 lbs apples for 2 pans) ingredients — filling large apples (half granny smiths, half something sweeter) — 1 ½ hotel pans: 30-36 (~12+ lbs) · ½ pan gf: 10-12 (~4+ lbs) juice of a couple of lemons in water, to save apples as you work granulated sugar — 1 ½ hotel pans: 1 ½ cup · ½ pan gf: ½ cup flour/gf flour — 1 ½ hotel pans: ¾ c · ½ pan gf: 4 tablespoons cinnamon — 1 ½ hotel pans: 6t · ½ pan gf: 2 teaspoon kosher salt — 1 ½ hotel pans: ¾ t · ½ pan gf: ¼ t ingredients — topping flour/gf flour — 1 ½ hotel pans: 4 ½ c · ½ pan gf: 1 ½ cup granulated sugar — 1 ½ hotel pans: 1 ½ c · ½ pan gf: ½ cup brown sugar — 1 ½ hotel pans: 2 ¼ c · ½ pan gf: ¾ cup kosher salt — 1 ½ hotel pans: 1 ½ t · ½ pan gf: ½ teaspoon oats (adjusted up to 3/4) — 1 ½ hotel pans: 4 ½ c · ½ pan gf: 1 cup butter/earth balance, melted — 1 ½ hotel pans: 3 cups = 6 sticks · ½ pan gf: 1 c preparation preheat oven to 350 degrees. (peel and) core apples and cut them into large uniform chunks. (can keep apples overnight in lemon water.) place apples in a bowl and toss with lemon zest, lemon juice, granulated sugar, flour, salt and cinnamon. transfer to either 5 one-cup ramekins or an 8″ square baking dish. for the topping: combine flour, sugars, salt, oats, and cold (or, easier, melted) butter. mix until well combined and crumbly. spread evenly over fruit mixture and pat down slightly. place baking dish on a cookie sheet and bake for one hour (allow for up to an hour 15 mins), until top is browned and fruit is bubbly. (you can also refrigerate, covered, and bake later.) serve warm with vanilla ice cream.

title: Artichoke Hummus
text: all recipes / side artichoke hummus tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × from cook's website. yield: 3x batch (~6 cups) or original single recipe (~2 cups) ingredients drained canned or jarred artichoke hearts, rinsed and patted dry — 3x: 1 lg jar · orig: 1 c lemon juice (save zest) — 3x: 1 c · orig: ¼ c grated lemon zest — 3x: 1 tsp · orig: ¼ t water — 3x: ¾ c · orig: ¼ c tahini, stirred well (see note) — 3x: 1c + 2 tbl · orig: 6 tbls extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra for drizzling — 3x: 6t · orig: 2t chickpeas, drained and rinsed — 3x: 1 ½ 29oz can (or 3 14oz cans) · orig: 1 14oz can garlic clove (blender will mince) — 3x: 3 · orig: 1 salt — 3x: 2 ½ tsp · orig: ½ tsp white pepper — 3x: ¼ tsp · orig: 0 cayenne — 3x: 2 pinches? · orig: pinch fresh parsley or mint — 3x: 2 tbl · orig: 2 tsp preparation set aside 4 whole artichoke pieces for garnish. combine lemon juice and water in small bowl or measuring cup. whisk together tahini and 2 tablespoons oil in a second small bowl or measuring cup. combine chickpeas, remaining artichokes, garlic, salt, cayenne, and lemon zest in a bowl. you'll probably need to do this in 2 batches, so half of each prepared mixture as follows: process half the chickpea mixture in food processor until almost fully ground, about 15 seconds. scrape down bowl with rubber spatula. with machine running, add half the lemon juice-water mixture in a steady stream through the feed tube. scrape down bowl and continue to process for 1 minute. with machine running, add half the oil-tahini mixture in a steady stream through the feed tube; continue to process until hummus is smooth and creamy, about 15 seconds, scraping down bowl as needed. taste — probably needs more lemon & salt, maybe some white pepper. transfer hummus to serving bowl. sprinkle reserved artichokes and parsley or mint over surface, cover with plastic wrap, and let stand until flavors meld, at least 30 minutes. drizzle with olive oil and serve.

title: Artichoke Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad artichoke salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (1 batch) equipment vitamix 2 pitchers ingredients 33 oz jar marinated artichoke hearts (add all including oil) 1 tsp tamari 3 tbsp dijon mustard 2 ½ tsp agave ½ tsp white pepper 1 cup water ½ cup rice vinegar 1 lemon: juice and zest 1 ½ cup light olive oil pinch salt, if needed preparation add all ingredients except oil in the vitamix container and mix on low, slowly increasing speed until all artichokes are pureed. drizzle oil into the vitamix while mixing. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. taste and adjust seasonings if needed. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Avocado Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad avocado salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (1 batch) equipment vitamix electric juicer 2 pitchers ingredients 2 cups water 1 cup lime/lemon juice (use 4 limes, top off with lemons if needed — can use rice vinegar if short of lemons/limes, but it tastes much fresher with citrus juice) 5 large-ish avocados ⅓ cup cilantro ½ tsp garlic powder ¼ cup agave ½ tsp cumin powder ¾ tsp white pepper 1 ¼ tsp salt 2 cups light olive oil ~¼ cup water (this is a thick dressing, but add more water if it seems too thick) preparation juice limes and lemons with juicer. add all ingredients except oil in the vitamix container and mix on low. taste and adjust salt, agave, pepper, and lime to taste if you wish. drizzle oil into the vitamix while mixing. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Baba Ganoush (Eggplant Dip)
text: all recipes / side baba ganoush (eggplant dip) tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × ingredients 2 to 3 medium eggplants (about 3 pounds total) 2 to 3 tablespoons olive oil 1/3 cup tahini 2 cloves garlic, peeled and crushed juice of 2 lemons (about 1/2 cup) kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper preparation preheat the oven to 450°f. rub the outside of the eggplants with olive oil and place them in a roasting pan. roast the eggplant until the skin has charred and the interior is tender, 15 to 20 minutes. let cool. peel and seed the cooled eggplant, roughly chop the flesh, and then transfer it to the bowl of a food processor. into the processor bowl add the tahini, garlic, lemon juice, some salt and pepper to taste, and a few teaspoons of cold water. process the mixture to a coarse paste, adding a bit more water as needed to allow the mixture to blend. adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper to taste and serve.

title: Balsamic Dressing
text: all recipes / salad balsamic dressing tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × instructions for a double recipe (makes two batches at once). yield: doubled recipe — 2 batches, each filling ~2 small pitchers equipment vitamix second 4 quart container with lid small skillet (for poaching garlic, if making that version) 2 small pitchers ingredients (for one container — you will put this much in each one) 1 ½ cups balsamic vinegar 1 t sherry vinegar 1 t dijon mustard 1 tsp black pepper ½ tsp honey ½ tsp salt 6 poached garlic cloves with half their cooking oil (see preparation) (or ¾ tsp garlic powder) 4 ¼ cups olive oil (use 4 ½ cups if using powdered garlic), drizzled in slowly preparation gather all ingredients, the vitamix container, and a second 4-quart container with lid. you will double this recipe by putting a set of the ingredients in each container. it's easiest to add all ingredients except the oil to both containers, then move to the next ingredient. if time allows: put 12 cloves of fresh garlic in a small skillet, cover with about ½ cup of olive oil, and heat over medium heat, watching closely until they sizzle and just begin to turn a bit brown around the edges. remove the skillet from the stove and set aside. (if there's no time, you can use powdered garlic instead — fresh unpoached garlic is too strong for many people.) add the above ingredients except the oil to each container. blend the contents of the vitamix container, slowly drizzling in 4 ¼ cups of olive oil (4 ½ cups if using powdered garlic) through the lid. fill 2 small pitchers with it. pour the second set of ingredients into the vitamix container and mix it, again slowly drizzling in the other batch of olive oil. pour the mixed dressing back into the mixing container, cover, label, and put in the fridge.

title: Balsamic Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad balsamic salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (1 batch); you may be asked to make 2 batches equipment vitamix 2 pitchers extra 2qt square container with green lid, for a second batch ingredients (quantities for one batch) 1 ½ cup balsamic vinegar 2 cups water 2 tsp sherry vinegar 2 tbls + 2 tsp dijon mustard 2 tsp agave 1 tsp black pepper ½ tsp salt 4 big cloves garlic, minced in mini cuisinart (or 1 ½ tsp garlic powder — fresh is better, but check diets for sensitivity to raw garlic) 2 cups olive oil 1 ¼ cups light olive oil preparation if making 2 batches, measure all but the oils for both batches at the same time, putting the second batch's quantities into a 4qt square container. mix all ingredients except oil in the vitamix until smooth. drizzle oils into the vitamix while mixing. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. for a second batch: pour the measured container of ingredients into the vitamix pitcher and blend. add the second batch of oils as above. pour back into the container, label, date, and store in the fridge for later.

title: Banana Bread with Almond Filling Swirl
text: all recipes / dessert banana bread with almond filling swirl tags: vegetarian, soy-free scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × banana bread with an almond filling swirl. yield: 1 loaf (9×5-inch), keeps ~4 days wrapped (freezes well) ingredients almond filling 2 cups almond flour 3/4 cup granulated sugar 1 large egg 3 tbsp unsalted butter, melted 1/2 tsp almond extract banana bread 6 oz unsalted butter, melted and browned (just over 1/2 cup) 2 cups all-purpose flour 3/4 cup granulated sugar 1 tsp baking soda 1/2 tsp salt 3/4 tsp ground cinnamon 2 large eggs 1 tsp vanilla extract 1/4 cup yogurt 1 1/4 cup mashed banana (about 3 medium bananas) slivered almonds (for topping) powdered sugar (optional, for dusting) preparation make almond filling. mix egg, almond flour, sugar, almond extract, and melted butter. refrigerate. prep oven/pan. heat oven to 350°f. grease and flour a 9×5-inch loaf pan. brown butter. melt butter in a saucepan; cook until nutty-brown. transfer to a bowl to cool. mix dry. whisk flour, sugar, baking soda, salt, cinnamon (and nutmeg if you like). mix wet. whisk eggs, vanilla, and yogurt; whisk in mashed banana; whisk in cooled browned butter. combine. fold wet into dry just until combined (don't overmix). layer. add half batter to pan, spread half almond filling, add remaining batter, then remaining filling on top. sprinkle slivered almonds. bake. bake 50–60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. cool. rest 15 minutes in pan, then remove and cool completely. dust with powdered sugar if desired.

title: Banana Nut Cookies
text: all recipes / dessert banana nut cookies tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × an original recipe of the spirit rock kitchen, especially mary schjeldahl. yield: ~5 dozen cookies (this batch is scaled 2.5× from the original recipe, which made ~2 dozen) ingredients 5 ¾ cups unsalted almonds, toasted (2 1/3 cups for the original 2-dozen batch) 4 ¼ cups unsalted cashews, toasted (1 2/3 cups for the original 2-dozen batch) 1 ⅔ cups very ripe bananas, frozen and thawed (2/3 cup for the original 2-dozen batch) 2 ½ tbsp vanilla extract (1 tbsp for the original 2-dozen batch) 1 ¼ cups maple syrup (1/2 cup for the original 2-dozen batch) 2 ½ tsp baking powder (1 tsp for the original 2-dozen batch) <1 tsp salt (1/3 tsp for the original 2-dozen batch) 2 ½ cups bittersweet chocolate chips (1 cup for the original 2-dozen batch) preparation preheat oven to 350°f. using a food processor, finely grind almonds and cashews until slightly coarser than sand — don't over-grind or they'll become nut butter! remove from the food processor and transfer to a large mixing bowl. place the thawed bananas, maple syrup, vanilla, baking powder, and salt into the food processor. pulse until smooth. using a spatula, fold this purée into the ground nuts. once incorporated, fold in the chocolate chips. using a cookie scoop (about 2 tbsp), scoop dough into balls. keep mounded high for rounder, chewier cookies, or flatten slightly for crispier cookies. place dough balls onto a cookie sheet lined with parchment paper or a silpat mat. bake for 10-15 minutes (or ~20), until cookies are baked through and turning golden. kitchen notes: consider swapping racks and turning the trays halfway through baking, since the back and bottom of the oven cook faster. let cookies cool well before picking them up.

title: Barley Vegetable Soup with White Bean
text: all recipes / soup barley vegetable soup with white bean tags: vegan, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × adapted from a recipe on allrecipes.com — noted here as modified since allrecipes marks their recipes all-rights-reserved; this is what was actually made. yield: for 16 ingredients 3 tbsp olive oil 4 quarts vegetable broth 1 red onion, chopped 5 small cloves garlic, finely diced 1-3/4 cup uncooked barley 4 large carrots, chopped 6 stalks celery, chopped 2 zucchini, chopped 1 28-oz can diced tomatoes with juice 6 bay leaves 2 tsp salt 1 tsp ground black pepper 2 tsp dried parsley 2 tsp curry powder 2 tsp smoked paprika 2 tsp red wine vinegar 2 (15-ounce) cans white beans (cannellini), drained preparation heat the olive oil in a large pot (12-qt). add onion and garlic, and sauté for a few minutes. add carrots, celery, zucchini, vegetable broth, barley, tomatoes, and bay leaves. season with salt, pepper, parsley, curry powder, smoked paprika, and vinegar. bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 60-75 minutes. add the beans after about 45 minutes. (note: adding them at the start along with everything else made them break down too much — better to add them later.) remove bay leaves before serving.

title: Basil Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad basil salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (1 batch) equipment vitamix 2 pitchers extra 2-qt square container with green lid (for a second batch) ingredients 1 cup lemon juice (4-5 lemons) ½ cup rice vinegar 1 ½ cup water 1 tsp garlic powder ¼ cup dijon mustard ¼ cup agave ½ tsp salt ¾ cup packed fresh basil leaves, picked off the stems (~¾ of a bunch) ¼ cup packed fresh parsley, cut off the main stem trunk (rest is ok to use) (~¼ of a bunch) 3 ½ cups light olive oil preparation rinse the herbs — no need to chop, the vitamix will do it. add everything except the oils into the vitamix container and mix on low. if making 2 batches, measure a second batch (except oils) into the square container. drizzle the oils into the vitamix while mixing. gradually increase speed until fully emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. for a second batch: pour the measured container ingredients into the vitamix and blend. add the second batch of oils as above. pour back into the container, label, date, and store in the fridge for later.

title: Black Bean Soup - Once Upon a Chef
text: all recipes / soup black bean soup - once upon a chef tags: neither, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: 4 servings (about 30 minutes total) ingredients 2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil 2 medium yellow onions, roughly chopped 4 large garlic cloves, crushed and peeled 2 carrots, peeled and roughly chopped 2 (15-ounce) cans black beans, drained and rinsed 5 cups low sodium chicken broth 3/4 teaspoon oregano 1 teaspoon ground coriander 1-3/4 teaspoons ground cumin 1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper 1/2 teaspoon salt 1 tablespoon fresh lime juice 1/3 cup sour cream handful chopped fresh cilantro preparation heat the olive oil over medium heat in a large soup pan. add the onions, garlic cloves, and carrots and cook, stirring occasionally, until onions are soft and translucent, about 8 minutes. do not brown. add the black beans, chicken broth, oregano, coriander, cumin, cayenne pepper, and salt and bring to a boil. reduce the heat, cover, and simmer gently for about 15 minutes. purée the soup using a hand-held immersion blender until very smooth and creamy. stir in the lime juice and season with salt and pepper to taste. ladle the soup into bowls and top each bowl with a dollop of sour cream and freshly chopped cilantro. note: if using a standard blender instead of an immersion blender, purée the soup in batches, being careful not to fill the jar more than halfway. leave the lid's steam vent open and loosely cover with a dish towel to let the heat escape. pour the blended soup into a clean pot.

title: Black Eyed Peas with Walnuts and Pomegranate
text: all recipes / side black eyed peas with walnuts and pomegranate tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × from cook's mediterranean. makes about 4-5 quarts with leftovers — enough for a full house — and fills a large bowl heaped up (or a medium-large metal bowl). off-season, could try swapping in cranberries and celery in place of the pomegranate. yield: ~4-5 quarts / about 38 servings (this batch is scaled 7× from the single-batch recipe below) ingredients black-eyed pea salad 1 ¼ cups olive oil (3 tbsp for a single batch) 1 ¼ cups dukkah (3 tbsp for a single batch; see dukkah recipe below) ¾ cup + 2 tbsp lemon juice, plus zest of 2-3 lemons (2 tbsp lemon juice + zest of 2-3 lemons for a single batch) ¾ cup + 2 tbsp pomegranate molasses (2 tbsp for a single batch) salt & pepper, to taste 14 (15-oz) cans, or 7 (28-oz) cans, black-eyed peas, rinsed (2 15-oz cans for a single batch; 1 can = 1 ¾ cups). note: with dry beans, 3 lbs dry cooked down to about 5 qts, and adding 4 cans made 6 qts / 24 cups beans total. 3 ½ cups walnuts, toasted and chopped (½ cup for a single batch) 3 ½ cups pomegranate seeds — used 3 large pomegranates (½ cup for a single batch) 3 ½ cups minced parsley — used ~2 cups (½ cup for a single batch) 28 scallions, sliced thin (4 scallions for a single batch) dukkah (makes ~2 cups; homemade, or use store-bought, e.g. trader joe's) 1 15-oz can chickpeas 1 tsp olive oil ½ cup pistachios, toasted 1/3 cup black sesame seeds, toasted 2 ½ tbsp coriander seeds, toasted 1 tbsp cumin seeds, toasted 2 tsp fennel seeds, toasted 1 ½ tsp pepper 1 ¼ tsp salt preparation dukkah: preheat oven to 400°f. rinse, drain, and pat the chickpeas dry. toss chickpeas with oil and roast until brown and crisp, 40-45 minutes, stirring every 5-10 minutes. process the roasted chickpeas in a food processor until coarsely ground. pulse the pistachios and sesame seeds to a coarse grind. pulse the coriander, cumin, and fennel seeds to a fine grind. combine, add pepper and salt, and whisk together. black-eyed pea salad: whisk the olive oil, ¾ cup of the dukkah, lemon juice and zest, pomegranate molasses, 1 ½ tsp salt, and 1 tsp pepper until smooth. add the black-eyed peas, walnuts, pomegranate seeds, parsley, and scallions, and toss. season as needed with salt and pepper (a bit of aleppo pepper also works, though it was only so-so here). sprinkle with the rest of the dukkah as garnish.

title: Black Bean Soup Blended
text: all recipes / soup black bean soup blended tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × if using dry beans: soak overnight, and allow ~1 ½ - 2 hours to cook the beans before adding them to the soup. yield: ~50 servings (~19 qts) equipment 32-qt (largest) stock pot, with a pot-saver/heat-diffuser under it ingredients ~⅓ cup olive oil (to coat the bottom of the stock pot) 4 lbs (~7 ea) onions, ½" dice 7 lbs carrots, ½" dice 25 ea garlic cloves, chopped 10 qts cooked black beans (~7 lbs dry black beans, pre-cooked!!) 1 jar better than bouillon, dissolved in ~2 qts hot tea-urn water 9 qts total water (2 qts hot with bouillon as above, + remaining 7 qts cold) 2 ½ tbsp oregano 3 tbsp + 1 tsp ground coriander 5 tbsp + 2 tsp cumin 1 tsp cayenne pepper (taste and adjust) 1 tbsp salt, plus more to taste ½ cup + 1 tbsp (~7 ea) fresh lime juice, save some zest in case needed (maybe more for the avocados) 3 bunches cilantro, for topping 2 pints sour cream, for topping (or see cashew green chili cream recipe) 3 cups roasted pumpkin seeds, for topping avocados, diced and preserved with lime juice, for topping (about 1 per 4 people) preparation prep ingredients: locate all ingredients. dice onions and carrots by hand, chop garlic in the mini-cuisinart. juice limes. juicer is near the rice-cooker. maybe zest a couple and set the zest aside. mix bouillon in 2 qts hot tea-urn water. note: this is not a long-cooking soup — about 1 ½ hrs from start to sauté to finish blending. beans are pre-cooked separately. make soup: be sure the heat-saver disk (on the stove shelf) is placed under the stock pot. coat the bottom of the pot with olive oil to about ⅛" deep. sauté (= fry in a little oil uncovered, stirring occasionally) the onions, garlic, and carrots until the onions are getting soft and translucent (not brown). add the rest: black beans, bouillon, water, oregano, coriander, cumin, cayenne, and salt. bring to a boil. reduce heat, cover, and simmer ~30 minutes. check that carrots are soft. purée the soup until smooth and creamy (there will still be little flecks of beans) using the immersion blender. stir in lime juice and taste (perhaps more salt, pepper, lime zest, or cayenne). serve with any or all of: cilantro, sour cream and/or vegan green chili cream, diced avocado, and roasted pumpkin seeds.

title: Blue Cheese Dressing
text: all recipes / salad blue cheese dressing tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × note: put out some non-dairy leftovers or an alternative for anyone avoiding dairy, since this dressing itself isn't dairy-free. yield: ~48 servings (1 batch) equipment vitamix 2 pitchers ingredients 4 x 5oz tubs (or 3 x 8oz trader joe's) crumbled blue cheese (quality matters) 3 cups milk ½ cup lemon juice ½ tsp salt (depends on the brand of cheese — add slowly and taste) 1 tsp white pepper preparation add everything to the vitamix container and mix on low. gradually increase speed until fully emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover and store in the fridge (if not using today, label and date it too). good to make early, since it gets thicker as it sits.

title: Borcht
text: all recipes / soup borcht tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × from surya. yield: for ~48 ingredients 6 medium onions, chopped 9 cups potatoes, sliced thin 6 cups beets, sliced thin 6 large carrots, sliced thin 6 stalks celery, diced 8 qt stock 2 tbsp salt 2 tbsp pepper 2 tsp dill ½ cup cider vinegar 4 tsp caraway seeds ½ cup honey 6 cups tomato puree

title: Breakfast Cereal Guidelines
text: all recipes / side breakfast cereal guidelines tags: vegan, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × placeholder — breakfast cereal guidelines, still needs info filled in. rolled oats (regular oats) ratio: 2 parts water to 1 part oats default starting quantity for a full retreat (~48): 3 qts oats, 6 qts water guideline for other groups: about ⅓ cup oats per person on day 1, thereafter more like ¼ cup steel cut oats cooks for a good hour — start early, leave the fire on low and stir the whole time(?) rice farina

title: Breakfast Stewed Fruit
text: all recipes / side breakfast stewed fruit tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × ingredients 1 orange, washed (sliced thin, including the peel) 1 fresh apple, washed and cut up (plus any leftover apple/orange pieces from the public cutting board, if available) ~7 cups prunes (or one costco bag) 1 cinnamon stick, 3" (from the spice jars) water, to cover the fruit plus about 1 inch preparation setup the prunes to soak overnight: get the smallest short round 2-handled pot with lid. wash and thinly slice 1 orange, including the peel, into the pot (slice it in half lengthwise, then in quarters lengthwise, then very thinly, so you get thin quarter-moon slices). oranges are usually in the back room middle fridge. wash and cut up a fresh apple and add it to the mix. apples are usually in the bottom of the kitchen pantry. it's also a good use for any pieces of apple or orange left on the public cutting board (you could collect these in the evening and put them in the fridge for this purpose). add ~7 cups prunes (or one costco bag). add one 3" cinnamon stick from the spice jars. fill with water to cover all the fruit plus about 1 inch of water. put the lid on, put the pot in the left side of the kitchen fridge wherever you can find room. leave it to soak overnight. in the morning, the breakfast cook brings it to a boil and simmers for a few minutes while the oats cook. can add to it and reheat for up to 3 days in a row, then start over.

title: Broccoli Cashew Soup
text: all recipes / soup broccoli cashew soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~50 servings ingredients 5 cups cashews water (to cover cashews for soaking) 4 lbs onions, diced 3/4 cup minced garlic 8 quarts water 8 lbs broccoli 4 lbs potatoes 1 container better than bouillon vegetarian stock 2 cups nutritional yeast juice of lemons, to taste (optional) preparation cover raw cashews with water by 2 inches and let sit for 1-2 hrs for the cashews to absorb water and soften. blend cashews in the water until creamy. sauté onions in a large stock pot until soft. add garlic and sauté for 1-2 minutes, stirring frequently. add remaining ingredients. bring to a boil and lower to a simmer. once the broccoli is cooked, about 15-20 minutes, blend with an emulsifying (immersion) blender. add lemon to taste.

title: Broccoli-Ricotta Lasagna
text: all recipes / entree broccoli-ricotta lasagna tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × a simple broccoli-and-ricotta lasagna with béchamel and smoked scamorza. yield: ~6 portions (as written) ingredients fresh lasagna sheets — 250 g (or no-boil sheets) broccoli, cleaned — 500 g ricotta — 200 g (sheep's milk if possible) béchamel — 500 ml parmesan, grated — 100 g smoked scamorza, cubed — 100 g salt, to taste béchamel milk — 500 ml butter — 50 g white flour or cornstarch — 50 g salt — a pinch preparation make béchamel. in a pan, whisk milk + butter + salt + flour/cornstarch before heating to dissolve lumps. cook, stirring constantly, until thickened (~10 minutes). prep broccoli + ricotta. steam broccoli, then mash with a fork. reserve ~3 tbsp broccoli for topping. mix ricotta with mashed broccoli. prep cheese. cube smoked scamorza. assemble. spread a layer of béchamel in the pan. add a layer of pasta, then béchamel, parmesan, scamorza, and broccoli-ricotta. repeat until used up; finish with béchamel + reserved broccoli + parmesan. bake. bake at 240°c covered with foil until bubbling, then reduce to 200°c and bake 30–40 minutes total. remove foil for the last ~5 minutes to brown lightly. serve. cool briefly, slice, and serve. for reheating leftovers, add a splash of milk and warm in a pan.

title: Broccoli Salad
text: all recipes / salad broccoli salad tags: neither, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × from trish, mom on timeout. yield: 12 servings ingredients 1 cup light mayonnaise 1/3 cup sugar 2 tbsp red wine vinegar 1 tsp celery seed 2 heads of broccoli, broken down into small florets 3/4 lb bacon, cooked and chopped into small pieces 1/2 cup toasted slivered almonds 2 green onions, thinly sliced 1 cup chopped celery 1 1/2 cups red seedless grapes, halved preparation whisk together mayonnaise, sugar, red wine vinegar, and celery seed in a small bowl. place in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. combine broccoli, bacon, toasted almonds, green onions, celery, and grapes in a large serving dish. (to toast almonds, place on a large baking sheet and bake at 350°f for 3-5 minutes, stirring in between. do not walk away — they burn easily. the almonds are toasted when they turn light brown.) toss the dressing with the rest of the salad ingredients and stir. dressing can be added at the last minute if desired.

title: Broccoli Soup From Deborah Madison
text: all recipes / soup broccoli soup from deborah madison tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × vegetable soups from deborah madison's kitchen (via lael). yield: ~42 servings (this batch is scaled 7× from the original, a ~6-serving recipe) ingredients 14 lbs broccoli (scant 2 lbs in the original 6-serving recipe — about 3 or 4 broccoli "trees") 1 tbsp neutral oil (e.g. safflower), for sautéing 6 onions, thinly sliced or finely diced 7 large garlic cloves, chopped 2 jalapeño chiles, seeded and diced 7 tbsp ginger, peeled and chopped 1 ¾ cups minced cilantro stems and/or chopped cilantro leaves 7 small potatoes 10 qts water (added in two stages; note: not veggie broth) sea salt, to taste 1 cup white miso (if serving no-soy people, save some out and add it last) roasted sesame oil (~1 tbsp, to finish) preparation separate the broccoli crowns from the stalks and cut into florets of similar size (small or large). thickly peel the stalks so none of the fibrous outer layer remains, then slice thinly. heat the oil in a wide soup pot. when hot, add the onion, garlic, chile, ginger, and cilantro and sauté, stirring rapidly, for 1 minute. add the potato and broccoli stems, season with a scant teaspoon salt, add ~2 qts of the water, and simmer, covered, until the onion is soft, about 5 minutes. add the broccoli florets and the rest of the water and simmer just until the broccoli is tender, 5 to 10 minutes once it returns to a boil. let cool briefly, then purée until smooth, leaving only tiny nubbins of broccoli. save some out for no-soy diets, then mix the miso with some of the soup to dilute it, and pour it back into the pot. taste for salt. stir in ~1 tbsp toasted sesame oil.

title: Brownies Vegan GF
text: all recipes / dessert brownies vegan gf tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × based on the minimalistbaker.com version. yield: one 2" hotel pan serves ~52, cutting 8x6 and halving the large corner pieces (or use a second half-pan for more). this batch is scaled to 1 ½ pans; a single 1-pan batch is noted alongside each ingredient. ingredients 4.5 cups (3 ¾ tubs) vegan butter, e.g. earth balance (3 cups / 2 ½ tubs for a single 1-pan batch) 6 ¾ cups cane sugar (4.5 cups for a single batch) 18 vegan eggs — 1 cup + 1 tbsp powder in 2 ¼ cups water (12 vegan eggs — e.g. bob's ¾ cup powder in 1 ½ cups water — for a single batch) 3 tbsp vanilla (2 tbsp for a single batch) 3 tbsp baking powder (2 tbsp for a single batch) 2 ¼ tsp salt (1 ½ tsp for a single batch) 4.5 cups cocoa powder (3 cups for a single batch) 6 ¾ cups gluten free flour, e.g. bob's 1-to-1 (4.5 cups for a single batch) optional — 3 cups walnuts or pecans (2 cups for a single batch) preparation preheat oven to 350°f and spray hotel pan. prepare vegan eggs in a small bowl, whisk well, and let rest for 5 minutes. melt earth balance on the stove in a saucepan. mix melted earth balance, sugar, vanilla, vegan eggs, baking powder, salt, and cocoa powder in a large bowl. whisk to combine. lastly, add the flour in stages and combine. fold in nuts if using. fill pan or muffin tins (¾ full). bake for 22-26 minutes (or more like 35 — check often). shake the hotel pan; it's done when the center is stable and the sides are pulling away. remove and let rest and cool before serving. serve or store in an airtight container for a couple of days, or freeze. yummy with or without ice cream.

title: Caesar Salad Dressing (Vegan)
text: all recipes / salad caesar salad dressing (vegan) tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings per batch equipment vitamix juicer 2 pitchers ingredients 3 ½ cups raw cashews, soaked (could be overnight, at least 2 hrs) 1 ¾ cup water ¾ cup + 2t ev olive oil 7 t lemon juice 3 ½ t dijon mustard 3 ½ tsp garlic powder 6 small cloves of garlic 3 ½ t vegan worcestershire sauce (wizard's...might be some in top of fridge) 4 tbls + 2 tsp capers ~1 tsp each salt & pepper (adjust to taste) preparation soak cashews covered with water (ideally km would do this early). juice lemons with juicer. add all except salt & pepper in vitamix container and mix on low. add salt & pepper to taste. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Carmelized Onion Black Bean Dip
text: all recipes / side carmelized onion black bean dip tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × ingredients 2 (15 oz) cans black beans, drained and rinsed 4 medium red onions, chopped 2 tbs olive oil 1 tbs balsamic vinegar 1/2 tsp salt 1/2 tsp paprika 1 tbs chopped parsley (for garnish) preparation cook oil and onions for about 10 minutes until golden brown. add vinegar and salt and paprika and cook 2 minutes longer. process in blender for 20 to 40 seconds or until dip consistency. garnish with 1 tbs chopped parsley.

title: Carrot Cashew Soup
text: all recipes / soup carrot cashew soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment heaviest 32 qt stock pot immersion blender ingredients 14 lbs carrots (could pre-slice the day before in the robo coupe) 3 lbs onions, diced 1 lb ginger (optional: up to 5 lbs yams, raw or cooked, peeled & diced) 3 lbs cashews 2 t five spice powder preparation cover cashews with water and soak for 1-2 hours (i.e. do it at the start of veggie chop, leave it till 9:30). dice onions. locate ~14 lbs of carrots & maybe yams: excess already shredded, leftover roasted yams. chop the ginger in batches in the mini-chopper (grossly cut up first, no need to peel if organic). sauté the onions in the large rondo pan until getting soft (20-30 minutes? not till browning). add carrots (and yams) and continue to sauté, stirring often over low heat until some light browning, not too brown. while these sauté: purée the cashews in the vitamix (multiple batches if needed). add ginger and 5 spice powder & sauté another minute or two. add cashew milk and water to bring it up to ~14 qts. bring to a boil, reduce to simmer, stirring frequently. after all ingredients are soft, use immersion blender to blend smooth. taste for seasonings and salt, or add more 5 spice as needed, or salt, pepper, lemon juice. aim to have it about 170 degrees by lunch time. then turn off the gas and leave the pot covered on the stove. it should stay above 145 for the afternoon. reheat at 5:00 to bring it back to 165. optional: serve with yogurt if 2x32oz is still left for final breakfast.

title: Carrot Soup Tofu Spread
text: all recipes / soup carrot soup tofu spread tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~44 servings (aiming to make about 8 qts, not counting excess water) equipment 24 qt stock pot medium plastic bowl ingredients carrot soup 13 lbs carrots, chopped 4 lbs onions, diced 2 lbs ginger, chopped garlic (amount not specified in source) 10 lbs yams, cubed or pulp, or whatever is leftover water to make 19 qts (aiming for 18 qts when done) 3 lbs cashews 2 t five spice powder tofu spread 6 lbs tofu 2 c vegenaise 4 c celery, fine dice 2 t turmeric 6 t dijon mustard 6 t nutritional yeast 1 bunch parsley 1 bunch dill or tarragon 3 bunches scallions, chopped 8 packs corn cakes preparation carrot soup: purée the cashews in the robo coupe. chop the carrots in the robo coupe. sauté the onions in the stock pot until translucent. add carrots, ginger, (yams), cashews, 5-spice & water to the stock pot. bring to a boil, reduce to active simmer, stir frequently. whisk or use immersion blender to blend smooth after all ingredients are cooked very soft. taste for seasonings & salt. tofu salad: crumble the tofu to the texture of crumbled eggs. wash & chop the herbs. add the other ingredients and mix. taste for salt, pepper, seasoning. refrigerate until serving time. serve with corn cakes.

title: Cashew Dressing
text: all recipes / salad cashew dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × ingredients 4 cups raw cashews 2 1/4 cups vegetable oil 3/4 cup cider vinegar 3 cups water 2 cloves garlic 1 1/2 tbs salt 1 1/2 tbs dill, fresh or dried 2 1/2 tbs parsley leaves, chopped 1 1/2 tbs oregano 1 tsp rosemary, fresh chopped 1 tsp pepper preparation blend all ingredients in large blender. adjust water to reach correct consistency.

title: Cashew Green Chili Cream
text: all recipes / side cashew green chili cream tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × goes well with the "blended black bean soup" recipe. yield: ~48-50 servings equipment vitamix ingredients 4 ½ cups cashews, soaked in water as long as overnight, or as short as needed 2 cups water (fresh, for blending, not the soaking water) 5-6 small cans diced green chilis, drained (or start with a bit less water) ¼ cup lime juice 6 garlic cloves (blending will chop) 1 tsp salt ½ tsp ground cumin pinch (> ⅛ tsp) cayenne (if using mild chilis) preparation soak cashews as long as you can (longer is smoother, but grainy is fine). drain them. add all ingredients to vitamix blender (works better than robocoupe for this). blend until smooth. taste and fiddle with seasonings until you like it! note on the green chilis: the quantity is a guess — the original cook used about ¾ cup of a tastier, hotter, fancier bottled brand from new mexico.

title: Cashew Ranch Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad cashew ranch salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings per batch equipment vitamix 2 pitchers ingredients 4 cups raw cashews 2 ¼ cups light olive oil ¾ cup apple cider vinegar 3 cups water 2 cloves (or ½ tsp) garlic cloves (or powder) 1 ½ tsp salt 1 ½ tbsp dill, fresh or dried 2 ½ tbsp parsley leaves, chopped 1 ½ tbsp oregano 1 tsp rosemary (check garden outside kitchen door, finely chop) 1 tsp pepper preparation add all ingredients to vitamix container and mix on low, slowly increasing speed until all puréed. taste and adjust seasonings if needed. divide between 2 small pitchers (save any extra in a storage container). cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Cashew Whipped Cream (2)
text: all recipes / dessert cashew whipped cream (2) tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~1 ¼ cups ingredients 1 cup raw unsalted cashews, soaked for 2 hours 1/2 cup (120ml) filtered water, plus more to taste 2 tablespoons maple syrup, plus more to taste 1 teaspoon vanilla, plus more to taste pinch salt preparation drain the cashews, and discard the soaking water. pour the fresh 1/2 cup filtered water into the blender, and add the soaked cashews with the maple syrup, vanilla, and salt. blast on high for 30 to 60 seconds, until smooth and creamy. tweak water, sweetener, and vanilla to taste. transfer to a sealed container in the fridge, and chill for a few hours to thicken. the cream will keep in the fridge for about 5 days.

title: Cashew Whipped Cream
text: all recipes / dessert cashew whipped cream tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × ingredients 1 cup raw unsalted cashews, soaked for 2 hours 1/2 cup (120ml) filtered water, plus more to taste 2 tablespoons pure maple syrup, plus more to taste 1 teaspoon natural vanilla extract, plus more to taste pinch of celtic sea salt preparation drain the cashews, and discard the soaking water. pour the fresh 1/2 cup filtered water into the blender, and add the soaked cashews with the maple syrup, vanilla, and salt. blast on high for 30 to 60 seconds, until smooth and creamy. tweak water, sweetener, and vanilla to taste. transfer to a sealed container in the fridge, and chill for a few hours to thicken. the cream will keep in the fridge for about 5 days.

title: Cauliflower Bake
text: all recipes / side cauliflower bake tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × from hollyhock cookbook. equipment large skillet 2 hotel pans, 2" deep container for no-dairy portion (to be reheated on stove top) ingredients enough canola oil to sauté the onions (~1/2 cup?) 3 qts chopped onions 8 leeks, rinsed & chopped ¼ cup crushed garlic 6 coarsely chopped heads of cauliflower 2t dried dill (or ¼ cup fresh, if some is around) 4 cups rough chopped kalamata olives (or no more than one jar — be sure no pits!) 1 cup chopped parsley 4 tsp black pepper 2 tsp salt 8 cups grated cheese (cheddar or feta or swiss/gruyère mix) 12 cups cooked quinoa or rice paprika, to garnish preparation try to do this during the veg chop period: set up a steamer to steam the cauliflower for ~5 minutes (not all the way done). perhaps even do this in the veg period: in the large skillet, sauté the onion and leeks in the oil until transparent. mix all ingredients except cheese in a very large bowl. set aside the no-cheese portion in a smaller put-away container (this will be reheated with some stock on the stove top later). estimate ~1 cup each for no-dairy people. mix cheese into the remaining mixture in the big bowl. spray the hotel pans with oil. divide between the 2 hotel pans. sprinkle with a bit of paprika for garnish. cover & refrigerate. at night: bake at 350 for 30-40 minutes (put it in cold, into an un-preheated oven, before the evening talk — should be ok for an hour). mix some bouillon (from a jar) and add enough to moisten the no-cheese part, then heat in a sauce pan on the stove.

title: Cauliflower Recipe
text: all recipes / side cauliflower recipe tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × note: some kms prefer to skip this recipe and just steam or roast plain cauliflower — consult the km. if steaming, start about 11:30; if roasting, about 11:15. equipment ~3 large baking sheets (as needed for single-layer) ingredients 1 case + 3 extra heads (or ~1 case if not doing the supper-leftovers batch) cauliflower, chopped into bite-size trees 3 lbs frozen peas (note bag size — if 10oz bags, use 4 bags) 1 ½ cups olive oil 3t ground coriander 3t ground cumin 4 ½ t curry powder 3t turmeric 3t ground ginger 3t ground fresh ginger (add after cauliflower is roasted) 3t lime zest or amchur mango powder, if we have any (add after cauliflower is roasted) salt and pepper, to taste (add after cauliflower is roasted) preparation turn on oven to 400 degrees. mix oil, coriander, cumin, curry powder, turmeric and ground ginger. in the largest bowl, in two batches, add the cauliflower and coat in the spice mixture. lay cauliflower evenly on baking sheets. cook about 45 minutes, starting at 11:15. (~11:45) add the peas and cook another 10-15 minutes, or until cauliflower is tender. remove from oven, combine trays into a large serving bowl, and sprinkle with grated lime (or amchur) and fresh ginger. squeeze a little lime juice to taste with salt and pepper, if you wish.

title: Chai Apple Crumb Cake
text: all recipes / dessert chai apple crumb cake tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × a chai-spiced apple crumb cake with optional glaze. yield: 1 (9") cake, ~12 slices (prep ~40 minutes, cook ~50 minutes, total ~1.5 hours) ingredients chai spice mix 2 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon 1/2 tsp each: allspice, cardamom, cloves, ginger chai apples 3 small apples, peeled & thinly sliced 40 g light brown sugar (about 3 tbsp) 1 tbsp chai spice mix streusel 60 g unsalted butter (1/4 cup), melted 90 g light brown sugar (1/3 cup + 1 tbsp) 120 g all-purpose flour (1 cup) 1 1/2 tsp chai spice mix butter cake 210 g all-purpose flour (1 3/4 cups) 2 tsp baking powder 1/2 tsp salt 125 g unsalted butter (1/2 cup + 1 tbsp), room temp 175 g granulated sugar (3/4 cup + 2 tbsp) 2 eggs, room temp 2 tsp vanilla 135 g whole milk (1/2 cup + 2 tbsp), room temp 75 g sour cream (5 tbsp), room temp 180 g apple butter (2/3 cup), optional optional glaze 90 g powdered sugar 1–2 tbsp reserved chai-apple juices (or milk) preparation prep pan. heat oven to 350°f / 175°c. generously butter a 9" pan. press in parchment (crumple/uncrumple helps it fit). make chai apples. toss sliced apples with brown sugar + chai spice. set aside and save the juices for glaze. make streusel. mix melted butter + brown sugar + flour + chai spice with a fork until clumpy. make batter. whisk flour + baking powder + salt. beat butter + sugar 3–4 min until fluffy. beat in eggs + vanilla (~1 min). mix in half the dry ingredients, then sour cream + milk, then remaining dry — fold gently. assemble. spread half the batter in the pan. dollop/spread apple butter (optional). add remaining batter. top with apples (leave juices behind). sprinkle streusel on top. bake. bake 40–50 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean / with a few moist crumbs. cool. cool until manageable, then lift out using the parchment. optional glaze. whisk powdered sugar with reserved apple juices (or a splash of milk) to desired consistency; drizzle over cake.

title: Chai
text: all recipes / side chai tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × this page combines two chai recipes found together in the source: a bulk institutional recipe (surya's) and a small-batch "chai masala" recipe. yield: surya's bulk batch (below, with milk added at serving) serves ~18. no yield was given for the chai masala recipe. ingredients surya's chai 1 gal water 1/3 cup grated ginger a spice grinder's top full of whole green cardamom, plus 1 t whole coriander 1 tsp whole cloves, not ground 1 cinnamon stick a palm-full of loose black tea (assam, breakfast, or darjeeling) ½–1 cup sugar 2/3 gal whole milk, for serving (3:1 ratio with chai base) chai masala (indian spiced tea) 6 cups water 4 teaspoons tea leaves 1 teaspoon coarsely chopped ginger (no need to peel) 2 green cardamom pods, cracked 1/2 cup milk sugar, to taste preparation surya's chai: simmer for an hour. sit overnight to steep. bring back to a boil. add the loose black tea. add the sugar. cook 5-10 minutes. strain & cool = chai base. serve 3:1 with whole milk, reheating (for a full recipe: all of the above plus 2/3 gal milk, serves 18). sourcing tip: a cheap source of cardamom is united natural foods / frontier herb, about $15 (per source note) — you need to find a non-profit that bulk-orders from them to piggyback onto. chai masala (indian spiced tea): pour six cups water, tea, ginger, and cardamom into a saucepan, bring to a boil and cook 3 minutes. add milk and sugar to taste, and boil 2 minutes more. strain and serve.

title: Chickpea Stew and Sweet Potato
text: all recipes / entree chickpea stew and sweet potato tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × ingredients 5 lbs onions, chopped 40 cloves garlic, chopped 10 (15 oz) cans chickpeas 1 (6 lb) can diced tomatoes ¾ cup sundried tomato, minced ¾ cup lemon ¼ cup oregano (fresh if available) 20 lbs sweet potato

title: Cilantro Lime Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad cilantro lime salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × note: taste this and adjust the recipe as needed — it still needs testing. yield: ~48 servings per batch (may need to be doubled — see preparation for how to make a second batch) equipment vitamix 2 pitchers extra 2 qt square container with green lid, for a second batch ingredients 1 ½ cup lime juice ¾ cup lemon juice 4 cloves garlic 1 ½ tbls sugar 2 tsp salt 1 tsp ground cumin 1 tsp ground coriander 1 ½ cup cilantro 1 ½ cups olive oil 2 ¼ cups light olive oil preparation add all ingredients except the oils in the vitamix container and mix on low. if making 2 batches, measure a second batch (except oils) into the square container. drizzle oils into the vitamix while mixing. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. for a second batch: pour the measured container ingredients into the vitamix and blend. add the second batch of oils as above. pour back into the container, label, date, and store in the fridge for later.

title: Cowboy Cookies Vegan GF
text: all recipes / dessert cowboy cookies vegan gf tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × from moosewood restaurant favorites. yield: approximately 60 large cookies (4x6=24 on each of 2 large sheets, plus 3x4=12 on a half-size sheet) ingredients 5 cups gf flour 2 ½ tsp baking soda 1 ½ tsp baking powder 1 ½ tsp salt 2 ½ c earth balance 1 ¼ c sugar 1 ¼ c brown sugar 5 "vegan eggs" (look for packets in pantry) 2 ½ tsp vanilla 4 c oats (should be gf, warn if not) 2 c coconut (ideally large flake, else whatever) 3 c chocolate chips 2 c raisins or mix of raisins & cranberries 3 c chopped nuts (any or mix of walnuts, pecans, slivered almonds) preparation preheat both ovens to 350. mix vegan egg with water per directions on package, let sit until ready to use. in a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. in a separate large bowl, use an electric mixer to beat sugars with earth balance until very well mixed. beat in vegan eggs and vanilla. if the red table mixer is available, use it for the next step. else use a large spoon & spatula — it's pretty stiff. add the flour mixture to the sugar mixture. add oats. put on latex gloves and mix in all the goodies (nuts, fruit, chips) by hand. line 2 large sheet pans and 1 half sheet pan with parchment. make large scoops (~¼ cup or a little more) with your gloved hands, flatten onto the sheet pans. bake ~20 mins, time varies, start checking at 15. should be medium brown on bottom, very light brown on top. cool on racks. store in red-snap lid boxes (kept above kitchen desk).

title: Creamy Avocado
text: all recipes / salad creamy avocado tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~1½ qts ingredients ½ cup water 1¼ cup lime/lemon juice (~4 limes, rest lemons) 4 lg avocados ⅓ c. cilantro ½ tsp garlic powder ½ tsp cumin ½ tsp white pepper ½ tsp salt 3¾ cups canola oil preparation add all except the oil to the blender. blend. drizzle in the oil while mixing (or just pour it all in and mix — works fine too). for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers.

title: Brown Rice
text: all recipes / side brown rice tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: two batch sizes — a larger batch "with supper leftovers" (headcount not stated in the source) and ~36 servings if not doing a supper leftover batch; both quantities are given below. equipment large strainer rice cooker ingredients 14 cups (12 cups for ~36) short grain brown rice (preferred) 16 cups (14 cups for ~36) water (ratio = 1 rice : 1 water + 2 cups) or: 14 cups (12 cups for ~36) brown basmati rice 21 cups (18 cups for ~36) water (ratio = 1 rice : 1.5 water) preparation (~10:30–11) rinse the rice well using the large double-mesh strainer (may take several batches). put the damp rice in the cooker. (about 11:00) add water to the rice in the cooker per above. plug in and turn on the cooker. it will take about 50–60 minutes to cook, then it switches to warm. before serving, check that it has switched to warm. if so, carefully open the lid and fluff it with a wood or plastic tool. serve with wooden spoons so as not to scratch the container.

title: Blended Simple Black Bean Soup
text: all recipes / soup blended simple black bean soup tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~50 servings (~19 qts), or ~36 for a smaller batch — with some leftover reserved as a base for a supper soup with lots of added veggies, broth, tomatoes, etc. equipment 32 qt (largest) stock pot, with pot-saver placed under it ingredients ~⅓ cup olive oil (to coat bottom of stock pot) 4 lbs, ~7 ea (3 lbs for ~36) onions, ½" medium/large dice — rough chop 7 lbs (5½ lbs for ~36) carrots, ½" medium/large dice — rough chop 25 ea (20 ea for ~36) garlic cloves, chopped 10 qts cooked = ~4.5 qts dry (8 qts cooked / ~3.6 qts dry for ~36) black beans [or ~13 29 oz cans!! or 6.6 lbs dry for shopping — best to measure in quarts] 1 jar better than bouillon (¾ jar for ~36), dissolved in ~2 qts hot tea-urn water ~9 qts total (7.5 qts total for ~36) water — use the 2 qts hot water with the bouillon above, plus bean cooking or canned bean water, plus remaining cold water to reach the total 2½ t (2 t for ~36) oregano 3 t + 1 t (3 t for ~36) ground coriander 5 t + 2 t (4.5 t for ~36) cumin 1 tsp, taste (¾ t for ~36) cayenne pepper 1 t + to taste (1 t + to taste for ~36) salt ½ cup + 1 t = ~7 ea (½ cup for ~36) fresh lime juice — save some zest in case needed, maybe more for avocados 3 bu (2 bu for ~36) topping: cilantro 3 pints (2½ pints for ~36) topping: sour cream, maybe mixed with green chilies, and/or see vegan cashew green chili cream recipe 3 cups (3 cups for ~36) topping: roasted pumpkin seeds preparation prepare ingredients: if using dry beans, soak overnight; allow ~1–2 hours to cook before adding them to the soup. cook the beans if not using canned — empty the soak water, cover by 2" with fresh water, and save (measure?) the cooking water to use as part of the soup liquid. dice onions and carrots by hand; chop garlic in the mini-cuisinart. juice limes (juicer is near the rice cooker). maybe zest a couple and set the zest aside. mix the bouillon in 2 qts hot tea-urn water. note: this is not a long-cooking soup — about 1½ hours from start to sauté to finish blending. beans are cooked separately. make soup: be sure the heat-saver disk (on the stove shelf) is placed under the stock pot. coat the bottom of the pot with olive oil to about ⅛" deep. sauté (fry in a little oil, uncovered, stirring occasionally) the onions, garlic, and carrots until the onions are getting soft and translucent (not brown). drain the beans, saving the liquid to use as part of the water measure. add the rest: black beans, bouillon, water, oregano, coriander, cumin, cayenne, and salt. bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer ~30 minutes. check that the carrots are soft. purée the soup until smooth and creamy (there will still be little flecks of beans) using the immersion blender. stir in the lime juice and taste (perhaps more salt, pepper, lime zest, or cayenne). serve with any or all of: cilantro, sour cream and/or vegan green chili cream, diced avocado, and roasted pumpkin seeds.

title: Kale with Mushrooms
text: all recipes / side kale with mushrooms tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (lunch only) equipment roasting sheet 2 steamer pan setups ingredients ~⅓ cup olive oil, enough to lightly coat the sliced mushrooms 1 case + 6 heads dino kale, de-stemmed and torn (each leaf-side) into 3–4 pieces 4 lbs sliced mushrooms preparation first thing in the morning (before you need the oven for the tofu): pre-heat oven to 350°f. toss sliced mushrooms in olive oil, spread on a baking sheet, and roast for ~15–30 minutes at 350°f (time depends on how thick they were sliced). check every 10 minutes, stir, and swap pans on oven shelves as needed. set aside when done (= appealing to eat, in your opinion!). or: some prefer to sauté them in the largest skillet (check the overhead rack or apron area for large skillets).
