(~11:00) steam the kale using 2 steamer setups — it will probably take two rounds of 2 steamers each, about 10 minutes per round. or: some prefer to sauté the kale in the rondo (the big round pan under the rice cooker). transfer the cooked kale, layering with the roasted mushrooms, into a 4" deep hotel pan to serve. cover to keep warm.

title: Vegan GF Cornbread
text: all recipes / side vegan gf cornbread tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × adapted from nisha vora, rainbowplantlife.com. this can take a couple of hours of off-and-on attention from someone, so plan for that (approximate times are noted below). measurements in grams need a precision grams scale (there's one above the spice shelf that looks like an ipad). yield: fills two 2" deep hotel pans, each cut into 6x8 pieces ingredients ½ gallon oatly full fat oat milk (from whole fds) 4 tbls apple cider vinegar 1170g stone-ground medium corn meal (not the polenta, that is too coarse) 564g gluten free all-purpose flour 8 tbls = ½ cup baking powder 3 tsp salt 336g vegan butter, melted 336g extra virgin olive oil 240g brown sugar 504g agave 24g = 6t finely chopped (use spice grinder) rosemary (from the kitchen garden) preparation preheat oven to 400°f (with the vulcan, try 450°f and watch it). (~10:15?) stir vinegar and oat milk together and set aside at least 10–20 minutes to curdle. in a large bowl, combine flour, cornmeal, baking powder, and salt. whisk well. (~10:30?) pour in the melted vegan butter, oil, brown sugar, agave, and curdled oat milk. careful not to overmix — some lumps are ok. should look like pancake mix. fold in the rosemary. allow batter to rest 10 minutes to 1 hour. (~11:10) heat the empty pans in the oven while the batter is resting, for about 10 minutes. remove from oven, add more lumps of vegan butter to melt and coat the pan, and sprinkle the pan bottom with cornmeal. pour in batter, dividing between the 2 pans. (~11:20) bake 25–35 minutes (in the vulcan, rotate front/back and top/bottom halfway through — might take longer than 25). test with a toothpick or knife. cool for 15 minutes before slicing 6x8 per pan.

title: Steamed or Roasted Green Beans
text: all recipes / side steamed or roasted green beans tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment 2 large baking trays, foil (for roasting) steamer pan setup — either 1 reused for 2 batches, or 2 setups (for steaming) preparation roasted (and steamed a bit first on the trays): toss beans in olive oil, sprinkle with salt and maybe pepper. heat oven to 350°f. these need to be done early to have time for the tempeh to use the oven. they can be served room temp. we found it best to "steam" them for 20–30 minutes first by covering the trays of beans with foil; when almost soft enough to eat, remove the foil and roast for another ~10 minutes until slightly browning. or simple steamed: you may need to wash the steamer pans used for the tempeh to reuse for the beans. these can be done anytime and served either warm or room temp. steam the beans for ~20 minutes until they are as soft as you like them. be sure to check that the water doesn't all boil off.

title: Quinoa
text: all recipes / side quinoa tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~50 servings with a supper leftover batch, or ~36 if no supper leftovers equipment rice cooker ingredients 9 cups (8 cups for ~36) quinoa (red, white, or mix — whatever we have, all cooks the same) 11¼ cups (10 cups for ~36) water (1 quinoa : 1.25 water) preparation rinse the quinoa very thoroughly (or it has a bitter taste) using the large double-mesh strainer (may take several batches). you can do this early and let it sit in the turned-off rice cooker. (about 11:00) add water. plug in and turn on the cooker. it will take about 45 minutes to cook, then it switches to warm. let it sit for a few minutes, then carefully open the lid and fluff it with a wood or plastic tool. unplug the machine to turn off the "warming." serve with wooden spoons so as not to scratch the container.

title: Broccoli Salad
text: all recipes / salad broccoli salad tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × alternative: plain steamed broccoli can be served instead. quantities of mix-ins are estimates — feel free to vary to taste or to what you have on hand. yield: ~50 servings, probably with some leftovers for a final snack, or ~36 servings equipment 2 steamer setups largest bowl to mix (maybe a smaller one to serve) ingredients case = 14 heads (~10 heads for 36) broccoli (very lightly steamed), cut into quite small florets, ~¾" ~1½ c (~1 c for 36) sunflower seeds ~1½ c (~1 c for 36) sliced almonds ~1½ c (~1 c for 36) raisins ~1 c (~¾ c for 36) optional if have: red onion or scallion, finely minced — could pan-fry the raw red or yellow onion to mellow it out first ~1½ c (~1 c for 36) shredded carrots, or optional if we have some: sundried tomatoes, chopped dressing: 4 c = 1 32 oz jar (3 c for 36) veganaise ½ c (⅓ c for 36) agave ½ c (⅓ c for 36) lemon juice ½ c (⅓ c for 36) apple cider vinegar 1½ tsp (2 tsp for 36) salt preparation make the dressing. toss all together.

title: Easy Refried Beans Recipe - Cookie and Kate
text: all recipes / side easy refried beans recipe - cookie and kate tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × these refried beans are delicious and so easy to make. this refried bean recipe is quick, too — use canned beans and they're ready in 25 minutes! plus, these beans are healthy, vegan, and gluten free. recipe from cookie and kate. author: cookie and kate. prep time: 10 minutes. cook time: 15 minutes. total time: 25 minutes. category: side dish. method: stovetop. cuisine: mexican. yield: 4 servings (the recipe's own headnote states it yields ~2½ cups / 21 ounces, enough for 5 servings) ingredients 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil 1/2 cup finely chopped yellow or white onion (about 1/2 small onion) 1/4 teaspoon fine sea salt 2 cloves garlic, pressed or minced 1/2 teaspoon chili powder 1/4 teaspoon ground cumin 2 cans (15 ounces each) pinto beans, rinsed and drained, or 3 cups cooked pinto beans 1/2 cup water 2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro 1 tablespoon lime juice (about 1/2 medium lime), to taste preparation in a medium saucepan over medium heat, warm the olive oil until shimmering. add the onions and salt. cook, stirring occasionally, until the onions have softened and are turning translucent, about 5 to 8 minutes. add the garlic, chili powder, and cumin. cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30 seconds. pour in the drained beans and water. stir, cover, and cook for 5 minutes. reduce the heat to low and remove the lid. use a potato masher or the back of a fork to mash up at least half of the beans, until you reach your desired consistency. continue to cook the beans, uncovered, stirring often, for 3 more minutes. remove the saucepan from the heat and stir in the cilantro and lime juice. taste, and add more salt and lime juice if necessary. if the beans seem dry, add a very small splash of water and stir to combine. cover until you're ready to serve. (variation: substitute black beans for the pinto beans.)

title: Fennel Leek Potato Soup
text: all recipes / soup fennel leek potato soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: for supper, ~36 servings (recipe created on the fly, 10/27/16) preparation sauté 4 chopped onions. add 7 chopped garlic cloves and sauté. add 4 each chopped carrot and celery stalks. chop 9 leeks, 6 bulb fennel, and ~10 lbs yukon gold potatoes. sauté all of that awhile, then add better than bouillon "no-chicken" broth paste and water per the jar instructions (enough to look soup-like). add ~1 t oregano. immersion-blend some of the soup and leave some whole. salt and pepper to taste. served with a caesar salad (parmesan, croutons, romaine — see the vegan caesar dressing recipe).

title: Frittata Lunch Recipe Two Quantities First go
text: all recipes / entree frittata lunch recipe two quantities first go tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: 2 full hotel pans, cut into 24 portions each (48 portions total); the equipment list also mentions a half hotel pan, but it isn't referenced in the steps below. equipment rondo two full 2" hotel pans one half 2" hotel pan ingredients 10 lbs mushrooms, sliced 1 cup olive oil, split in two 7 lbs greens, roughly chopped 6 cups onions, chopped 30 cloves garlic 4 cups parmesan cheese 8 dozen eggs 4 cups half and half 24 scallions, chopped 4 cups smoked gruyere cheese for beans: 6 to 8 –29 oz cans cannellini beans, drained and rinsed ? cups mushrooms and veggies preparation cook veggies: preheat oven to 425°f. heat the rondo on medium heat and add oil to the pan. once hot, add mushrooms, allowing them to brown on each side. once mushrooms are browned, add onion and cook until tender. then add garlic and cook for a minute or two until fragrant, and add greens until wilted. remove approximately ⅓ of the veggie mixture for bean salad. constructing frittata: while veggies are cooking, mix eggs, half and half, parmesan cheese, and scallions. add veggie mixture to egg mixture and place in 2 full hotel pans; sprinkle with gruyere cheese. place in oven at 11 am and cook for 45–60 minutes or until frittata is firm in center. remove from oven and cut into 24 portions per pan. for bean salad: add 6–29? ounce cans cannellini beans to veggies. taste to ensure flavor.

title: Frittata Lunch Recipe Two Quantities
text: all recipes / entree frittata lunch recipe two quantities tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: quantities below are for the batch "with supper leftovers"; a smaller "no supper leftovers" batch size was in the template but its quantities were never filled in. equipment rondo two full 2" hotel pans ingredients 7–10 lbs veggies of choice (red pepper, zucchini, kale, spinach, mushroom, etc.) 6 cups onions, sliced 30 cloves garlic olive oil 4 cups parmesan cheese 10 dozen eggs 5 cups milk or half and half, if you have on hand 24 scallions, chopped 4–6 cups cheese, shredded or crumbled 2–29 oz cans white beans preparation cook veggies: preheat oven to 350°f. heat the rondo on medium heat and add oil to the pan. once hot, add onions. once onions begin to get tender, add garlic and cook for a minute or two until fragrant. add chopped veggies of km's choice. constructing frittata: while veggies are cooking, mix eggs, milk, parmesan cheese, and scallions. once veggies are cooked, reserve 2 cups of veggie mixture for alternative-diet folks if relevant this meal. then add veggies to two hotel pans evenly. top veggies with cheese and pour egg mixture over, distributing between two pans evenly. place in oven at 11:00 am and cook until frittata is firm in center, 45–60 minutes. remove from oven and cut into 24 portions per pan. for bean salad: add 2–29 oz cans white beans to reserved veggies. taste to ensure flavor; salt and pepper as needed.

title: Galette (Sweet or Savory)
text: all recipes / dessert galette (sweet or savory) tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × a basic galette dough (sweet or savory) plus filling ideas. yield: 1 large galette (about 14-inch round) ingredients 1 1/2 cups flour 1 1/2 tsp sugar (sweet only; omit for savory) 1/4 tsp salt 8 tbsp cold unsalted butter, cubed (1/2" pieces) 1/3 cup ice water 2 tbsp melted butter (for brushing) turbinado/raw sugar (sweet only; omit for savory) preparation make dough. in a food processor, pulse flour + sugar (if using) + salt. add butter; pulse 8–10 times to coarse crumbs. add water. run processor and add ice water 1 tbsp at a time until dough comes together. chill. form into a 4-inch disk, wrap tightly, and chill at least 30 minutes (or overnight). preheat. heat oven to 375°f. line a sheet pan with parchment. roll + fill. roll dough into a ~14-inch round. add filling, leaving a 1–2 inch border. fold + finish. fold edges up, pleating as you go. brush edges with melted butter; sprinkle sugar for sweet galettes. bake. bake 35–45 minutes until golden. cool ~15 minutes. filling ideas — savory roasted red onion rosemary chorizo balsamic reduction filling ideas — sweet apple clementine zest cardamom cinnamon ginger lemon juice cocktail (ideas) gin (small amount) rosemary simple syrup lemons seltzer

title: Gazpacho Toledano
text: all recipes / soup gazpacho toledano tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: a single batch serves 6 to 8; the "x8" batch (scaled ×8, quantities in parentheses below) served a group of ~39 with about 7 qts left over. ingredients 7-8 medium-sized ripe tomatoes (56 for the x8 batch) 2 medium-sized cucumbers (16 for the x8 batch) 1 green pepper (8 for the x8 batch) 1 small onion (8 for the x8 batch) 2-3 cloves garlic (20 for the x8 batch) 1½ slices french bread (omit, or use gluten-free, for the x8 batch) 1½ cups cold water (12 cups for the x8 batch) 6 tbs. olive oil (3 cups for the x8 batch) 4-5 tbs. wine vinegar, or to taste (32? tbs. for the x8 batch) 3 tsp. salt, or to taste (24 tsp. for the x8 batch) 2 tsp. paprika (16? tsp. for the x8 batch) pinch ground cumin (8 pinches for the x8 batch) fresh ground pepper to taste garnish (big bowl of mixed extras, ~1/4 c each = 10-12 cups total): croutons (we have bread for the side) garnish: chopped onions garnish: chopped red and green bell peppers garnish: chopped cucumber garnish: chopped tomatoes garnish: maybe parmesan? preparation cut the tomatoes into quarters. peel and seed the cucumbers and cut into approximately 1-inch pieces. seed the bell pepper and cut into approximately 1-inch pieces. peel and coarsely chop the onion. put the garlic through a press. cube the bread. now put the prepared ingredients, 2 to 3 cups at a time, into a blender, adding a little of the water each time. blend at medium or high speed until the vegetables and bread are puréed. pour the purée into a large bowl. add the oil and vinegar, the remaining water, and the seasonings, and whisk vigorously until all is blended. if the soup is too thick, it may be thinned with a little more cold water. chill the soup in the refrigerator for several hours before serving. arrange the garnishes attractively on a large platter and pass them around the table as you serve the soup. (we just did cucumber, tomato, and parmesan for garnish last time.) optional: set out canned white beans and walnuts as a salad topping, for protein.

title: Ginger Miso Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad ginger miso salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: 1 batch (~48 servings) equipment vitamix 2 pitchers ingredients ½ cup apple cider vinegar ½ cup tamari ½ cup agave ¾ cup yellow miso (or any kind will do) ¼ cup chopped ginger (rough chop, let the vitamix take it from there) ½ cup water 1 tsp toasted sesame oil 4 cups light olive oil preparation rough chop the ginger. add all except the oil to the vitamix container and mix on low. drizzle the oil into the vitamix, mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. taste and adjust seasoning if needed. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover and store in the fridge (if not for today, label and date it too).

title: Glazed Tempeh
text: all recipes / entree glazed tempeh tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × sweet and sticky with just a little kick, these sliced tempeh strips are briefly marinated, baked, then re-glazed to trap in maximum flavor and tender texture. yield: serves 6 (or 36 at scale — see quantities below; the tempeh, collards, and corn scale ×6, but sauce/marinade ingredients scale ×12, i.e. double the sauce) ingredients 2 8-oz. pkg. (×6: 12 8-oz. pkg.) tempeh, sliced into ½-inch strips ⅓ cup (×12: 4 cups) maple syrup ¼ cup (×12: 3 cups) orange juice ¼ cup safflower oil, divided (2 tbs. for the marinade, ×12: 1½ cups; 2 tbs. for sautéing, ×6: ¾ cup) 2 tbs. (×12: 1½ cups) ketchup 2 tbs. (×12: 1½ cups) dijon mustard 1 tbs. (×12: ¾ cup) sriracha sauce 1 tbs. (×12: ¾ cup) low-sodium tamari 1 tsp. (×12: ¼ cup) freshly ground black pepper ¼ tsp. (×12: 1 tbs.) ground cinnamon 2 cloves (×12: 12 cloves) garlic, minced (2 tsp., ×12: ½ cup) 2 12-oz. (×6: 12 12-oz.) bunches collard greens, stems and ribs removed, leaves thinly sliced 2 cups (×6: 12 cups) frozen fire roasted corn, thawed preparation place tempeh strips in a medium heat-proof bowl. set aside. whisk together maple syrup, orange juice, 2 tbs. (×12: 1½ cups) oil, ketchup, mustard, sriracha, tamari, pepper, and cinnamon in a medium saucepan. bring to a simmer over medium heat and cook 5 to 7 minutes, or until slightly thickened. pour the hot mixture over the tempeh strips, cover, and let marinate 30 minutes, or overnight. preheat oven to 350°f. line a baking sheet with foil, and coat with cooking spray. arrange the marinated tempeh strips on the prepared baking sheet; reserve the marinade. cover the baking sheet tightly with foil, and bake 15 minutes. remove the foil, and flip the tempeh pieces. bake, uncovered, 5 minutes more, or until the tempeh is slightly browned. remove from oven, and brush the tempeh with the remaining glaze. meanwhile, heat the remaining 2 tbs. (×6: ¾ cup) oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. add garlic, and cook 30 seconds. add the collard greens in two batches, wilting the first batch before adding the second. stir in the corn, and season with salt and pepper, if desired. cook 5 to 7 minutes, or until the greens are tender, stirring occasionally. serve topped with the tempeh slices.

title: Golden Beet Borscht
text: all recipes / soup golden beet borscht tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × from spirit rock. we were blown away the first time we made this soup – it is delicate but full of flavor, satisfying and savory but full of the sweetness of perfectly cooked vegetables, and wonderfully adaptable for colder or warmer seasons. it quickly became one of our year-round go-to dishes for retreat suppers! traditionalists can serve the soup with a dollop of herbed sour cream, but the original recipe from the world-famous bay area vegan restaurant millennium offers a delicious non-dairy alternative. adapted from a recipe by eric tucker & john westerdahl, from "the millennium cookbook". yield: 8 servings ingredients soup: 2 quart vegetable stock 2 large yellow onions, thinly sliced 6 medium carrots, thinly sliced ¾ cup dry sherry, white wine, or nonalcoholic wine 4 medium yellow beets, peeled and thinly sliced 1 bay leaf ½ tsp toasted and ground caraway seeds 2 tsp fresh thyme, minced 3½ tbs white miso, or more to taste 1 tbs sherry vinegar (optional) ¼ cup minced fresh dill salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste tofu dill sour cream: 3¼ oz silken tofu 1 tbs white miso, to taste (optional) ¾ cup fresh lemon juice 4 tbs minced fresh dill ½ tsp ground nutmeg, to taste ¾ cup water, plus more as needed preparation if you are making your own stock from scratch, begin by making your stock. a light, soft broth is nice in the summer, whereas a hearty, dark roasted broth can be nice in the winter. if you have a nice pre-made stock that you enjoy, feel free to use it as a short cut. coat the bottom of a large soup pot with a thin layer of sunflower oil. place over medium heat. when the oil is hot, add the onions, carrots, and sherry, and cook until the onions are soft, about 15 minutes (keep the vegetables nice and light, so no need to do any heavy browning before adding the cooking liquid). add the beets, bay, caraway, thyme and vegetable stock. cover and reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer for 40 minutes or until the beets are very tender. meanwhile, make the tofu topping: in a blender or food processor, blend all tofu dill sour cream ingredients until smooth. thin out with as much of the water as needed. set the topping aside in a bowl, and garnish with dill or other herbs immediately prior to service. to finish the soup, pull one cup of broth into a small prep bowl, and whisk in the miso paste to make a slurry. pour the miso broth into the soup and stir to combine. add the vinegar and the fresh dill. season with salt and pepper and serve hot. alternately, if you would like a blended soup rather than a brothy soup, blend prior to adding the dill.

title: Greek Lemon Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad greek lemon salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (1 batch) equipment vitamix microplane zester (or box grater) electric juicer 2 pitchers ingredients ~½ tbsp zest of 1 lemon (zest is just the outermost colored layer of the peel) ½ cup lemon juice (about 6 lemons) 2 limes, juiced (optional if no limes) 1 cup rice vinegar ⅓ cup agave 2 tbls dijon mustard 6 cloves garlic (or 1½ tsp garlic powder) 1 t oregano 2 cups olive oil 2 cups light olive oil ¾ cup water ½ tsp salt preparation zest lemons with zester. be careful, very sharp! juice lemons with press juicer. add all except oil in vitamix container and mix on low. drizzle oil into vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. taste & adjust seasoning if needed. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Herb Vinaigrette--update
text: all recipes / salad herb vinaigrette--update tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × note: this recipe is also used for "tarragon" on menus (see herb substitution below). yield: ~1½ qts (or ~3 qts for 2 meals) ingredients 1½ cups rice vinegar (3 cups for 2 meals) ¼ cup honey (½ cup for 2 meals) ¼ cup dijon mustard (½ cup for 2 meals) 6 cloves garlic (12 cloves for 2 meals) ~¾ cup fresh herbs (~1½ cups for 2 meals) — for "herbal" use 1 bunch basil + ½ bunch parsley; for "tarragon" use 1 clamshell of tarragon 4 cups canola oil (8 cups for 2 meals) ½ cup water (1 cup for 2 meals) salt to taste preparation rinse the herbs & pick the leaves off the stems. poach the whole peeled garlic cloves in one cup of the oil (one cup out of the amount called for) in a small saucepan or skillet on medium heat for ~5 minutes to make them more mild. add all except the rest of the oil to the blender (poached garlic cloves and their oil can be added unchopped). blend. if room in the vitamix, drizzle in the oil as you keep blending. if no room, transfer to a larger container and whisk in the oil or use the immersion blender. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper or other seasonings. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with smallest ladles.

title: Herbal Dressing
text: all recipes / salad herbal dressing tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment vitamix container a second 2- or 4-quart container with lid 2 small pitchers ingredients for one container (you will put this much in each one) 1 cup water ¾ tsp garlic powder (on spice shelf far left) — or if time: poach in oil or boil in water 6 cloves of garlic (don't use just raw garlic, too strong) 3¾ cup canola oil 2 cup rice vinegar ¼ cup honey ¼ cup dijon mustard ½ cup fresh basil ½ cup fresh parsley preparation you will double this recipe by putting a set of the above ingredients in each container — it's easiest to add each ingredient to both containers, then go to the next ingredient. pick fresh basil leaves until you have a loosely packed cup. pick fresh parsley leaves until you have a loosely packed cup. rinse both herbs and divide each in half. add the above ingredients list to each container. blend the contents of the vitamix container using the vitamix. fill 2 small pitchers with it. pour second set of ingredients into the vitamix container and mix it. pour the mixed dressing back in the mixing container, cover, label and put in the fridge.

title: Herbal Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad herbal salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings per batch (recipe can be doubled — see note in preparation) equipment vitamix 2 pitchers extra 2 qt square container with green lid, for second batch ingredients 1¾ cup rice vinegar 1½ cup water 1 tsp garlic powder ¼ cup + 2 tbsp dijon mustard ⅓ cup agave ½ tsp salt 1 tsp pepper ½ bunch fresh basil leaves, picked off stems (= ~½ cup packed down) ½ bunch fresh parsley, main stem trunk removed, rest ok to use (=~½ cup packed down) 3½ cups light olive oil preparation note: you may be asked to make 2 batches — read all steps below first; the quantities above are for one batch. rinse herbs, no need to chop, vitamix will do it. if making 2 batches, measure a second batch (except oils) into the square container. add all except oils to the vitamix container and mix on low, increasing to high. drizzle oils into vitamix, mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. for second batch: pour measured container ingredients into vitamix and blend. add second batch of oils as above. pour back into container, label, date and store in fridge for later.

title: Hollyhock Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad hollyhock salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (1 batch) equipment vitamix 2 pitchers ingredients ¾ cup apple cider vinegar ¾ cup water ¾ cup tamari 9 cloves garlic (or 2 tsp garlic powder) 1 cup nutritional yeast (yellow stuff in pantry near oatmeal) 3 cups + 3½ cups light olive oil (added in 2 batches) preparation add all vinegar, water, tamari, garlic and the first 3 cups of canola oil to the vitamix container and mix on low. add nutritional yeast and blend in thoroughly. drizzle remaining oil into vitamix, mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Hollyhock
text: all recipes / salad hollyhock tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~1.5 qts ingredients ¾ cup water ¾ cup tamari ¾ cup apple cider vinegar 9 cloves garlic 3 cups canola or other non-olive oil 1 cup nutritional yeast 3.5-4 cups canola oil (added later) preparation blend the water, tamari, apple cider vinegar, garlic, and 3 cups oil well in the vitamix. add the nutritional yeast and blend well again. add the remaining 3.5-4 cups canola oil and blend well again. fill 2 small pitchers if for today, or else store in a 2 quart (smallest square) container with label & date.

title: Honey Mustard
text: all recipes / salad honey mustard tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~1½ qts (or ~3 qts for 2 meals) ingredients 1¼ cup apple cider vinegar (2½ cups for 2 meals) ½ cup + 2 t dijon mustard (1¼ cups for 2 meals) ½ cup + 2 t honey (1¼ cups for 2 meals) — hint: coat the cup with oil first, the honey slides right out 3½ cups canola oil (7 cups for 2 meals) preparation add all except oil to the blender. blend. if room in the vitamix, drizzle in the oil as you keep blending. if no room, transfer to a larger container and whisk in the oil. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper or other seasonings. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with smallest ladles.

title: Kale Salad from Carol Collins
text: all recipes / salad kale salad from carol collins tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: 4 servings (as a main dish) ingredients ½ cup lightly roasted walnuts 8 oz. kale (lacinato/smooth kale preferred) 1 cup red cabbage ½ cup dried cranberries 1 medium granny smith apple 2 oz. soft goat cheese, chilled dressing: 3 t olive or canola oil 1½ t apple cider vinegar 2 teas rice vinegar 1 t smooth dijon mustard 1½ teas honey preparation pull kale leaves off the tough stems and discard stems. chop the kale and the cabbage into small, bite-sized pieces. chop the apple into small, bite-sized pieces and add to a small bowl of cold water with about 1 t of lemon juice. transfer kale and cabbage to a large bowl. sprinkle a small amount of sea salt or kosher salt and massage the leaves with your hands by lightly scrunching big handfuls at a time, until the leaves are darker in color and fragrant. add the cranberries and walnuts. drain the apple and add to the mix. crumble the goat cheese over the top. in a small bowl, whisk the dressing ingredients together vigorously and pour over the salad. toss until the salad is evenly coated with dressing. allow the salad to marinate for an hour or so before serving.

title: Lael Simple Dal
text: all recipes / entree lael simple dal tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × for when we're tired of the usual onion & tomato base. ingredients 6 qt red lentils 12 qt water ¼ c + 2t turmeric ¼ c salt 4 oz chopped ginger + 4 oz pureed ginger (added later) ½ c cumin seeds ⅓ cup ground coriander ¼ cup garam masala ¾ tsp cayenne ~¼ cup oil ½-1 c. lemon juice optional: spinach or other greens preparation bring lentils, water, turmeric, chopped ginger and salt to a boil and then simmer until done. when nearly done: fry cumin seeds in oil for 1 min, add coriander, garam masala & cayenne. add fried spices to dal. add greens to dal if using. just before serving, stir in the 4 oz pureed ginger and the lemon juice to taste. taste for salt, lemon.

title: Lasagna notes
text: all recipes / entree lasagna notes tags: vegetarian, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: 2 regular hotel-pan lasagnas + ¼ special-needs (sn) pan ingredients total for 2 regular pans + ¼ sn pan: 3 boxes lasagna noodles 1 box gluten-free noodles 8 (10 oz) frozen spinach bags 5x32oz ricotta 4 tubs trader joe's goat cheese (= 2 cups) 8 eggs 4 cups bread crumbs 2 lbs tofu 28 c (or 8.5 qts) sauce with mushrooms & onions (probably less needed) 8 c mozzarella 1 no-dairy cheese (optional, tbd) 2 lemons half case mushrooms 4 lbs onions basil dry basil (optional) nutmeg alt version, ¼ pan for 6 (no gluten, no tofu allergy): 1 lb spinach (adult portion) rice lasagna noodles (gluten-free) 1 lb tofu, for tofu ricotta (blend with lemon juice, 2 garlic cloves, ¼ c non-dairy milk, 2 t fresh basil in vitamix) 4 c sauce alt cheese for top (optional, tbd) preparation scaling notes (for reference): need 12 cups cheese/spinach mix (24 cups = 8 qts when doubled); 11 cups sauce ×2.5 = 28 cups; 23 sheets of tj's noodles (~21 per box) means ordering 2 boxes → 3 boxes total; 4 cups mozzarella doubles to 8 cups; 2 cups parmesan doubles to 4 cups; 2 cups bread crumbs ×2 = 4 cups. cheese mix (need 12 cups total; ratio is 1 cup ricotta : ½ cup spinach): about 9 lbs raw spinach or 9 (10 oz) frozen bags (4 cups prepped/cooked ×2.25); about 8 lbs ricotta (7 cups = 4 lbs, doubled to 7.5 → about 5x32oz tubs, or 8 15oz tubs); about 4 cups goat cheese (1 cup = 2 trader joe's tubs or 1 small log, doubled); 8 eggs (4 eggs = ~1 cup, doubled); 1 cup bread crumbs (buy); 1 t nutmeg; salt & pepper. sauce: bottled sauce plus sautéed 4 lbs mushrooms and 4 lbs onions. layer (per hotel pan): 2c sauce; 7½ sheets tj's lasagna noodles; 6c cheese/spinach mix; 3c sauce; 3c mozzarella; 7½ sheets noodles; 6c cheese/spinach mix; a layer of julienned basil (optional); 3c sauce; 7½ sheets noodles; 3c sauce; top with 2c parmesan + 1c bread crumbs + 1c mozzarella. sauté the mushrooms and onion, maybe with some extra dry basil and oregano. mix mushrooms and onion into the sauce. steam the spinach and press dry (set aside some spinach for the special-needs version(s)). beat the eggs and mix the cheeses with the spinach and nutmeg (for the alt version, make tofu ricotta and add spinach). layer the pans as above. (~11:00) bake for 1 hour, then let sit 15 minutes.

title: Lemon-garlic dressing
text: all recipes / salad lemon-garlic dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: 12 servings ingredients 2 garlic cloves 1.5 t. salt 6 t. fresh lemon juice 3 t. white wine vinegar (or orange muscat vinegar, if white wine vinegar isn't on hand) ¾ t. lemon zest ground black pepper to taste 1-1/8 c. extra-virgin olive oil (evoo)

title: Lemon Tahini Dressing-IF
text: all recipes / salad lemon tahini dressing-if tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment vitamix container (use two, one per batch, if doubling) ingredients for one vitamix container (do this twice if making extra) 1 cup lemon juice (juice from about 4 fresh lemons) ¾ cup parsley 5 cloves garlic 2½ cups water 1½ tablespoon tamari (if no soy, use salt instead) 2 teaspoons ground cumin ½ teaspoon white pepper 2½ cup tahini preparation if needed, double the recipe using two vitamix containers. using electric juicer, juice the lemons. wash parsley and cut off stems (some of the upper stems are ok). add all ingredients in the order above to the vitamix container. repeat if making two batches in a second vitamix container. fill two small pitchers with each vitamix container of salad dressing made.

title: Lemon Tahini Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad lemon tahini salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × note: this recipe needs reworking — we currently prefer the orange tahini dressing instead. yield: ~48 servings (1 batch) equipment vitamix electric juicer mixing bowl whisk 2 small pitchers ingredients 2½ cups water 1 cup lemon juice (4-6 lemons) ¾ cup parsley 5 cloves fresh garlic (or 1¼ tsp garlic powder) 1½ tblsp tamari 2 tsp cumin ½ tsp white pepper 2 cups tahini (= 1 whole tin of joyva, or measure out bulk) ½ cup light olive oil preparation using juicer, juice the lemons. wash parsley and cut off stems (some of the upper stems are ok). in a medium sized bowl, use a hand whisk to mix lemon juice, tahini and 1 cup of the water so that the tahini is not too clumpy (or else it will stall the vitamix). then blend in the vitamix with the rest of the ingredients. divide between two small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Lemon Cookies (2)
text: all recipes / dessert lemon cookies (2) tags: vegan, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: 18 cookies ingredients ½ c refined coconut oil, melted ¾ c sugar 3 t mylk 2 t lemon zest (about 2 lemons) 1 tsp vanilla 1.5 c flour 1 tsp cornstarch ½ tsp baking powder ½ tsp salt lemon glaze: 2 c powdered sugar 3 t lemon juice ½ tsp vanilla 1 t refined coconut oil preparation preheat oven to 350°. using a fork or electric mixer, beat sugar and oil together. add mylk, zest and vanilla; beat until it resembles applesauce. add half the flour and the remaining cornstarch, baking powder and salt. add remaining flour. spoon about 2 t per cookie, flatten with hands. bake 10-12 min until bottoms are golden brown. lemon glaze: sift powdered sugar and add remaining glaze ingredients, whisk well, then drizzle on completely cooled cookies and place in fridge to harden the glaze.

title: Malaysian Tofu
text: all recipes / entree malaysian tofu tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × malaysian influenced tofu, from deborah madison. yield: ~48 servings (quantities below are the larger figure for possible leftovers; the figure in parentheses is for the "no supper leftovers" version) equipment 2 large baking sheets rondo (or large stock pot) ingredients 15 lbs (12 lbs) tofu, cubed ¾" cubes spray oil, as needed 1 #10 can + 1 small can (1 #10 can) coconut milk (whole, not lite; add water as needed — tbd est. water amt.) ½ cup + 2 t (½ cup) brown sugar ¾ cup (⅔ cup) coriander seeds, lightly toasted & ground 10 t (8 t) curry powder 2½ t (2 t) turmeric ½ tsp + pinch (½ tsp) cayenne pepper (start with this, check for not too hot) ¼ c + 1 t (¼ cup) tamarind paste 1 16 oz jar (1 16 oz jar) cashew butter (bought, or see recipe below — or: 4 cups cashews + 2 tsp coconut oil) 17 cloves (14 cloves) garlic, chopped in mini-cuisinart ¾ cup (⅔ cup) ginger, chopped in mini-cuisinart 6 lbs (5 lbs) mushrooms, cut chunky (~ in fourths) 1 lg can + 1 med can (1 lg can) diced tomatoes 4 bunches (3 bunches) scallions, sliced thin including greens (for garnish) preparation bake tofu: preheat oven to 350. cube tofu into ¾" cubes, layout on baking sheets on parchment and spray with oil. (this may not be cubed until ~10:15.) bake for ~30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally until lightly browned. while they cook, proceed with next steps. if needed, make cashew butter (if not using bought): 4 cups cashews, roast lightly (@350 for ~10 mins, watching carefully!), puree until very fine in a robo-coupe, add ~2 tsp oil and puree more until no longer grainy, almost dough- or butter-like (doesn't have to be really all the way to commercial butter). (~10:30) start sauce: check allergies — maybe make a no-cashew side version? could try with some tahini. mix all sauce ingredients except mushrooms, tomatoes and scallions in the rondo (or large stock pot if no rondo) on a flame disperser. heat on the stove, whisking to blend. reduce to simmer for 10 minutes. once the sauce is smooth and heated, add the mushrooms. (~11:00) add tofu and garnish: add the tofu and tomatoes to the sauce and stir. watch for low simmer and non-sticking. garnish with chopped scallions just before serving.

title: Rice Pilaf
text: all recipes / side rice pilaf tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings if there's no supper that day (we make soup from the leftover tagine instead), or ~36 servings otherwise. equipment large strainer largest skillet or rondo rice cooker large bowl to mix & serve (maybe) ingredients 14 cups (10 cups for 36) short grain brown rice (ideally; could use basmati if that's all we have) 17½ cups (12½ cups for 36) water — ratio of rice:water used here is 1:1¼ (make some into bouillon using better than bouillon, see instructions) 2 cups (1½ cups for 36) raisins 2 cups (1½ cups for 36) chopped dried apricots 2 cups (1½ cups for 36) coarsely chopped almonds (or a mix of almonds & pistachios) 4 (3 for 36) onions, chopped 2 oranges (1½ for 36), zested preparation prep: chop the apricots and almonds and/or pistachios, and measure out the raisins. chop the onions. zest the oranges. rinse the rice using the large double-mesh strainer. make bouillon with ~2 qts hot tea water and ~⅓ cup better than bouillon; add the rest of the water cold. make rice: using the bouillon and the rest of the water, make the rice in the rice cooker. sauté: while the rice is cooking, sauté the onions; when translucent, add the fruit and sauté a bit. finish: when the rice is done, stir in the sautéed onions, apricots, and raisins. let it sit for ~10 minutes, covered. stir in the orange zest. maybe set aside a no-nuts portion. stir in the nuts just before serving.

title: Two Quantities Baked Potato Bar
text: all recipes / side two quantities baked potato bar tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment 2-3 large baking sheets ingredients 25 lbs white potatoes (with-supper-leftovers batch; quantity not specified in the original for the no-supper-leftovers batch) 15 lbs sweet potatoes (with-supper-leftovers batch only; not used in the no-supper-leftovers batch) olive oil (amount not specified, for rubbing the potatoes) preparation prep potatoes: preheat ovens to 400 degrees. rub potatoes with olive oil and sprinkle with salt and pepper, and place on baking sheets. bake: bake 1-2 hrs? — if it needs more time, turn and continue baking.

title: Mexican Hot Chocolate Snickerdoodles
text: all recipes / dessert mexican hot chocolate snickerdoodles tags: vegan, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × a beautiful crackle topped chocolate cookie with a spicy cayenne kick and a sugary cinnamon coating. sold? yield: makes 2 dozen cookies. ingredients for the topping: 1/3 cup sugar 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon for the cookies: 1/2 cup canola oil 1 cup sugar 1/4 cup pure maple syrup 3 tablespoons almond milk (or your preferred non-dairy milk) 1 teaspoon vanilla extract 1 teaspoon chocolate extract (or more vanilla extract if you have no chocolate extract) 1 2/3 cups flour 1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder 1 teaspoon baking soda 1/4 teaspoon salt 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon 1/2 teaspoon cayenne preparation preheat oven to 350°f. line 2 large baking sheets with parchment paper. mix the topping ingredients together on a flat plate. set aside. in a medium mixing bowl, use a fork to vigorously mix together the oil, sugar, syrup, and milk. mix in the extracts. sift in the remaining ingredients, stirring as you add them. once all ingredients are added, mix until you've got a pliable dough. roll dough into walnut-sized balls. pat into the sugar topping to flatten into roughly 2-inch discs. transfer to the baking sheet, sugar side up, at least 2 inches apart (they do spread) — this should be easy since the bottom of the cookies should just stick to your fingers so you can flip them over onto the baking sheet. bake for 10 to 12 minutes; they should be a bit spread and crackly on top. remove from oven and let cool for 5 minutes, then transfer to a cooling rack to cool completely.

title: Minty Pea Dip (2)
text: all recipes / side minty pea dip (2) tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × adapted from a martha stewart recipe, via lael. vegan, nut free. yield: ~36 servings for the mid-size batch (the ingredient list also gives quantities for a larger "full" batch and for the original single batch). ingredients 12 cups frozen peas (9 cups for the ~36-serving batch; 3 cups in the original single batch) 1 cup mint leaves (¾ cup for ~36; ¼ cup original) 4 lemons, zest and juice of (3 for ~36; 1 original) 4 cloves garlic (3 for ~36; 1 original) 8 tbls olive oil (6 tbls for ~36; 2 tbls original) 4 tbls tahini (3 tbls for ~36; 1 tbls original) salt & pepper, to taste preparation blanch peas in salted boiling water for <~1 minute, then cool & drain. pulse the peas in the robo coupe with all other ingredients. season to taste with salt & pepper. serve, maybe garnished with a drizzle of olive oil and a mint sprig.

title: Minty Pea Dip
text: all recipes / side minty pea dip tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × adapted from a martha stewart recipe, via lael. vegan, nut free. yield: ~36 servings for the mid-size batch (the ingredient list also gives quantities for a larger "full" batch and for the original single batch). ingredients 12 cups frozen peas (9 cups for the ~36-serving batch; 3 cups in the original single batch) 1 cup mint leaves (¾ cup for ~36; ¼ cup original) 4 lemons, zest and juice of (3 for ~36; 1 original) 4 cloves garlic (3 for ~36; 1 original) 8 tbls olive oil (6 tbls for ~36; 2 tbls original) 4 tbls tahini (3 tbls for ~36; 1 tbls original) salt & pepper, to taste preparation blanch peas in salted boiling water for <~1 minute, then cool & drain. pulse the peas in the robo coupe with all other ingredients. season to taste with salt & pepper. serve, maybe garnished with a drizzle of olive oil and a mint sprig.

title: Moroccan Lentil Soup
text: all recipes / soup moroccan lentil soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~12 quarts ingredients 6 tbsp. extra virgin olive oil 5 large onions, chopped 6 celery stalks, chopped 6 carrots, chopped 16 garlic cloves, chopped 8 tsp. ground coriander 4 tsp. ground cumin 4 tsp. ground turmeric 2 tsp. sweet paprika 1 tsp. ground cinnamon 2 tsp. sea salt 1 tsp. pepper 8 qts vegetable broth (i used 1 jar of better than bouillon dissolved in 1 qt tea water + 7 qts water) 1 large can crushed tomatoes (or diced tomatoes) 8 cups red lentils, picked over, washed, and rinsed until the water runs clean ½ cup (~6 lemons), juiced ~¼ tsp cayenne 1 cup fresh flat-leaf parsley, chopped fresh cilantro, chopped (on the side) preparation heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. add the onions, carrots, and celery and sauté until tender (about 15 minutes). add the garlic, coriander, cumin, turmeric, paprika, cinnamon, salt, and pepper and continue cooking for another 2-3 minutes, stirring the whole time. add the broth, tomatoes, and lentils, stir well, and heat to a boil. simmer uncovered on low heat for about 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring occasionally. blend with an immersion blender (doesn't have to be blended all the way — more than half, maybe). stir in the lemon juice, red pepper flakes, parsley, and cilantro, cover, and cook for 10 minutes. garnish with cilantro if you desire.

title: Mu Shu Wraps
text: all recipes / entree mu shu wraps tags: vegetarian, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: about 1½ wraps per person; quantities below are given for batches of 2, 14, 21, or 30 people (3, 21, 30, or 45 tortillas respectively). ingredients large onion, slivered — 1/5 (2 people), 1 (14 people), 1½ (21 people), 3 (30 people) garlic, minced — 1 large clove (2 people), 4 (14 people), 6 (21 people), 9 (30 people) ginger, minced — 1 tsp (2 people), 2 tbsp + 1 tsp (14 people), 3 tbsp (21 people), 4½ tbsp (30 people) ginger, slivered — 1 tbsp (2 people), ~½ cup (14 people), ¾ cup (21 people), 1¼ cup (30 people) carrots, julienned (or robo-shredded) — ¼ large carrot (2 people), 2 (14 people), 3 (21 people), 5 (30 people) 5-spice tofu, julienned (recipe below) — 1/8 of a 14oz box (2 people), 1½ boxes (14 people), 2 boxes (21 people), 3 lbs (30 people) tree ear mushrooms, dried, pre-shredded — a few (2 people), 1 oz (14 people), 1.5 oz (21 people), 2.25 oz (30 people) shiitake mushrooms — 2 (2 people), 14 (14 people), 21 (21 people), ~30 (30 people) lily buds, dried — ~10 (2 people), 70 (14 people), 100 = 2-3oz (21 people), 150 (30 people) cabbage — 1/5 of 1 lb (2 people), 1½ lb (14 people), 2 lb (21 people), 3 lbs (30 people) sauce: tamari — 1 tbsp (2 people), 7 tbsp (14 people), 10 tbsp (21 people), 1 cup (30 people) rice vinegar — 1 tbsp (2 people), 7 tbsp (14 people), 10 tbsp (21 people), 1 cup (30 people) brown sugar — 1 tbsp (2 people), 7 tbsp (14 people), 10 tbsp (21 people), 1 cup (30 people) hoisin — 1 tbsp (2 people), 7 tbsp (14 people), 10 tbsp (21 people), 1 cup (30 people) fixings (for serving): hoisin sauce — 3 tbsp (2 people), 1¾ cup (14 people), 2¼ cup (21 people), 3½ cup (30 people) reserved shiitake soaking liquid — 3 tbsp (2 people), 1¾ cup (14 people), 2¼ cup (21 people), 3⅓ cup (30 people) scallions, slivered — 2 (2 people), 14 (14 people), 21 (21 people), 30 (30 people) fajita-type wheat tortillas (or rice, for gluten-free diners) — 3 (2 people), 21 (14 people), 30 (21 people), 45? (30 people) homemade hoisin sauce (makes about 1 cup — see fixings quantities above for how much you'll need): 4 tbsp dark brown sugar 4 tbsp chinese black bean and garlic paste (or use 2/3 can black beans, drained, plus 1 tsp chopped garlic) 2 tbsp tamari 1 tbsp honey 4 tsp rice vinegar (or lemon juice, if avoiding vinegar) ½ tsp chinese five-spice powder 2 tbsp peanut butter ¼ tsp salt preparation note: figure out a strategy for special dietary needs (e.g. some diners get scrambled eggs instead of tofu, alternate sauces, etc.). night before: marinate the tofu (see 5-spice tofu steps below). first thing: bake the marinated tofu slices at 350°f until dry and firm-looking (keep an eye on it, turning halfway through). soak all the dried ingredients (tree ears, shiitakes, lily buds) in boiling water for about 30 minutes. cut the lily buds in half after soaking. stir-fry: stir-fry the onion, minced ginger, and garlic. add the tree ears, shiitakes, and lily buds (take off the heat once the steamed parts are nearly ready). add the sauce to the stir-fry. steam: steam the cabbage, ginger slivers, and carrots in a steam tray (allow about 30 minutes). mix together the steamed vegetables, the stir-fry, and the tofu. maybe heat the tortillas (the thin ones don't need it). serve with sliced scallions, a ½ hoisin / ½ reserved mushroom-soaking-liquid mix, and the tortillas, with instructions to spread some hoisin and scallions on a tortilla, add some mu shu filling, then wrap. good served with butternut squash or yams, a kale salad with orange and roasted cashews, and miso dressing, for example. 5-spice tofu (try to make the day before): press the tofu, then cut the loaf into thin-ish slices horizontally. marinate in 1 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp water, ¼ tsp 5-spice powder, and 2 drops sesame oil (large baggies work well for marinating). refrigerate overnight. next day: bake the tofu slices on a baking sheet at 350°f for about an hour, turning halfway; check often for burning and add a little water as needed — you want it to dry out and get firmer. cut the slices into matchsticks for the mu shu. homemade hoisin sauce: blend all the hoisin sauce ingredients together (listed above). you could cook it a little on the stove afterward, or it's fine just blended.

title: Mushroom gravy
text: all recipes / side mushroom gravy tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: sized to use up a "leftover amount" (no specific serving count given in the original). equipment rondo ingredients ½ cup earth balance vegan butter 3 lbs onions 5 lbs mushrooms 3 qts water 1 cup cornstarch ½ jar veggie stock 2 tbsp rosemary (from the garden) 2 tbsp sage (from the garden) ¾ cup nutritional yeast salt and pepper, to taste preparation sauté: melt the butter on medium heat in the rondo and add the onions. sauté for 5-10 minutes until they begin to soften. add the mushrooms and sauté until liquid begins to release. mixing: mix the water, veggie stock, and cornstarch, and add to the mushroom and onion mixture. add ingredients and finish: add the remaining ingredients — rosemary, sage, nutritional yeast — and bring to a boil; reduce to a simmer until thick and delicious. add salt and pepper to taste.

title: north african stew
text: all recipes / entree north african stew tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × this warming, highly spiced stew is rich in beans, grains and chunks of sweet winter squash. feel free to substitute other grains for the barley. farro works particularly well. if you'd prefer something soupier, thin it with a little broth or water before serving. yield: 8 to 10 servings (about 1 hour 45 minutes total time). recipe by melissa clark. ingredients ⅓ cup extra-virgin olive oil, more for serving 2 leeks, white and green parts, diced 1 bunch cilantro, leaves and stems separated 1 cup finely diced fennel, fronds reserved (about ½ large fennel bulb) 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped baharat spice blend (2½ tbsp total, for the stew): 2 tablespoons sweet paprika 1 tablespoon ground coriander 1 tablespoon ground cumin 1 tablespoon ground turmeric 2 teaspoons black pepper 1 teaspoon grated nutmeg 1 teaspoon ground cardamom 1 teaspoon allspice ½ cinnamon stick 2 tablespoons tomato paste 2 quarts chicken or vegetable broth ½ cup pearled barley 2½ teaspoons kosher salt, more as needed large pinch saffron, crumbled (optional) 4 cups cooked beans or chickpeas 2 cups peeled and diced butternut squash (about 1 small squash) ¾ cup peeled and diced turnip (about 1 medium) ½ cup red lentils plain yogurt, for serving aleppo pepper or hot paprika, for serving preparation in a large pot over medium heat, heat oil and cook leeks until they begin to brown, 10 to 12 minutes. finely chop cilantro stems. stir into pot, along with diced fennel and garlic. cook for 2 minutes. stir in baharat, cinnamon, and tomato paste, and cook until paste begins to caramelize, about 2 minutes. stir in broth, 3 cups water, the barley, and the salt. bring to a gentle boil, stir in saffron if using, and reduce heat to medium. simmer uncovered for 40 minutes. stir in beans, squash, turnip, and lentils; cook until barley is tender, about another 20 to 30 minutes. taste and adjust seasonings if desired. remove cinnamon stick. ladle stew into bowls. spoon a dollop of yogurt on top and drizzle with olive oil. garnish with cilantro leaves, fennel fronds, and aleppo pepper or paprika.

title: Cheese Polenta
text: all recipes / side cheese polenta tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment two 4" full-sized hotel pans one half-sized 4" hotel pan (it won't be full, but it's easier if it doesn't slosh, so use a 4" pan) ingredients large pans (x2), each pan gets: 5 cups polenta (coarse corn meal) 20 cups water 1 t salt half pan (no-cheese version): 2½ cups polenta 10 cups water ½ t salt cheese mix-in (for the two large pans, mixed in a bowl and set aside): 1.5 lb shredded swiss/gruyere mix (or other "italian mix" or jack — ask km) 2 tubs crumbled blue or gorgonzola cheese 2 t dried basil 1½ t black pepper parmesan topping (for the tops of the large pans): 3 cups shredded parmesan cheese (1½ cups each) no-cheese seasoning (for the half pan, mixed and set aside): 1 t olive oil 1 t dried basil 2 tsp black pepper preparation preheat the oven to 425°f (turn down if needed after 30-40 minutes). put lids on the pans and put them in the oven about 10:15. set a timer for an hour. mix the cheeses & spices as described above (for the two large pans and the no-cheese pan). (~11:15) carefully, with hot pad gloves (and maybe with help), stir the pans. don't worry if not thick yet. set the timer for another 15-20 minutes if not thick yet. when the polenta has become thick (after ~60-80 minutes), add the cheese to the cheese-y versions: again carefully with gloves and help, stir half the jack/blue/basil/pepper mix into each of the two full-sized pans. sprinkle half the parmesan cheese over each of the two large pans. don't stir cheese into the half-pan — stir in the olive oil, basil, pepper mix instead. return all pans to the oven, uncovered, for about half an hour (or ok to leave for longer). if the cheese is getting too brown on top, put the lids back on; if it is not getting brown, turn the heat up to 500°f for a few minutes.

title: Artichoke Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad artichoke salad dressing tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~1.5 quarts ingredients 33 oz marinated artichoke hearts (add all, including the oil) 1 tsp tamari (omit if there are no-soy people on the retreat; probably need more salt at the end) 1 tbsp dijon mustard ½ tsp honey ½ tsp white pepper (or more to taste) ½ cup water ½ cup white wine vinegar (or rice vinegar) 1 cup canola oil salt to taste preparation add all ingredients except the oil to the blender. blend. if there's room in the vitamix, drizzle in the oil as you keep blending. if there's no room, transfer to a larger container and whisk in the oil. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper, or other seasonings. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with the smallest ladles.

title: Herbal Dressing
text: all recipes / salad herbal dressing tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: recipe as written makes one container's worth; make it twice (once in the vitamix, once in a second container) for a full doubled batch — about 1.5 qts per container. equipment vitamix container a second 2-quart (smallest square) container with lid ingredients (for one container — you'll put this much in each of the vitamix and the side container) 1½ cups rice vinegar 1½ cups water 1 tsp garlic powder ¼ cup honey (tip: coat the cup with oil first, so the honey slides right out) ¼ cup dijon mustard ½ tsp salt ½ bunch fresh basil leaves, picked off the stems (about ½ cup packed) ½ bunch fresh parsley, main stem removed (rest of stems ok), about ½ cup packed 3½ cups canola oil preparation gather all ingredients, the vitamix container, and a second 2-quart (smallest square) container with a lid. this recipe is doubled: put a full set of the ingredients in each container — it's easiest to add each ingredient to both containers, then move to the next ingredient. rinse the herbs (no need to chop; the vitamix will do it). add the ingredient list above to each container. blend the contents of the vitamix container. fill 2 small pitchers with it. pour the second set of ingredients into the vitamix container and mix it. pour the mixed dressing back into the mixing container, cover, label, and put in the fridge.

title: Lemon Tahini Dressing-IF
text: all recipes / salad lemon tahini dressing-if tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~1.5 qts (quantities below are for one vitamix container — double the recipe using two containers if making extra) equipment vitamix container (a second one if doubling) ingredients (for one vitamix container — do this twice if making extra) 1 cup lemon juice (juice from about 4-6 fresh lemons) ¾ cup parsley 5 cloves garlic 2½ cups water 1½ tablespoons tamari 2 teaspoons ground cumin ½ teaspoon white pepper 1 whole tin of joyva tahini (about 2 cups) ½ cup canola oil preparation gather all ingredients and one vitamix container (double the recipe using two vitamix containers if needed). using an electric juicer, juice the lemons. wash the parsley and cut off the stems (some of the upper stems are fine to leave on). in a medium sized bowl, use a hand whisk to mix the lemon juice, tahini, and 1 cup of the water so the tahini isn't too clumpy (otherwise it will stall the vitamix). then blend in the vitamix with the rest of the ingredients. fill two small pitchers if serving today, otherwise put it in a 1 qt (smallest square) container.

title: Orange Ginger Salad Dressing (2)
text: all recipes / salad orange ginger salad dressing (2) tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: for 1 batch (~48 servings) equipment vitamix microplane zester (or box grater) juicer 2 pitchers ingredients ~1 tbsp zest of 2 limes (zest is just the outermost colored layer of the peel) ~2 tbsp zest of 2 oranges ~1-2 tbsp juice of the two limes 3 cups juice of about 4 oranges, topped off with apple cider vinegar 2" piece ginger, roughly chopped 1 tbsp agave 1½ tbsp cumin 1 cup olive oil 2½ cups light olive oil 2 tsp salt preparation zest limes and oranges with the zester. be careful! very sharp! juice limes and oranges with the juicer (next to the rice cooker). rough chop the ginger (vitamix will do the rest). add all except oil in the vitamix container and mix on low. drizzle oil into the vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Orange Ginger Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad orange ginger salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~1.5 quarts ingredients ~1 tbsp zest of 2 limes ~2 tbsp zest of 2 oranges ~1-2 tbsp juice of the 2 limes 3 cups juice of about 4 oranges, topped off with apple cider vinegar 2 tbsp chopped ginger (about a 2" piece — coarsely chop it and let the vitamix chop it fine along with the rest) 1½ tbsp ground cumin (pre-ground is fine) 1 cup olive oil 2½ cups canola oil preparation using the microplane zester or box grater, scrape off just the colored layer of rind from the limes and oranges, trying not to get much of the white (it is more bitter). be careful with your fingers and knuckles — this tool is very sharp! using the electric juicer, juice the limes and oranges. add all except the oil to the blender. blend. if there's room in the vitamix, drizzle in the oil as you keep blending. if no room, transfer to a larger container and whisk in the oil. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper, or other seasonings. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with the smallest ladles.

title: Orange Tahini Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad orange tahini salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: for 1 batch (~48 servings) equipment vitamix 2 pitchers ingredients 2¼ cups orange juice (check if we bought some, else squeeze ~4-6 oranges; use at least one or two fresh oranges, i.e. the 2 you zest below) 2 oranges, zest of 2 tbsp lemon juice 1 cup tahini (1st use up any partial jars on the breakfast tray; 1 cup = ½ jar) 1 cup water 2¾ tsp salt 1½ tbls agave 2½ tbls finely chopped ginger 5 tbls apple cider vinegar 2 cups light olive oil preparation add all except oil in the vitamix container and mix on low, gradually increasing speed. drizzle oil into the vitamix mixing while you do. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Orange Vinaigrette
text: all recipes / salad orange vinaigrette tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (1 batch) equipment vitamix microplane zester (or box grater) electric juicer 2 pitchers ingredients ~1 tbsp zest of 2 limes (zest is just the outermost colored layer of the peel) ~2 tbsp zest of 2 oranges ~1-2 tbsp juice of the two limes 2 ½ cups orange juice (store-bought fresh oj if available, otherwise juice ~6 oranges) ½ cup apple cider vinegar ½ cup dijon mustard ½ cup agave 1 cup olive oil 2 cups light olive oil 1 t salt 1 tbsp black pepper preparation zest the limes and oranges with the zester. be careful, very sharp! juice the limes and oranges with the juicer (next to the rice cooker). add all ingredients except the oils to the vitamix container and mix on low. drizzle the oil into the vitamix while mixing. gradually increase speed until fully emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover and store in the fridge (if not using today, label and date also).

title: Pasta Puttanesca Notes
text: all recipes / entree pasta puttanesca notes tags: neither, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × notes from watching dan make it. yield: ~50 servings, plus a supper leftover batch ingredients lots of evoo (enough to coat the rondo ⅛" deep or more) ~40 cloves garlic, chopped in mini-cuisinart ~1 ½ cups black olives cured in oil, chopped (e.g. roland foods oil cured black olives, 5-lb bag — far less than this is needed, 1 lb or less is plenty; our kalamatas would work fine too, maybe even better) calabrian peppers, seeded and chopped (e.g. roland foods calabrian chili peppers in vinegar, 17.5 oz) oregano, fresh if we have it: 3-4 long stems, leaves chopped (or probably 3-4 t dried) ~2 ½ cups capers (save the caper liquid) large jar of caper liquid, mixed with an equal part water 12 x 14 oz cans crushed tomatoes 3-4 cups flat leaf parsley, chopped (save some for garnish) 8 lbs spiral pasta, plus 1-2 lbs gluten-free as needed optional: pan-fried chunks of tofu, mixed in parmesan cheese, for serving preparation start a 32 qt pot of water boiling at 9:30 — it takes a long time to boil, 1 ½ hrs even (our pasta insert pan isn't really big enough). prep all ingredients. about 11:00: heat a large skillet (rondo?) over medium heat and add oil, garlic, anchovies, and chopped black olives. sauté the mixture until the anchovies melt into the oil and completely dissolve and the garlic is tender, about 3 minutes — your kitchen never smelled so good! add the olives and capers, sauté some more, then let it sit a while on very low or off to blend the flavors. if using: pan-fry chunks of extra-firm tofu (frozen/thawed worked best for consistency) — he had it in big chunks, though smaller pieces (or none) might be preferable. add the tomatoes, oregano, calabrian peppers, caper water, black pepper, and parsley. (take out a no-tofu portion first if needed, then add the tofu to the rest.) bring the sauce to a bubble, reduce heat, and simmer 8 to 10 minutes. save some sauce out for the gf portion (and/or the no-soy portion, if using tofu). while it simmers, make 2 kinds of pasta (wheat for most, gf for however many need it). you can make the gf pasta by just pouring some of the clean boiling water over the gf pasta (or use tea water) and letting it sit about a minute. when the pasta is a couple of minutes from done (less done than al dente), don't just drain it — lift it out with a big ladle, including some water, and add it to the sauce. add more pasta water to the sauce and try to keep it mixed (it's hard to really mix in the full rondo and it won't come to a full boil, so don't burn it) — the idea is this binds the starches in the pasta and pasta water with the sauce and makes it creamy. garnish with parsley. serve with parmesan and vegan parm.

title: Pasta Sauce
text: all recipes / side pasta sauce tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × make-ahead note: for retreat use, this part must be made ahead and frozen (no time on the retreat day of serving!). this makes about 14 quarts, and freezes in 2 8-qt cambros. this batch is not really enough for serving over pasta on its own — it's sized for lasagna, enough for 2 4" deep pans of lasagna (per the recipe in the folder). yield: ~50 servings (reduced quantities for a smaller batch are also given below, though the source doesn't specify that batch's serving count) equipment rondo or large sauce pot ingredients olive oil, as needed 4 lbs (3 lbs for smaller batch) onions, chopped 4 lbs (3 lbs for smaller batch) mushrooms, sliced 30 cloves (24 for smaller batch) garlic, minced in mini-cuisinart 4 6-lb cans (2 6-lb cans for smaller batch) tomato sauce (or, if only diced tomato, blend in vitamix to make a sauce) 5 cans (3 cans for smaller batch) tomato paste 1 cup + 2 t (¾ cup for smaller batch) dry basil 8 t (6 t for smaller batch) oregano 5 t (3 t for smaller batch) thyme 10 (8 for smaller batch) bay leaves sugar, to taste (¼ cup for smaller batch) sun-dried tomato, optional (2 cups, or 1 ½ cups for smaller batch) salt and pepper, to taste 6 lbs (4 lbs for smaller batch) frozen spinach (or wait and add when thawing) preparation sauté: add olive oil to the pan on medium-high heat and add the onion. when the onions are partly soft, add the mushrooms and sauté until the water is released and mostly cooked off. cook until the onions have softened, then add the garlic. cook the garlic for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, then proceed to add the remaining ingredients. add ingredients: add the tomato sauce, tomato paste, basil, oregano, thyme, bay leaves, and sugar. if using sun-dried tomatoes, they can be added now too. bring to a boil, then lower to a simmer. simmer for 1-3 hours to let the flavors integrate. salt and pepper to taste. add water if the sauce gets too thick (it should be pretty thick, though). add spinach: this step can be done at the end of making the sauce ahead of time, or, best, just before using it for lasagna. if using frozen spinach: thaw and squeeze dry (thoroughly — very important!), then add after the sauce is done.

title: Peanut Lime Dressing
text: all recipes / salad peanut lime dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × this is intended to be served on the side with the thai salad for first-day supper. yield: ~48 servings equipment vitamix bowl ingredients 2 ¼ cups peanut butter 2 cups water 1 ¾ cups lime juice (10-12 limes), keep zest of ~4 (ok to top off with lemons if limes are short or not juicy) ¾ cup rice vinegar 3 tsp sesame oil ½ cup agave ½ cup tamari 6 cloves garlic (vitamix will chop) 1 t ginger (rough chop, vitamix will fine chop) 1 ½ cups light olive oil preparation mix peanut butter and water in a bowl with a whisk. add that and everything else, except the light oil, to the vitamix and mix. drizzle in the oil while mixing to emulsify. taste and adjust the balance of agave, tamari, vinegar, and water.

title: Peanut Sesame Dressing
text: all recipes / salad peanut sesame dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × as a pre-tossed salad — either the supper noodle or rice dish, or a slaw — this is not enough for a self-serve setup. yield: ~48 servings equipment vitamix bowl ingredients 1 t light olive oil 2 t sesame oil ½ cup ginger, chopped in mini-cuisinart 6 cloves garlic, chopped in mini-cuisinart (easiest when thawed) 2 cups peanut butter 3 cups water ¾ cup rice vinegar ¾ cup tamari ½ cup agave preparation pre-mix the peanut butter and water with a whisk (too thick for the vitamix to handle). vitamix the rest and add in the peanut butter/water mix.

title: Pumpkin Chocolate Chip Cookies
text: all recipes / dessert pumpkin chocolate chip cookies tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: 60 cookies ingredients 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, softened 1 cup white sugar 1 cup light brown sugar 2 large eggs 1 teaspoon vanilla extract 1 cup canned pumpkin puree 3 cups all-purpose flour (did it with tj's gluten free... yummy) 2 teaspoons baking soda 1/2 teaspoon salt 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves 2 cups (12-ounce bag) chocolate chips nonstick cooking spray or parchment paper preparation heat the oven to 350 degrees f. spray cookie sheets with nonstick spray or line them with parchment paper. using a mixer, beat the butter until smooth. beat in the white and brown sugars, a little at a time, until the mixture is light and fluffy. beat in the eggs 1 at a time, then mix in the vanilla and pumpkin puree. in a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and cloves. slowly beat the flour mixture into the batter in thirds. stir in the chips. scoop the cookie dough by heaping tablespoons onto the prepared cookie sheets and bake for 15 to 20 minutes, or until the cookies are browned around the edges. remove the cookie sheets from the oven and let them rest for 2 minutes. take the cookies off with a spatula and cool them on wire racks. recipe courtesy george duran, foodnetwork.com

title: ALT Supper Dal Soup or Casserole
text: all recipes / soup alt supper dal soup or casserole tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × this recipe has two forms, made from leftovers: a soup, or a casserole. yield: soup makes ~15-16 quarts; casserole serves ~48 (fills two hotel pans at least half full) equipment largest (32 qt) stock pot, for the soup two 2" deep hotel pans, for the casserole ingredients soup: leftover curried cauliflower (if you made plain steamed, look at the curry recipe and add some of those spices and some frozen peas) ~4 qts leftover dal ~3 medium cans tomatoes with juice 1 large can coconut milk water + bouillon paste, as needed to make a total of ~15-16 qts of soup 1-2 qts leftover rice casserole: leftover dal (~4-5 quarts; if less than this, add a can of white or garbanzo beans) leftover cauliflower and peas (add more frozen peas if short) 2 small cans coconut milk, to mix with the veggies leftover rice (~4-5 quarts; if short, make some more on the stove) 1-2 tsp curry powder, if you added a lot of new unseasoned stuff preparation soup: mix it all up, bring to a boil, taste, turn off, cover, and it should keep hot for the afternoon. serve with sides of leftover raita or yogurt, and leftover chutney or raisins. casserole: layer the food into the 2 pans: rice, veggies, dal. serve with sides of leftover raita or yogurt, and leftover chutney or raisins.

title: Black Eyed Pea Salad
text: all recipes / salad black eyed pea salad tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × assumes the dukkah spice mix is pre-made (see the dukkah ingredients and steps below) — try to make it ahead. yield: ~50 servings, with some leftovers equipment if making the peas and rice: 2 10-12 qt sauce pans ingredients 8 cups dry black-eyed peas (= ~6.25 qts cooked) 3 cups dry wild rice (= ~4 qts cooked) 1.5 cups extra-virgin olive oil 1 ½ cups dukkah (middle eastern spice mix — see dukkah recipe below; try to pre-make) 1 cup lemon juice, plus zest of all the lemons (set the zest aside to use as needed) 1 cup pomegranate molasses, plus ~1 more cup (we always wind up adding another cup at the end) 4 cups walnuts, toasted and chopped (leave big chunks, like halves cut in half) 4 cups pomegranate seeds (= 4 or 5 large pomegranates, seeded) 3 cups minced parsley 1 cup minced mint 6 bunches scallions, thin sliced (white and green parts) salt and pepper, to taste dukkah (spice mix — makes 2 cups, plenty for the salad above) 15 oz can chickpeas/garbanzo beans 1 t olive oil ½ cup pistachios, toasted ⅓ cup black sesame seeds, toasted 2 ½ t coriander seeds, toasted 1 t cumin seeds, toasted 2 t fennel seeds, toasted 1 ½ t pepper 1 ¼ t salt preparation first thing: cook and cool the peas and rice, and toast the walnuts. assuming pre-soaked peas: rinse and cover with water by ~3" in a 12 qt stock pot, bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cover. cook ~20-40 minutes or until done (timing varies) — you want them al dente, not mushy, since it's a room-temp salad. drain and spread out on a sheet pan to cool. rinse the rice and add water at a 4:1 ratio in a 10-12 qt stock pot, bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cover. cook ~40 minutes or until well done (all soft). drain if needed and spread out on a sheet pan to cool. toast the walnuts in a ~250° oven, checking every 10 minutes so they don't get too dark. mix sauce: whisk together the ev olive oil, dukkah, lemon juice, 1 cup of the pomegranate molasses, 1 t salt, and 2 tsp pepper. mix salad: combine the room-temp peas and rice with about ¾ of the pomegranate seeds (save the rest for garnish), the parsley, mint, scallions, and sauce. if serving is more than ½ hour away, refrigerate and bring back out about ½ hour before serving. just before serving: taste and add — typically the 2nd cup of pomegranate molasses, quite a bit of the lemon zest, and maybe another tablespoon of salt. mix in the toasted walnuts and garnish with the remaining pomegranate seeds. dukkah — roast/toast: rinse and dry one 15 oz can of chickpeas, toss with olive oil, and roast at 350° for ~40-50 minutes, tossing every 10 minutes; set aside to cool. also toast the pistachios a few minutes in the same oven if not pre-toasted (no oil), watching carefully. separately, lightly toast the sesame seeds, coriander, and cumin in a skillet on the stove (timing and grinding differ for each). dukkah — grind and mix: process the cooled roasted chickpeas in the mini cuisinart until coarse ground; put in a bowl. pulse the toasted pistachios and sesame to coarse ground and add to the bowl. pulse the coriander and cumin to fine ground and add to the bowl. add the pepper and salt and mix it all together. keeps for about a week in a jar in the fridge.

title: Blackbean Burgers
text: all recipes / entree blackbean burgers tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × using ⅓ cup portions, the larger recipe made 66 burgers — quite a few people ate 2. the smaller batch (~⅔ recipe) made 46, which was way too many for 36 light eaters! you might want to cut these down further for light eaters or fewer people. yield: ~50 servings = 66 burgers (or ~36 servings using the smaller quantities below = 46 burgers) equipment big bowl robocoupe mini-cuisinart sheet pans ingredients 11 t (8 t for 36) vegan egg + water, as directed on package 2 cups (1 ⅓ cups for 36) finely chopped (i.e. in robo coupe) re-hydrated shiitake mushrooms ¾ cup (½ cup for 36) finely minced onion (mini cuis?) 25 (16 for 36) cloves garlic, finely minced (mini cuis?) 8 ¼ cups (6 cups for 36) rolled oats (our std. oatmeal), quickly pulsed 5-6 times in robocoupe (not all the way to flour, in between oats and flour) 16 cups already-cooked black beans = 2 6-lb cans, or fewer than 6 29-oz cans, or ~7 cups dry (for 36: 4 x 29-oz cans = 4 ½ cups dry) — start at 6:40 if you need to cook them, or use an instant pot 3 cups (2 cups for 36) sunflower seeds 3 cups (2 cups for 36) shredded carrots 1 ½ cups (1 cup for 36) shredded beets 1 ½ t (1 t for 36) chili powder 5 t (3 t 1 t for 36) smoked paprika 3 t (2 t for 36) ground cumin ½ cup (6 t for 36) olive oil 3 t (2 t for 36) salt 2 ¾ tsp (2 t for 36) balsamic vinegar 2 t??
