(1 ½ t?? for 36) vegan liquid smoke, if we have any (new idea, start small) 2 ¾ cups (2 cups for 36) chopped parsley preparation early: maybe at 6:40, set the shiitakes to soak in hot (tea machine) water. if you don't have canned or pre-made beans, start the black beans and plan to stay with them until done, or turn off for a sit. ~9:30 prep ingredients: mix the vegan egg per package instructions. strain canned beans, saving the liquid in case needed (probably not). lightly pulse the oats in the robocoupe (using the clear plastic setup), 5-6 quick pulses. squeeze the shiitakes dry, trim the hard stems, and chop in mini-cuisinart, robocoupe, or by hand until finely chopped, not all the way to a paste. mince the onions and garlic (by hand or in mini-cuis). chop the parsley. mix: roughly mix all ingredients in a large bowl. in batches as it fits, pulse the mixture in the robocoupe — not all the way to a puree, leaving some rough texture. if needed, add some bean liquid or more oats to get a good texture for forming into patties. shape: scoop out 1/3 cup portions and shape by hand (wearing gloves) into burger patties. make them on the thin side (~¼"), they are dense. let patties sit about 5 minutes before baking. bake: at 350 for 15 minutes, flip over, and bake 15 minutes on the other side. cheese (optional): maybe add cheese, in the diet-appropriate quantity, for the last few minutes. a popular option with the dairy eaters, or serve on the side. we do now have sliced vegan cheese to put out, but leave several plain.

title: Blended Simple Black Bean Soup
text: all recipes / soup blended simple black bean soup tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × if using dry beans: soak overnight, and allow ~1-2 hours to cook them before adding to the soup. the smaller batch leaves some leftover as a base for a supper soup with lots of added veggies, broth, tomatoes, etc. yield: ~50 servings (~19 qts), or ~36 servings if planning a supper leftover batch equipment 32 qt (largest) stock pot, with pot-saver under it ingredients ~⅓ cup olive oil, to coat the bottom of the stock pot (same for both batch sizes) 4 lbs / ~7 ea (3 lbs for 36) onions, ½" medium/large dice - rough chop 7 lbs (5 ½ lbs for 36) carrots, ½" medium/large dice - rough chop 25 ea (20 ea for 36) garlic cloves, chopped 10 qts cooked = ~4.5 qts dry (8 qts cooked = ~3.6 qts dry for 36) black beans [or ~13 29 oz cans!! or 6.6 lbs dry for shopping — best to measure in quarts] 1 jar better than bouillon (¾ jar for 36), dissolved in ~2 qts hot tea-urn water ~9 qts total water (7.5 qts total for 36) — use 2 qts hot with bouillon as above, plus bean cooking or canned water, plus remaining cold to reach the total 2 ½ t (2 t for 36) oregano 3 t + 1 t (3 t for 36) ground coriander 5 t + 2 t (4.5 t for 36) cumin 1 tsp, taste (¾ t for 36) cayenne pepper 1 t + to taste (1 t to taste for 36) salt ½ cup + 1 t = ~7 ea (½ cup for 36) fresh lime juice, save some zest in case needed (maybe more for avocados) 3 bunches (2 bunches for 36) cilantro, for topping 3 pints (2 ½ pints for 36) sour cream, maybe mixed with green chilies, for topping (and/or see vegan cashew green chili cream recipe) 3 cups (3 cups for 36) roasted pumpkin seeds, for topping preparation prepare ingredients: cook the beans if not using canned. empty the soak water, cover by 2" with fresh water, and save (and measure, if possible) the cooking water to use as part of the soup liquid. dice the onions and carrots by hand, and chop the garlic in the mini-cuisinart. juice the limes (juicer is near the rice-cooker); maybe zest a couple and set the zest aside. mix the bouillon in 2 qts hot tea-urn water. note: this is not a long-cooking soup — about 1 ½ hrs from start to sauté to finished blending. the beans are cooked separately. make soup: be sure the heat-saver disk (on the stove shelf) is placed under the stock pot. coat the bottom of the pot with olive oil to about ⅛" deep. sauté (fry in a little oil, uncovered, stirring occasionally) the onions, garlic, and carrots until the onions are getting soft and translucent (not brown). drain the beans, saving the liquid to use as part of the water measure. add the rest: black beans, bouillon, water, oregano, coriander, cumin, cayenne, and salt. bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer ~30 minutes. check that the carrots are soft. puree the soup until smooth and creamy (there will still be little flecks of beans) using the immersion blender. stir in the lime juice and taste (perhaps more salt, pepper, lime zest, or cayenne). serve with any or all of: cilantro, sour cream and/or vegan green chili cream, diced avocado, and roasted pumpkin seeds.

title: Bread sides for White Bean Soup
text: all recipes / side bread sides for white bean soup tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × either garlic bread or plain artisan bread with "basil butter" (either only if not having butternut squash — check with km what's planned and what ingredients we have). equipment either large trays or a 4" hotel pan foil for the bread bowls for the butters ingredients garlic bread: 4-5 loaves of sourdough or other "white" artisan bread olive oil (~1 cup to start?) ~20 cloves of garlic, minced in the mini cuisinart optional: dried basil and marjoram (~1 t each) basil butter (with plain heated artisan bread): 4-5 loaves mixed artisan breads, sliced thick (or use 2-3 of tj's big triangles of whole wheat bread, cut triangle in thirds or fourths, then slice) gluten-free bread slices as needed (~1⅕ per gf person) 1 ¼ lb regular butter ½ tub earth balance (check quantity estimate against the no-dairy head-count) 1 bunch basil preparation garlic bread: mix the oil, garlic, and herbs (if using). put the mix on the needed number of regular and gluten-free slices (do the gf first, to avoid contamination of oil and utensils). slice the bread in half lengthwise (separating the top half and bottom half) and spread both halves with the garlic oil mix. put uncovered on large trays. about 11:30: bake at 350 for ~½ hour, or until lightly browning (gf may take less time). slice each baked half into ~1 ½" thick slices and serve in a basket with a decorative cloth (bottom of the cloth rack). basil butter: put the regular butter out early to soften a bit (not so important if using the robocoupe). wash the basil. proportion the basil between the regular butter and the earth balance. works well to mix the regular butter in the robo coupe (clear bowl setup) and the non-dairy in the little mini-cuisinart. put the sliced bread into a hotel pan, cover with foil or a domed lid. about 11:30: heat at 350. serve in a basket with the butters on the side.

title: Broccoli Salad
text: all recipes / salad broccoli salad tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × quantities of mixins are estimates — feel free to vary to your taste or what you have. (could also just do simple steamed broccoli instead.) yield: ~50 servings (or ~36), probably some leftovers for a final snack equipment large bowl ingredients 1 case = 14 heads (~10 heads for 36) broccoli (raw for this, or very lightly steamed), cut into quite small florets, ~¾" ~1 ½ cups (~1 cup for 36) sunflower seeds ~1 ½ cups (~1 cup for 36) sliced almonds ~1 ½ cups (~1 cup for 36) raisins ~1 cup (~¾ cup for 36) optional, if have: red onion or scallion, finely minced (could pan-fry the raw red or yellow onion to mellow it out) ~1 ½ cups (~1 cup for 36) shredded carrots, or optional if we have some: sun-dried tomatoes, chopped dressing: 4 cups = 1 32 oz jar (3 cups for 36) veganaise ½ cup (⅓ cup for 36) agave ½ cup (⅓ cup for 36) lemon juice ½ cup (⅓ cup for 36) apple cider vinegar 1 ½ tsp (2 tsp for 36) salt preparation make the dressing. toss all ingredients together.

title: Brown Basmati Rice Curry
text: all recipes / entree brown basmati rice curry tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × note: there may be bags of tj brown jasmine in either pantry — replace or supplement with brown basmati (they cook together ok). yield: ~48 servings with supper leftovers, or ~36 servings (also with supper) equipment large strainer rice cooker ingredients 16 cups (12 cups for ~36) brown jasmine or basmati rice 24 cups (18 cups for ~36) water preparation rinse the rice well using the large double-mesh strainer (may take several batches). (~10:30–11:00) add water in the ratio of 1 ½ cups of water for each cup of rice. about 10:45: plug in and turn on the cooker. it will take about 50-60 minutes to cook, then it switches to warm. before serving, check that it has switched to warm. if so, carefully open the lid and fluff it with a wood or plastic tool. unplug the machine to turn off the "warming". serve with wooden spoons so as not to scratch the container.

title: Brown Basmati Rice
text: all recipes / side brown basmati rice tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: 16 cups dry rice if doing a supper leftovers batch, or 13 cups if not equipment large strainer rice cooker ingredients 16 cups (13 cups if no supper leftovers) brown basmati rice 20 cups (16 ¼ cups if no supper leftovers) water (ratio 1 : 1.25) preparation rinse the rice well using the large double-mesh strainer (may take several batches). (~10:30–11:00) add the rice and water, per the quantities above, to the rice cooker. leave it unplugged until ready to start cooking. about 10:45: plug in and turn on the cooker. it will take about 50-60 minutes to cook, then it switches to warm. before serving, check that it has switched to warm. if so, carefully open the lid and fluff it with a wood or plastic tool. unplug the machine to turn off the "warming". serve with wooden spoons so as not to scratch the container.

title: Brown Rice
text: all recipes / side brown rice tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × quantities were reduced a bit as of 7/23 (per cc). yield: 12 cups dry rice if doing a supper leftovers batch, or 10 cups if not equipment large strainer rice cooker ingredients 12 cups (10 cups if no supper leftovers) either short grain (preferred) or basmati brown rice 15 cups (12 ½ cups if no supper leftovers) water (ratio = 1 rice : 1.25 water) preparation (~10:30–11:00) rinse the rice well using the large double-mesh strainer (may take several batches). put the damp rice in the cooker. about 11:00: add water to the rice in the cooker, per the quantities above. plug in and turn on the cooker. it will take about 50-60 minutes to cook, then it switches to warm. before serving, check that it has switched to warm. if so, carefully open the lid and fluff it with a wood or plastic tool. unplug the machine to turn off the "warming". serve with wooden spoons so as not to scratch the container.

title: Butternut Squash Soup
text: all recipes / soup butternut squash soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × see squash ordering note at the end of the ingredients and instructions. yield: ~50 servings (~24 qts), with supper leftovers equipment 32 qt (largest) stock pot, with pot-saver under it ingredients ~⅓ cup light olive oil, to coat the bottom of the stock pot 4 cups thinly sliced onions (ok if they get diced too) 4 cups thinly sliced shallots (optional/n/a) 8 cups thin sliced leeks (white part only) — see bouquet garni below, maybe save some greens 4 cups (or 2) smallish diced carrots 24 cloves (or 12) garlic, roughly chopped in mini cuisinart 25 lbs cubed butternut squash (see squash ordering note below) ½ cup (or ¼?) agave 1 jar better than bouillon, dissolved in ~2 qts hot tea-urn water 12 qts total water (2 qts hot with bouillon as above, plus remaining 10 qts cold) bouquet garni: 32 sprigs fresh thyme (~2 packs), 8 sprigs parsley, 8 bay leaves, 2 tsp black peppercorns — made into 4 packets, each containing 8 sprigs fresh thyme, 2 sprigs italian parsley, 2 bay leaves, and ½ tsp black peppercorns or pepper (for a half batch: 16 sprigs thyme, 4 parsley, 4 bay, and 1 tsp pepper total, across 2 packets) 1 t salt, plus more to taste optional topping: 2 quarts greek yogurt (plus a vegan option), fine without optional topping: nutmeg, shaken from a shaker (shakers are in the stair pantry) preparation prepare ingredients: locate all ingredients. make the bouquet garni. slice/dice all the onions, leeks, shallots, and carrots, if not already done. mix the bouillon in 2 qts hot tea-urn water. sauté: be sure the heat-saver disk (on the stove shelf) is placed under the stock pot. coat the bottom of the pot with light olive oil to about ⅛" deep. sauté (fry in a little oil, uncovered, stirring occasionally) the onions, leeks, shallots, and carrots until the onions are getting soft and translucent (not brown). add the diced squash, garlic, 3 t salt, and 1 ½ t pepper, and cook gently for a few minutes, reducing the heat as necessary to keep the garlic and squash from coloring. may need to add a little of the stock to make it stirrable. stir in the agave and cook, stirring, for a few more minutes. add stock and simmer: add the stock and bouquet garni bags, bring to a simmer, and cook until the squash is tender. puree: puree the soup until smooth and creamy using the immersion blender. taste and salt as needed. squash ordering note: pre-ordering 25 lbs of pre-cubed squash a week in advance from coast used to be the plan, but they have a terrible record of forgetting it, messing it up, or bringing the wrong thing — and it's way too hard for yogis to peel and cube that much hard squash along with everything else needed for the meal. new discoveries: order or buy ~30 lbs (~10 each) of whole butternuts and freeze them whole, then thaw overnight — the skin gets really soft and is easy enough for yogis to peel and cube. too watery to roast this way, but fine for soup. or, better: poke several holes in them with a fork and roast whole the day before in the oven for ~1 hr at 400, then let cool — easy to peel afterward. could also microwave, but pre-roasting might be easier for a crew of 10.

title: Cashew Green Chili Cream(1)
text: all recipes / side cashew green chili cream(1) tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × goes well with the "blended black bean soup" recipe. for a simpler alternative: add some lemon juice and salt (both to taste) to a carton of vegan cashew yogurt, and add green chilies if you like and there are no chili allergies. yield: ~48-50 servings (smaller amounts in parentheses below are for a vegan-only batch) equipment vitamix ingredients 4½ cups (2 cups for vegan-only) cashews, soaked in water as long as overnight, or as short as needed 2 cups (¾ cup for vegan-only) water (fresh, for blending, not the soaking water) — maybe start with a bit less, see what's needed for a thick sauce 4-5 small cans (3 small cans for vegan-only) diced green chilis, drained (or start with a bit less water) ¼ cup (2 t for vegan-only) lime juice 6 (3 for vegan-only) garlic cloves (blending will chop them) 1 tsp (½ tsp for vegan-only) salt ½ tsp (¼ tsp for vegan-only) ground cumin pinch, more than ⅛ tsp (tiny pinch for vegan-only) cayenne (if using mild chilis) preparation soak the cashews as long as you can (longer is smoother, but grainy is fine). drain them. add all ingredients to the vitamix blender (works better than the robocoupe for this). blend until smooth. taste and adjust seasonings until you like it.

title: Cashew Green Chili Cream
text: all recipes / side cashew green chili cream tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × goes well with the "blended black bean soup" recipe. for a simpler alternative: add some lemon juice and salt (both to taste) to a carton of vegan cashew yogurt, and add green chilies if you like and there are no chili allergies. yield: ~48-50 servings (smaller amounts in parentheses below are for a vegan-only batch) equipment vitamix ingredients 4½ cups (2 cups for vegan-only) cashews, soaked in water as long as overnight, or as short as needed 2 cups (¾ cup for vegan-only) water (fresh, for blending, not the soaking water) — maybe start with a bit less, see what's needed for a thick sauce 4-5 small cans (3 small cans for vegan-only) diced green chilis, drained (or start with a bit less water) ¼ cup (2 t for vegan-only) lime juice 6 (3 for vegan-only) garlic cloves (blending will chop them) 1 tsp (½ tsp for vegan-only) salt ½ tsp (¼ tsp for vegan-only) ground cumin pinch, more than ⅛ tsp (tiny pinch for vegan-only) cayenne (if using mild chilis) preparation soak the cashews as long as you can (longer is smoother, but grainy is fine). drain them. add all ingredients to the vitamix blender (works better than the robocoupe for this). blend until smooth. taste and adjust seasonings until you like it.

title: Chicken Fried Tofu
text: all recipes / entree chicken fried tofu tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × note: set aside the equivalent of one whole sheet if you want to make a leftover batch for a full house — people will over-eat this until it's all gone! you may need to put the last half-sheet in to cook over lunch while you serve the other 3½. yield: 48 servings with a leftover supper batch reserved (or the smaller amounts in parentheses below for 48 servings with no leftover supper reserved — about 2.5 slices each — or roughly 36 servings if also serving supper) equipment 4 large baking sheets & 1 half sheet (or sometimes 3 large & 3 halves if you roasted the beans) note: best with no parchment — hard to serve with it 3 medium metal bowls ingredients 16 lbs (12 lbs for the smaller batch) tofu, sliced thin — try to get 12 slices per lb (for a 1 lb slab: cut in half, cut each half in half again, then each fourth into thirds); bigger batch ≈ 192 slices / 4½ pans at 42 slices per pan, smaller batch ≈ 144 slices / 3 pans + one half pan ~4 cups (~3 cups for the smaller batch) canola oil, set up in 1-2 medium-small metal bowls for dipping coating mix: 5½ cups (4 cups for the smaller batch) nutritional yeast (ideally "large flake", but regular works ok too) 5½ cups (4 cups for the smaller batch) "no-chicken" vegetable broth powder (pseudo-chicken broth mix, frontier brand — in the stair pantry spice boxes) 2 cups (1¾ cups for the smaller batch) corn starch 3½ tbl (2½ tbl for the smaller batch) sage 3½ tbl (2½ tbl for the smaller batch) thyme preparation setup: preheat oven to 350°. (assume the morning yogi has sliced the tofu.) mix the coating mix — use "large flake" nutritional yeast if we have it. plan to do this with all 3 cooks: set up one bowl of oil and 2 bowls of coating mix. no parchment! efficient layout on the center island: uncoated tofu, then sheet-pan / mix-bowl / oil-bowl / mix-bowl / sheet-pan, worked by person 1, person 2, and person 3. coat pieces: person 2 dips each slice of tofu in oil and places them alternately in one of the 2 mix bowls. persons 1 and 3 pat the coating onto both sides of the slices and lay them flat (very close to each other but not overlapping) on the sheet pans. takes ~15 minutes. bake: allow about 30 minutes to bake, but keep an eye on the browning process. no need to flip the pieces — just check for crispy golden brownness on both sides of sample pieces. if done early, maybe turn off the oven and leave them in to stay warm. for the bigger batch: bake 4 pans for lunch and slide the extra half-pan in as soon as you can, taking it out at the end of lunch (~30 minutes) — this pan goes entirely to the supper (plus hopefully some leftovers from the other 4 pans, so set some aside!). if you plan on supper, hold back at least ¾ or a whole tray for that — people tend to eat this until it's gone. serve on the baking sheets.

title: Chili Sides
text: all recipes / side chili sides tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment largest salad bowl (over the pan rack) 2-3 small/medium bowls (under the island) small pitchers (hanging on the center rack) ingredients 6 cups grated cheddar cheese, in small/medium bowls 3 (16 oz) containers sour cream, in a small/medium bowl 2 bunches cilantro, chopped (if on hand), in a small/medium bowl

title: Chili
text: all recipes / entree chili tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × note: "supper leftovers" here assumes something like a light sprinkle on top of nachos, not a whole other serving. equipment 32 qt (largest) stock pot for the beans rondo for the chili mini cuisinart ingredients to cook dry beans: 4 quarts dry pinto beans (km soaks them the night before) water, to cover the beans for chili: 1 cup olive oil 8 lbs chopped yellow onion 7 lbs red bell pepper, chopped 5 lbs sweet potato, peeled and chopped into small pieces 50 cloves garlic, minced in the mini cuisinart 1¾ cup chili powder (more if needed) ½ cup oregano ¼ cup smoked paprika ½ cup cumin 1 six-lb can diced tomatoes salt, to taste cooked beans (from above) preparation rinse the beans in a strainer, place in the 32 qt stock pot, and cover with water by 6-8 inches. bring to a boil, lower to a simmer, and cook for 1-1½ hours until the beans are tender. add water if too dry. sauté: heat the olive oil in the rondo and add the onions; sauté until translucent. (note: maybe separate out a second no-bell-pepper version here, for andrea or other teacher needs.) add the bell peppers and yams/sweet potato and cook until they begin to soften. add ingredients: add the chili powder, oregano, and cumin to the sauté mixture and cook for a few minutes. add the tomatoes, bring to a boil, and lower to a simmer. add beans: we keep cooking the beans separately because they need to cook almost all morning to get soft — they might not get enough heat mixed in with the rest too soon. when the beans are soft enough to eat, mix them in with the rest of the stew. finish: let simmer until serving time, adding bean liquid as needed if it's getting too thick (or you can cover and turn it off — it will stay warm).

title: Chutney Raita
text: all recipes / side chutney raita tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × note: usually done by 9:30 by the yogi helper. apricot/mango chutney ingredients 4 cups dried apricots, chopped (tip: put some oil on a paper towel and oil the knife frequently — it cuts sticky apricots more easily) 3 cups raisins 4 cups, about 1 lb dry, dried mango, pre-soaked (save the water), cut into bite-sized pieces ¾ cup coconut 6 cups water (include the mango water if saved) 3 t rice vinegar 1½ t cloves, ground (see below) 2 t coriander seeds, ground (see below) preparation soak the mangoes in a metal bowl using hot water (from the tea machine) for a few minutes; save the water. cut into bite-sized pieces. cut the apricots into fourths or sixths. grind the cloves and coriander in the black spice grinder (together is fine). mix all the ingredients together in the smallest stock pot. bring to a boil, reduce heat to a simmer, and let simmer for about 15 minutes. remove from heat, cool, and refrigerate if making for the next day. nice to garnish with nasturtiums or herbs. raita make 2 versions: one dairy (larger batch), one vegan (smaller batch). check the roster and maybe adjust the dairy:vegan proportions — the amounts below assume fewer than about 10 vegan, with the rest dairy. ingredients 2½ (dairy) or ½ (vegan) hothouse cucumbers, shredded (hand box-grater or robocoupe) 1½ cartons dairy yogurt (½ carton vegan yogurt for the vegan batch) — use more yogurt if not enough cucumber ⅓ cup chopped (dairy) or 2 t chopped (vegan) mint (maybe from the garden outside the kitchen if any, else look for bought) ½ lemon (dairy) or ~1 tsp (vegan) lemon juice and zest 1 t (dairy) or ¼ t (vegan) ground cumin ½ t (dairy) or large pinch (vegan) white pepper ½ t (dairy) or ¼ t (vegan) garlic powder salt, to taste preparation wash the mint, pick the leaves, and cut into thin strips. mix with the yogurt(s). add the shredded cucumber if using. add the spices and mix. cover and refrigerate.

title: Curried Cauliflower and Peas
text: all recipes / entree curried cauliflower and peas tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment one 6" (deepest) full-sized hotel pan with lid ingredients 16 small heads (1 case) cauliflower 3 lbs frozen peas (note the bag size — if 10 oz, use 4-5 bags) ½ cup canola oil 4 t curry powder 1 t paprika 4 t spice mix for the dal 1 (6 lb) can, or 2 smaller cans, coconut milk 2 (14 oz) cans diced tomatoes preparation make sauce, add veg, and cook on stovetop: open the cans of coconut milk and tomatoes so they're ready to pour. mix the curry powder, paprika, and dal spice mix together. fry the spice mix for a minute or so in the oil in the bottom of the hotel pan on low heat, watching and stirring the whole time. add the coconut milk and tomatoes to the fried spice mix. add the cauliflower and stir it up a bit if possible. cover and cook over medium heat (lower the heat once it gets going). (~11:15) cook about 30 minutes, checking and stirring occasionally. (~11:45) add the peas and stir it all up if possible.

title: Dal
text: all recipes / entree dal tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × note: a few changes from lael, 11/2023. yield: ~50 servings. quantities below are listed as three numbers — 50 servings with supper leftovers reserved / 50 servings with no supper leftovers / 36 servings if also serving supper. equipment 32 oz stockpot (the largest one) largest skillet ingredients 5 qts (4 qts for 50 no leftovers, 3 qts for 36) red lentils (d1:c3) 9 qts (7 qts for 50 no leftovers, 5½ qts for 36) water (add more if needed, plus we use the liquid from the tomatoes below) 4 t (3½ t for 50 no leftovers, 3 t for 36) salt 3½ lbs (3 lbs for 50 no leftovers, 2 lbs for 36) onions, medium dice 1¼ cup (1 cup for 50 no leftovers, ⅔ cup for 36) chopped ginger — 1¼ cup = 7.5 oz (+2 t if making the fancy roasted cauliflower version) 30 cloves (25 cloves for 50 no leftovers, 20 cloves for 36) garlic, chopped (divide the total in half — used in 2 ways below) 4 tbs (3½ t for 50 no leftovers, 3 tbl for 36) turmeric 1½ cups (1¼ cups for 50 no leftovers, 1 cup for 36) light olive oil 4 tbl (3½ t for 50 no leftovers, 3 tbl for 36) mustard seeds 4 tbl (3½ t for 50 no leftovers, 3 tbl for 36) cumin (pre-ground, or toasted and ground from whole) 4 tbl (3½ t for 50 no leftovers, 3 tbl for 36) coriander (pre-ground, or toasted and ground from whole) 1½ tbl (1 t for 50 no leftovers, 1 tbl for 36) fenugreek ¼ tsp (¼ t for 50 no leftovers, ¼ tsp for 36) cayenne pepper — maybe more, taste! 1 (6 lb) can + 1 (28 oz) can, or 4 (28 oz) cans (for 50 no leftovers: 1 six-lb can or 3 28-oz cans; for 36: 2 28-oz cans) canned tomatoes, with juice (note: one 6 lb can ≈ 3.6 28-oz cans) 4 ea (4 ea for 50 no leftovers, 3 ea for 36) bay leaves ½ cup (~⅓ cup for 50 no leftovers, ~⅓ cup for 36) lime juice (save the rinds to zest if using the roasted cauliflower recipe) salt, and juice of 1-2 lemons — as needed preparation start lentils simmering: sauté the onions in some oil in the bottom of the stock pot. rinse the lentils in a strainer under running water — they tend to clump, so separate with your fingers; this may take several batches. put the lentils, bay leaves, water, and salt in the stock pot. bring to a boil and skim off the foam. after the foam is skimmed off, lower the heat. add the ginger and half the garlic. reduce to an active simmer. check frequently that it's still actively simmering, but not over-boiling. stir often, all the way to the bottom, and always put a heat deflector under this pot — it's easy to burn. maybe use a big paddle. if it seems to be getting too thick, you can add more water; it should be thick but still pourable. prepare the spice mixture once the dal is cooked (add to the dal shortly before serving, about 12:00): heat the oil in the large skillet until hot. add the mustard seeds and stir, cooking just until they pop (a few seconds). once they pop, add the cayenne, turmeric, bay leaves, cumin, coriander, fenugreek, and the rest of the garlic, stirring a few times. turn heat to low and cook until the garlic just begins to brown. add the tomatoes and cook a few minutes, stirring often. remove the bay leaves from the dal if you can find them, and add the spice/tomato mixture along with the lime juice. taste for heat and salt. (probably add the juice of 2 lemons, maybe a little brown sugar too — have all the cooks taste it!)

title: Fancier Mushroom Gravy
text: all recipes / side fancier mushroom gravy tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: 48 servings (larger amounts include a reserve for supper leftovers; smaller amounts in parentheses are for 48 servings with no supper leftovers) equipment large skillet small rondo (aka "prune pot") or 10 qt pot ingredients 6 lbs (5 lbs for no supper leftovers) onions, slivered 5 lbs (4 lbs for no supper leftovers) regular white or brown mushrooms, sliced 7 (6 for no supper leftovers) dried shiitake mushrooms (optional, usually don't have) 20 cups (16 cups for no supper leftovers) stock: cups of water as shown, plus 1 tsp better than bouillon per cup (use mushroom btb if we have any, else "no-chicken" is fine) 2½ tbls (2 tbls for no supper leftovers) sage 2½ tbls (2 tbls for no supper leftovers) thyme 7 tbls (6 tbls for no supper leftovers) tamari 5 tbls (4 tbls for no supper leftovers) sherry vinegar 2½ tsp (2 tsp for no supper leftovers) black pepper salt, if needed (taste after adding the tamari) 8 tbls (7 tbls for no supper leftovers) corn starch, dissolved in cold water — start with less and see preparation prepare: in the largest skillet, begin to caramelize the onions. (caramelize means frying them in oil but on very low heat for a long time — about 30-40 minutes — stirring occasionally until they all turn brown but not burned.) this step is optional; you can just sauté them until soft if short on time. start stock: mix the bouillon, add in the dry shiitakes if using, and simmer (ideal to use the 8 qt "prune pot"). chop shiitakes: when the shiitakes are soft, fish them out, remove the stems, chop them up, and return them to the stock. sauté mushrooms: when the onions are done, set them aside and sauté the mushrooms in the same skillet (you may need more oil). when done, you could "deglaze" the skillet: put a cup or so of stock water in the skillet and stir it up to capture the flavored oil and caramelized bits, then pour it back into the stock. add rest: add the caramelized onions, sautéed mushrooms, and all other seasonings except the cornstarch to the stock. thicken: mix the cornstarch with enough cold water to dissolve it. add to the gravy. bring to a boil for 3-5 minutes until it thickens. return to a simmer. taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

title: Garlic Bread
text: all recipes / side garlic bread tags: vegan, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment large trays ingredients 4-5 loaves of sourdough or other "white" artisan bread olive oil (~1 cup to start) ~20 cloves of garlic, minced in the mini cuisinart optional: dried basil and marjoram (~1 t each) preparation mix the oil, garlic, and herbs if using (these quantities are a guess — make more if needed). put the mix on the needed number of regular gluten-free slices (do the gf slices first, to avoid contaminating the oil or utensils). slice the bread in half lengthwise (separating the top half and bottom half). spread both halves with the garlic oil mix. put uncovered on large trays. (~11:30) bake at 350° for about ½ hour, or until lightly browning (gf may take less time). slice each baked half into about 1½" thick slices. serve in a basket with a decorative cloth (bottom of the cloth rack).

title: Ginger Tofu
text: all recipes / entree ginger tofu tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: 48 servings (lunch, plus some leftovers set aside for a yam side dish) equipment two (and maybe a half) large baking trays blender large 4 qt pitcher ingredients 15 lbs tofu (we use a whole case of 12 x 15.5 oz packs, plus another 2 lbs if we have it), sliced into 12 slices per pack (by the morning prep yogi) sauce: 1¼ cups chopped ginger (≈ 7.5 oz ginger root) 15 cloves garlic 3 cups (1½ containers) miso (whatever color we have in stock — e.g. red, white, yellow) ~1 tsp sesame oil 1½ cups agave 1½ cups rice vinegar 2¼ cups tamari 4 cups water garnish: 2 bunches scallions, thinly sliced (white and light green parts) preparation preheat oven to 400° (after the assist has toasted the seeds). slice each ~pound of tofu into 12 long rectangular slices (i.e., 6 per half-pack in our usual brand). lay flat on sheet pans. (prep yogi usually does this.) find and set out all the sauce ingredients. rough-cut the ginger into chunks about ½ inch long — no need to peel it. using one of the blender pitchers (you can share the machine base with the assist cook if needed): put the ginger chunks, garlic, miso, sesame oil, agave, rice vinegar, and tamari (i.e., all sauce ingredients except water) in the blender and process, gradually raising the speed until smooth. pour into a large plastic pitcher, add 4 cups of water, and whisk. pour the sauce over the tofu. let the tofu sit in the marinade until time to bake it. put the pans in the oven, uncovered, for 45-60 minutes total. set a timer to baste every 20 minutes or so. if it's looking too dark, turn the heat down or off. if it's not getting brown by the last 20 minutes, turn the heat up. just before serving, garnish the pans with scallions.

title: Kale with Mushrooms
text: all recipes / side kale with mushrooms tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: 48 servings (lunch only) equipment roasting sheet 2 steamer pan setups ingredients ~⅓ cup (?) olive oil, enough to lightly coat the sliced mushrooms 1 case + 6 heads dino kale, de-stemmed and each leaf-side torn into 3-4 pieces 4 lbs sliced mushrooms preparation first thing in the morning (before you need the oven for the tofu): preheat oven to 350°. toss the sliced mushrooms in olive oil and spread on a baking sheet. roast for ~15-30 minutes at 350° (time depends on how thick they're sliced). check every 10 minutes, stir, and swap pans on oven shelves as needed. set aside when done — i.e., when they look appealing enough to eat! (or: some prefer to sauté them in the largest skillet — check the overhead rack or apron area for large skillets.) (~11:00) steam the kale using 2 steamer setups — it will probably take two rounds of 2 steamers each, each about 10 minutes. (or: some prefer to sauté the kale in the rondo, the big round pan under the rice cooker.) transfer the cooked kale, layering with the roasted mushrooms, into a 4" deep hotel pan to serve. cover to keep warm.

title: Lasagna
text: all recipes / entree lasagna tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × could either make an extra no-dairy, no-egg lasagna with the "vegan ricotta" recipe and vegan mozzarella (if shopped for), or have sauce, spinach, beans, and gf rotelli on the side. yield: 48 servings (or 36 — makes 2 full pans, or 1½ pans for the smaller batch) equipment 2 (2-inch deep, or could use 4" deep for no-slosh but only half-filled) full-sized hotel pans mixing bowl 12 qt pot for side pasta, or another pan/half-pan if making vegan lasagna ingredients 1 recipe (¾ recipe for 36) pasta sauce, pre-made (see other recipe) 6 lbs (4 lbs for 36) frozen spinach (also listed in the sauce recipe as an option — best to add here) 6 lbs (5 lbs for 36) ricotta 8 (6 for 36) eggs 5 lbs (4 lbs for 36) shredded mozzarella, separated in half 2 t (1½ t for 36) salt 1 t (¾ t for 36) pepper 3-4 packages (as needed for 36) no-boil gluten-free lasagna noodles (4 10oz packs of barilla, or 3 tj 1lb packs, seemed plenty) simple gf/vegan alternative (if planned ahead — make 1 or ½ pan of vegan tofu-based lasagna instead, using the "vegan ricotta" recipe and vegan mozzarella; our sauce is already vegan): ~¾ cup per person pre-made sauce, including spinach ¼ cup per person white (cannellini) beans gf pasta such as spirals — see package for portion per person preparation prepping ingredients (this assumes the sauce was pre-made earlier — see the separate pasta sauce recipe): preheat oven to 375°. start the sauce reheating — see if you need to add the spinach, and if so, drain it very well (press hard with spoons into a large strainer). mix the ricotta, eggs, half the mozzarella, salt, and pepper. maybe reserve: reserve some sauce (depending on headcount) for the gf/df alternative (see below). reserve some mozzarella and/or parmesan for a side condiment for special diets. layering: spray the pans with spray oil! layer the lasagna per pan: bottom (first) — a thin layer of sauce to coat the pan, noodles, ricotta mix (if doing 2 pans use ¼ of the total here, if doing 1½ pans use ⅓ of the total here), a thicker layer of sauce (5-6 cups for a whole pan), a light sprinkling of mozzarella, noodles, ricotta mix (another ¼ or ⅓ of the total), a thicker layer of sauce (5-6 cups for a whole pan), a light sprinkling of mozzarella, noodles, a thin layer of sauce; top (last) — a generous sprinkling of mozzarella. baking: top the pans with the new dome lids (on top of the pan rack), or make peaked lids of foil. bake 60 minutes, remove the lids, and bake another 20 minutes. remove from the oven and let set for 20-30 minutes before serving. make gf/dairy-free alternative: if needed, make the gf spiral pasta per package instructions so it's done just prior to serving (typically boils 6-10 minutes). heat the reserved sauce and white beans in a saucepan. combine the pasta with the sauce and beans.

title: Lentil Grape Salad
text: all recipes / salad lentil grape salad tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~50 servings with a supper-leftovers reserve (or the smaller amounts in parentheses below for either 50 servings with no supper reserve, or 36 servings if also serving supper) equipment 12 qt stock pot large skillet large metal mixing/serving bowl ingredients 12 cups uncooked (9 cups uncooked for the smaller batch) french green lentils (the small dark green ones) water, to cover by ~3" (we will drain them, so plenty is fine) 3 bay leaves 4 t (3 t for the smaller batch) salt, plus more to taste ~½ cup olive oil, as needed to sauté (maybe use a little more to keep the whole dish from being too dry) 24 each ≈ 16 lbs (18 each ≈ 12 lbs for the smaller batch) leeks, thinly sliced, white to light green parts only (sold in bunches of 3, so 8 bunches or 6 bunches) 7 t (5 t for the smaller batch) dijon mustard, more to taste 2 cups (1½ cups for the smaller batch) sherry vinegar, more to taste 2¼ cups (1¾ cups chopped for the smaller batch) fresh mint (maybe from the garden outside the kitchen door, or bought in clamshell packs) 1¼ cup (1 cup for the smaller batch) chopped fresh parsley 4 cups (3 cups for the smaller batch) nuts, usually pecans or shelled pistachios — consider nut allergies, maybe set aside no-nut portions for lunch and supper 6 lbs (4 lbs for the smaller batch) red grapes, cut in half to release some juice ~2 lbs feta cheese, crumbled, on the side if we have some left (set up by assistant) preparation cook lentils: rinse the lentils; put the lentils, water, salt, and bay leaves in a stock pot. bring to a boil and lower to an active simmer. stir occasionally and add water if it gets low. simmer about 20-30 minutes until the lentils are cooked but not mushy. when the lentils are done, strain them in a colander and remove the bay leaves if you can find them. make leeks and sauce: sauté the leeks in the olive oil until soft, using the large skillet or the rondo. make a sauce of the mustard, sherry vinegar, and a bit more olive oil, and mix (note: we now add this to the warm lentils, not sautéed with the leeks). mix salad: mix the lentils, mustard sauce, grapes, mint, parsley, and sautéed leeks in a large metal or plastic bowl. just before serving: check for nut allergies, maybe set aside a no-nut portion, then add the nuts to the main portion. serve in a large plastic or metal bowl, with crumbled feta cheese on the side if there's enough.

title: Lentil Soup
text: all recipes / soup lentil soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (14-15 qts) equipment 32 qt (largest) stock pot, with pot-saver under it small skillet zester juicer mini cuisinart ingredients ~⅓ cup olive oil (to coat the bottom of the stock pot) 4 lbs onions, ½" dice 4 lbs carrots, ½" dice 1 head celery, ½" dice 4 lbs yukon potatoes, ¾" dice 2 t salt 10 c lentils (if we have plain ones use them, otherwise use "french green") 4 bay leaves 12 qts water (add more later if too thick) 2 c (~1½ bunches) parsley, finely chopped 4 stalks marjoram (from the garden, or 2 t dry marjoram or 2 t dry thyme) 4 t cumin seeds 25 cloves garlic, + 5 more for later (probably in the white yogi freezer) 4 bunches greens, usually collards, could be kale etc. ~2 t zest, ~½ c juice — zest and juice of 2 lemons 4 t sherry vinegar 3 t smoked paprika rest of paste: ½ cup more olive oil, plus the 5 garlic cloves saved above 2 t each, to taste — salt and pepper (add each gradually and taste) preparation prepare ingredients: locate all ingredients. measure out the lentils, check for stones, rinse, and set aside. dice the onions, carrots, celery, and potatoes. collards: remove the thick stem from the center, slice the leaf halves crosswise into 1" wide strips. wash the lemons. zest the lemons (scrape off the thin outermost yellow layer of skin) using either the microplane (sharp!) or box grater (suggest wearing the cut-resistant glove for either). juice the lemons using the electric juicer or wooden reamer. wash the parsley, discard the main trunk of the stems, and finely chop the rest. chop the garlic in the mini cuisinart on the chop setting (best if thawed). toast and grind the cumin using the small skillet, watching carefully just until it's fragrant. grind in the black spice grinder, wiping out the grinder before and after. sauté: be sure the heat-saver disk (on the stove shelf) is placed under the stock pot. coat the bottom of the pot with olive oil, about ⅛" deep. sauté (fry in a little oil, uncovered, stirring occasionally) the onions until they're getting soft. add in the carrots and celery and 2 t salt. sauté for 20 minutes or so to develop the flavor. add in the potatoes and sauté for another 10 minutes. tip: you may want to stand on a stool and/or use the big paddle to get good stirring leverage. cook lentils: add the lentils, bay leaves, marjoram, cumin, garlic, parsley, and water to the pot and stir. gradually bring to a boil on medium-high heat, then reduce to an active simmer. let it simmer at least until the lentils are soft (1 hour or more) — fine to leave it 2 hours or more, or until you leave for the meeting. stir occasionally, adding more water if it's getting too thick. prepare paprika mix: (~4:00) prepare the final paprika mix to add in later: chop the extra garlic, sauté it with the smoked paprika in the extra olive oil in the small skillet for about a minute. turn off the heat and leave it. add greens: (~4:20) just before going to the orientation meeting, stir in the greens. turn off the heat and put a lid on the pot. after meeting: (~5:10) leave the meeting early. add the lemon juice, zest, sherry vinegar, and smoked paprika oil mix. add half the suggested salt and pepper, taste, and add more as needed. put the gluten-free bread in the oven just to warm up a bit. help get the main bread into a basket.

title: Mashed Potatoes
text: all recipes / side mashed potatoes tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: 48 servings with a supper-leftovers reserve (or the smaller amounts in parentheses below for 48 servings with no supper leftover, ~36 if also serving supper) equipment 2 6" deep hotel pans large metal bowl potato masher (hand tool) maybe mixer ingredients 20 lbs (15 lbs for the smaller batch) yellow, white, or red potatoes, cut into quarters (yukon gold are best if available) ~1½ cups (1 cup for the smaller batch) earth balance (no-soy if needed) 1 tbls + to taste (2 tsp + to taste for the smaller batch) salt preparation put into 2 deep hotel pans and cover with water and 1 tsp salt per pan. cover and bring to a boil. cook until tender (estimated 40-45 minutes). drain each pan into a large colander and put back in the pan. working in batches, mash with a hand-held pastry cutter (or try the electric mixer or immersion blender if you like it super smooth, but rough is fine). add in earth balance as needed for good mashed-potato texture. salt to taste (lightly — they can always add more).

title: Moroccan Chickpeas and Chard
text: all recipes / entree moroccan chickpeas and chard tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings with supper (or ~36 servings if planning supper leftovers) equipment rondo for stew ingredients 4 lbs (3 lbs for 36) chickpeas, dry (soaked overnight or quick soaked by km) 5 lbs (3.5 lbs for 36) yellow onions, chopped 2 lg (1 ½ lg for 36) jalapeno pepper, seeded & chopped fine 20 cloves (15 cloves for 36) garlic ⅓ cup (4 tbls for 36) ginger 2 t (1 ½ t for 36) salt 3 t (2 t + 1 t for 36) turmeric 3 t (2 t + 1 t for 36) paprika 2 t (1 ½ t for 36) cinnamon 1 ½ t (1 t + 1 t for 36) cumin 1 ½ t (1 t + 1 t for 36) black pepper ½ tsp (pinch for 36) cayenne (to taste, not too hot for yogis, more if no jalapeno) 2 6oz cans (1 ½ cans for 36) tomato paste 8 bulbs (6 bulbs for 36) fennel bulb (save fronds for garnish) 9 bunches (7 bu for 36) rainbow chard (stems chopped separately, leave in lg chunks) 15 (11 for 36) carrots, diced 14 lg-ish (12 lg-ish for 36) yukon potatoes 3 cups (2 ¼ cup for 36) dried apricots, diced ½ cup (6 t for 36) lemon juice, save zest also 2x32oz (1 ½ for 36) greek yogurt (for side) 4 bunches (3 bu for 36) cilantro (for side) preparation note: the chickpeas are not cooked separately, just add them into the stew at the ~10:15 step below. sauté: heat oil in rondo pan over medium heat. add onion and jalapeño and sauté until limp, a few minutes. add garlic, ginger, salt, turmeric, paprika, cinnamon, cumin, black pepper and cayenne and sauté until they release their fragrance, about 2 minutes. add tomato paste and sauté for another minute, until darkened but not burned. (if tomato paste looks too dark too quickly, lower heat.) add fennel, chard stems, carrot and turnip/potatoes and continue to sauté until vegetables start to soften, about 20 minutes. add chickpeas: by about 10:15, rinse and drain the soaking chickpeas and add to the stew. add fresh water to cover. return heat to high if you lowered it and bring to a simmer. partly cover pot, lower heat to medium low, and simmer for about 1 1/2 to 2 hours (i.e. for the rest of the morning), until chickpeas are softened. add more water as needed (this should be like a stew and nearly fill the rondo once the chard is added). finish: about 11:30, add apricots. about 11:50, add chard leaves and lemon juice & zest to taste, continue simmering until chard is tender, about 5 minutes longer. season with more salt if desired, and serve garnished with reserved fennel fronds. serve with greek yogurt and cilantro on the side.

title: Peanut Stew
text: all recipes / entree peanut stew tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings with supper leftovers (or ~36 servings with supper leftovers) equipment rondo ingredients 2 qts dry (1 ½ qts dry for 36) chickpeas (pre-soaked) (or ~6 28oz cans for 48, ~4.5 cans for 36) ~3 (~3 for 36) bay leaves (for cooking chickpeas, or add to stew if canned) ½ cup (as needed for 36) olive oil 5 lbs (4 lbs for 36) red onions, chopped ¾ cup (4 ½ tbls for 36) minced ginger 30 cloves (23 cloves for 36) garlic, minced 2 ½ cups (2 cups for 36) peanut butter 9 lbs (7 lbs for 36) yams, chopped into 1-inch (not too small) cubes 6 lbs (5 lbs for 36) zucchini, cut 4x by length and 1" cubes [optional] 1 6lb can (about 1.5 cups less for 36) chopped tomato w/liquid (have another med. can in reserve if needed) ½ tsp (¼ tsp for 36) cayenne (more to taste if needed, not too hot for yogis) 6 quarts water + ¾ jar broth paste (4 qts 2 cups water + ½ jar broth paste for 36) broth: mix 3 quarts of hot tea-urn water with all the veggie broth paste, then use the rest of the water cold as needed 9 bunches (7 bu for 36) kale (stems removed), roughly chopped 4 cups (3 cups for 36) peanuts, separated in half — half go whole into the stew, half are chopped and added for garnish salt and pepper to taste preparation note: the stew will thicken once kale is added. cook chickpeas: these should have been soaked overnight or "quick soaked" earlier. drain soaking water, rinse, cover with fresh water. add ~3 bay leaves and bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. let them cook while you get the rest of the stew ready, checking occasionally for doneness. sauté: sauté onion until translucent. add garlic & ginger and sauté another minute. add remaining ingredients in steps: add yams, tomato, peanut butter, cayenne, and veggie broth (as needed). bring to a boil and lower to a simmer. cook until sweet potatoes are tender. (~11:15) add zucchini and drained chickpeas. (~11:30) add kale and half the whole peanuts. check seasoning. garnish with the rest of the chopped (or whole) peanuts to serve.

title: Pinto Beans
text: all recipes / side pinto beans tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~50 servings either way. use the first (larger) quantity below unless the retreat is very small (~30) or you don't want leftovers for a supper casserole — pinto beans are a popular leftover for rvs. second, smaller quantity is for no supper leftovers. equipment 20 qt stock pot for the beans large skillet for the onions ingredients 5 qts (3.5 qts for no supper leftovers) pinto beans, pre-soaked (rinse soaked beans) 9 qts (7 qts for no supper leftovers) fresh water 4 tbls (3 tbls for no supper leftovers) salt 4 (3 for no supper leftovers) bay leaves oil, as needed to coat the pan 4 ½ lbs (3 lbs for no supper leftovers) onions, medium chopped 25 cloves (20 cloves for no supper leftovers) garlic 5 cans (3 cans for no supper leftovers) tomato paste (mix with ½ cup water to aid in mixing if helpful) 6 t (4 t for no supper leftovers) whole cumin 4 ½ t (3 t for no supper leftovers) oregano 2 t (1 ½ t for no supper leftovers) chili powder ¾ t (½ t for no supper leftovers) cayenne pepper (add gradually and taste, heat varies) 3 t (2 t for no supper leftovers) brown sugar 20oz = 5 sm cans (12oz = 3 sm cans for no supper leftovers) green chiles — look at can size, may vary, go by oz more salt to taste preparation prepare and start beans: rinse the soaked beans. put beans, salt and fresh water in the stockpot. bring to a boil and skim off any foam. when done skimming, add bay leaves. turn down to a vigorous simmer; check frequently to be sure it is still simmering actively and has adequate liquid. prep other ingredients: chop garlic in mini-cuisinart. toast & grind cumin. sauté other ingredients: in the large skillet or small brazier, sauté the onions. when they are translucent, add the garlic. stir tomato paste with 1/2 c. water and add to the onion mix; simmer 10 minutes. add all the other seasonings (cumin, oregano, chili powder, brown sugar, salt). simmer another 10 minutes, stirring frequently. combine and finish: scrape the onion & spice mix into the bean pot. put a heat deflector under the bean pot! let it continue to simmer, checking and adding water as needed to make a good burrito filling consistency (not too soupy, not too thick to burn). about 11:45, add the green chilies, check taste, and add salt as needed. serve with slotted spoons if still watery.

title: Polenta
text: all recipes / side polenta tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × note: this version is simplified to be all vegan, no cheese — serve cheese on the side for the whole meal. yield: 2–3 full pans depending on supper plans (only 1 pan needed for a group of ~36 with no supper; ask how many pans are needed — usually 2 if no supper or a supper "minestrone" soup is planned, 3 if a supper casserole is planned). ingredient quantities below are per full pan. equipment if doing supper: 3 full pans — serve 2 and save the third for supper. if no supper, just 2 full-size pans. use 4" (medium depth) pans so they don't slosh when going into the oven. if making 3 pans: since there are only 2 4"-deep full pans, use 2 4" half pans or a 6"-deep one for the third, and save that third pan for the supper leftover. ingredients (per full pan) 5 cups polenta 20 cups = 5 qts water with bouillon (3 t bouillon paste mixed with 1 quart of hot tea-urn water per pan, the other 4 quarts water cold) 1 t salt (optional — the bouillon is already salty, taste before adding) 2 t olive oil 2 t dried basil 1 t white pepper ½ cup (optional, quantity needs to be verified) nutritional yeast ~¼ cup per pan (optional) earth balance, stirred in at the end if using preparation mix and bake polenta: preheat oven to 425°. spray pans with spray oil. mix polenta and seasonings in each of the pans you are using. leave pans uncovered and put them in the oven about 10:15. set a timer for an hour. stir & maybe cover: about 11:15, carefully (with hot pad gloves, and maybe with help) remove the pans and stir. peek every 20 minutes or so. if the top is getting too brown, put the lid on. if done, turn off the ovens and leave the pans inside to stay warm. maybe stir in some earth balance at the end. alternate (stovetop, from lael): some cooks prefer this stovetop version — it frees up the oven so you can pre-roast more of the ratatouille veggies (which improves that dish), but it takes more attention. bring 10 quarts water to a boil (get this going early, ~10:45); be sure a heat deflector is under the pot. add ⅓ cup salt. about 11:20, slowly pour 10 cups polenta into the pot, whisking constantly to avoid lumps. keep whisking while it thickens. when thickened, turn the flame down to a bare simmer. stir every 10 minutes for 40 minutes — this long simmer brings out the sweet corn flavor. add more boiling (tea machine) water if too stiff. stir in some earth balance (or other vegan butter) to taste. note on using leftovers for the next night's supper: if there's quite a bit left (~4 qts), it's best to do this right after lunch, during the put-away period: grease a sheet pan with olive oil, spread the polenta on it to ~½–¾" thick (¾ of a sheet pan is enough), sprinkle with basil and vegan parmesan, and put the sheet in the fridge (maybe covered with foil or another sheet pan). at 5:00 on supper day, put in a 400° oven for a half hour. cut into ~7x8 pieces. (oven-baked polenta could probably be used the same way, but it's harder to spread.)

title: Portuguese Kale White Bean Soup
text: all recipes / soup portuguese kale white bean soup tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × adapted from moosewood restaurant favorites. yield: ~48 servings (~14–15 qts), or ~36 servings (~11 qts). this gets eaten — no leftover meal is expected. equipment 32 qt (largest) stock pot with pot-saver under it zester juicer spice grinder mini cuisinart separate 12 qt pot to give the beans a head start prep ahead: soak 2 qts dry cannellini beans overnight, or quick soak in the morning, or use ~7 x 28oz canned beans (not as good, gets mushy). ingredients whole lg jar (¾ jar for 36) sun-dried tomatoes (whole 32–34oz jar, oil-packed), drained, reserve oil for sauté if needed, olive oil (to supplement sun-dried tomato oil for sauté) 4 lbs (3 lbs for 36) onions, ½" dice 2 lbs (1 ½ lbs for 36) carrots, ½" dice ~4-6 bulbs (4 bulbs for 36) fresh fennel bulbs (quantity depends on size), ½" dice 4 lbs (3 lbs for 36) potatoes (ideally yukon gold), ½" dice 14 cloves (11 cloves for 36) garlic, chopped in mini-cuisinart 4 ½ tbls (3 ¼ tbls for 36) fennel seeds, very lightly toasted and ground 4 ½ tbls (3 ¼ tbls for 36) thyme 2 ½ tsp (1 ¾ tsp for 36) salt, & to taste at end 1 ¼ tsp (1 ¾ tsp for 36) pepper, & to taste at end 7 qts water + 1 jar better than bouillon (5 qts + 1 cup water + ¾ jar for 36) — dissolve the better than bouillon in 1 qt hot tea water plus the remaining water cold (can use the bean cooking water, not the soaking water) 1 lg (+ 1 med) can (1 lg can for 36) canned diced tomatoes (i.e. 1 6lb6oz + 1 28oz) 2 qts dry (1 ½ qts dry for 36) cannellini (white) beans (or ~6-7 28oz cans) 5 bunches (4 bunches for 36) kale, torn into pieces (very roughly 2"x2") ~1 cup = ~8 lemons (~¾ cup = ~6 lemons for 36), juiced — save some zest in case needed, add to taste preparation cook beans: the beans should have been pre-soaked. rinse soaked beans. in a separate 12 qt pot, cover with fresh water, bring to a boil and right away turn to a low simmer, skim if needed, and toss in a stalk of fresh rosemary. add to the main soup pot about 10:30. locate & prepare ingredients: strain the oil from the oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, saving the oil to use for sautéing the onions in the step below. set aside the tomatoes. when the beans are done, use bean broth and/or water as needed to make bouillon with better than bouillon. dice onions, carrots, fresh fennel, and potatoes (usually veggie choppers). kale: remove the thick stem from the center and tear into large, bite-sized pieces. wash lemons. zest 1-2 lemons (scrape off the thin outermost yellow layer of skin) using either the microplane (sharp!) or box grater (suggest wearing the cut-resistant glove for either). set aside in case needed at the end. juice lemons using the juicer (near the rice cooker). lightly toast the fennel seeds dry in a small skillet. grind using the spice grinder. chop garlic in the mini cuisinart on the chop setting (best if thawed). sauté: be sure the heat-saver disk (on the stove shelf) is placed under the stock pot. using the reserved sun-dried tomato oil if you have it, or else olive oil, sauté the onions until they are getting soft. add in chopped garlic and 2 tsp salt. sauté another minute. add the ground fennel and diced fennel and cook for ~10 minutes. stir in the carrots, potatoes, thyme, sun-dried tomatoes, and black pepper and cook for ~20 minutes. combine & cook soup: about 10:30, add tomatoes, bouillon, and beans. stir well, bring to a boil, and reduce to a simmer. be sure there is a pot-saver/heat disperser under the pot. simmer until potatoes are just tender. add greens: about 11:30, stir in the kale. final seasoning: stir in (some) lemon juice & zest to taste and salt to taste. serve with a large bowl of parmesan.

title: Quick Mushroom Gravy
text: all recipes / side quick mushroom gravy tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings with supper leftovers (the alternate quantity column covers ~48 servings with no supper leftovers, or ~36 servings with supper). equipment 2 largest skillets 10 qt stock pot (or the largest of the small pots) ingredients olive oil, as needed 2 lbs (1 ½ lbs alt) onions, chopped 2 lbs (1 ½ lbs alt) regular white or brown mushrooms, sliced 4.5 qts (3.5 qts alt) stock: cups of water as shown + 1 tsp better than bouillon "no-chicken" per cup (avoid mushroom btb, it has soy ingredients) 2 tbls (1 ½ tbls alt) sage (double if using fresh) 2 tbls (1 ½ tbls alt) thyme (double if using fresh) 5 tbls (4 tbls alt) tamari — less, to taste; the bouillon is quite salty 4 tbls (3 tbls alt) sherry vinegar 2 tsp (1 ½ tsp alt) black pepper salt, if needed (taste after adding tamari — really doubt this is needed) ¾ cup (½ cup alt) corn starch, dissolved in cold water (may need more; quantity shown is of the corn starch — use about an equal quantity of cold water to dissolve well) preparation brown mushrooms & onions: use the 2 largest skillets and brown mushrooms and onions at the same time. cook the mushrooms at least until all the water is gone. ideally get the onions a bit browned, but at least very soft. when done, you could "deglaze" the pans: put a cup or so of stock water in the pans and stir it up to capture the flavored oil and caramelized bits, then pour it back into the stock pot. stock: mix the bouillon and water until dissolved (for ~1 qt of the water, use some hot tea-urn water to dissolve the bouillon). add rest: add all other ingredients except the cornstarch. thicken: mix cornstarch with enough cold water to dissolve it. add to the gravy. bring to a boil for 3-5 minutes until it thickens. return to a simmer. taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

title: Quinoa
text: all recipes / side quinoa tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (lunch only) equipment large strainer rice cooker (clean rice cooker if needed) ingredients 10 cups quinoa (note: we sometimes have red, sometimes white quinoa — use what you can find and prefer) 12 ½ cups water (ratio of quinoa:water we use is 1:1 ¼) preparation (~10:30) rinse the quinoa very thoroughly, or it has a bitter taste, using the large double-mesh strainer and running your fingers through it (may take several batches). put the rinsed grains into the rice cooker (not turned on). they can sit there rinsed until it's time to add the water and cook. (just before 11:00) add water (as above) in the ratio of 1 ¼ cups of water for each cup of quinoa. (11:00) plug in and turn on the cooker. it will take about 45 minutes to cook, then it switches to warm. set a timer to check when it should be done. let it sit for a few minutes, then carefully open the lid and fluff it with a wood or plastic tool. if there is time, cover the pot with 2-3 clean white towels and gently set the lid back down. this will absorb excess moisture and help the quinoa be fluffier. you must unplug the machine to turn off the "warming." serve with wooden spoons so as not to scratch the container.

title: Ratatouille
text: all recipes / side ratatouille tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~50 servings with supper leftovers and more (or ~50 servings with no supper leftovers, using the alternate quantities). note: the larger quantity won't fit in the rondo — good to save some for supper in any case, by moving ~6-8 qts to a small stock pot and setting it aside for a supper soup base. equipment large rondo pan with lid 2-3 large baking sheets small stock pot ingredients 8 (7 alt) globe eggplant, cubed to 1" cubes olive oil (and some spray), enough to coat the rondo 5 lbs (3 lbs alt) onions 6 lbs (5 lbs alt) mushrooms, in chunks (e.g. quartered) 20 (14 alt) garlic 2 6lb cans = 7 28oz cans (1 6lb can + 1 28oz can = 4.5 28oz cans alt) diced tomatoes (note: 1 6lb can = ~3.5 28oz cans) 3 6oz cans (1 ½ cans alt) tomato paste 5 t (3 t alt) basil 5 t (3 t alt) thyme (& maybe ~4 t fresh oregano from the garden) 5 t (3 t alt) fennel seeds, toasted and ground 1 cup (¾ c alt) chopped parsley 15 (12 alt) red/yellow/orange bell peppers, 1" chunks 4 bulbs (3 bulbs alt) fresh fennel bulbs, ~1" dice 13 lbs (10 lbs alt) zucchini, ~1" chunks salt & pepper to taste (est. ~1 t salt at least) 1 bunch (¾ bu alt) fresh basil garnish, washed & slivered preparation roast eggplant & maybe fennel: set the oven to 375° (you can put the eggplant and fennel in as soon as ready, no need to wait for preheat). set the eggplant up on large baking sheets, spread in a single layer. spray the paper with olive oil spray. optionally, do the same with the fresh fennel (or it can just be added in with the mushrooms). roast the eggplant (& fennel) cubes for about 30 minutes, stirring once. set aside. you may also roast the peppers and even the zucchini if you have time and oven space. while it roasts, get the polenta ready for the oven (see other recipe). prep: chop the garlic in the mini-cuisinart (chops better when thawed). lightly toast 4 t fennel seeds in a small skillet, watching closely, and grind in the spice grinder (wipe or brush out the spice grinder before and after). sauté: coat the rondo with olive oil to about 1/8" and sauté the onion. when the onions get translucent, add mushrooms (& fresh fennel if using, whether pre-roasted or not). sauté until they soften. add the tomato paste to the onions & sauté a couple of minutes. add the garlic and sauté briefly. option: drain the tomatoes, saving the liquid to add in as needed or for future use in a leftovers casserole. add the tomatoes, dried herbs, and parsley. let the sauce simmer for ~15 minutes. add vegetables: add the zucchini and eggplant. (this is where you should shift some off into a side stock pot, both for space and to save for supper.) if andrea fella is teaching, set aside a no-pepper version for her (including enough for leftovers if having): could add some celery or extra fennel, if available, to her version instead of bell peppers. add bell peppers to the main version. put a heat deflector under the rondo pan! the stew can simmer anywhere from 45-90 minutes; stir often. maybe cover if not too juicy. prep sides, season, garnish: wash and cut the basil leaves into thin strips. set up a side bowl of parmesan cheese. about 30 minutes before serving time, check that the vegetables are all soft and taste the seasoning. add more herbs if needed, salt and pepper to taste. garnish with the slivered fresh basil, if using. serve in the rondo pot.

title: Red Lentil Dal
text: all recipes / entree red lentil dal tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment largest stockpot note: to ease this day, you may want to prepare the spice mix during the work period or even sometime the day before. ingredients 4 ½ qts red lentils 9 qts water (add more if needed) 1 cup chopped ginger up to 2 qts baked yams, mashed (optional, if available, or use a 29oz can of pumpkin puree) 5 lbs diced onions 15 cloves, minced in cuisinart garlic 6 ½ t cumin seed, toasted & ground (spice mix, shared with the cauliflower dish) 6 ½ t coriander seed, toasted & ground (spice mix, shared with the cauliflower dish) 1 ½ t fenugreek seeds, toasted & ground (spice mix, shared with the cauliflower dish) 4 ½ t turmeric (spice mix, shared with the cauliflower dish) 5 ½ t brown mustard seeds (spice mix, shared with the cauliflower dish) ½ t cayenne pepper (add more if needed) 3-4 lemons, juiced salt, to taste preparation start lentils simmering: rinse the lentils in the strainer under running water. they tend to clump, so separate with your fingers — this may take several batches in the strainer. put lentils & water in the stock pot. bring to a boil and skim off foam. after foam is skimmed off, lower heat and add the chopped ginger and cubed yams. reduce to an active simmer. check frequently that it is still actively simmering, but not over-boiling, and stir often all the way to the bottom. always put a heat deflector under this pot. to stir, you may want to stand on a stool and use the big paddle. if it seems to be getting too thick, you can add more water — it should be thick, but still pourable. while it simmers, prepare the yams, spices & garlic: check if there are leftover yams, peel and mash if not already done, or get out a can of pumpkin puree (or skip this if none). chop the garlic in the mini-cuisinart. toast the cumin, coriander, and fenugreek. use the small skillet, keep the heat low, and wait for it to start to be fragrant and a little brown, but not very (and not burned!). grind them (you may grind together) in the spice grinder. add turmeric and brown mustard seeds. set aside 4 t of the mix to add to the cauliflower. stir and check the lentils frequently — this dish is easy to burn! sauté onions & spices: use the large skillet, coat it lightly (~1/8") with canola oil. sauté the onions over med/low heat until soft. add the garlic and sauté another minute. add the spice mix and cayenne and continue to sauté over low heat for 1-2 minutes. set aside if it's not yet time to add to the dal. stir and check the lentils frequently — this dish is easy to burn! blend the lentils, add the remaining ingredients: when the lentils are soft (maybe ~11:15), add the yams or pumpkin. using the immersion blender, blend the dal to a smooth consistency, being careful not to submerge the blender beyond the stem, and using a spoon to stir up the dal from the bottom. add the onion/spice mixture to the dal, stirring well. cook for about 5 minutes and then add the lemon juice & maybe zest to taste, stirring well. salt to taste. when it's ready, you can put a lid on it and leave it turned off — it will stay warm.

title: Roast Brussels Sprouts
text: all recipes / side roast brussels sprouts tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment 2 large baking sheets ingredients 25 lbs brussels sprouts, cut in half lengthwise unless tiny salt & pepper olive oil preparation preheat oven to 400°. toss in a large bowl with oil, salt & pepper to taste. spread out on large baking sheets (no parchment). put most of them face down if cut in half. put tray in oven, check & stir every 20 minutes. probably takes about 45 minutes. done when tender and nicely browning.

title: Roast Butternut Squash
text: all recipes / side roast butternut squash tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment large baking sheets (est. 3-4) ingredients 1 case butternut squash (peel left on, seeds removed, cut into big pieces — typically 4 pieces out of the round end, 2-4 pieces out of the thinner end of each). for a smaller retreat, just do it all and have extra for soup later. oil, to coat preparation preheat oven to 400° (or okay to put in not pre-heated). oil each piece if not done already. roast ~2 hours (allow the whole morning, can be unpredictable; okay to serve at room temp if done early). test doneness with a fork — should be very soft, browning lightly.

title: Roast Squash
text: all recipes / side roast squash tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment 4 large baking sheets ingredients 30 lbs (25 lbs for no supper leftovers) mixed yellow squash and zucchini 5 onions (4 onions for no supper leftovers) red onion, slivered salt olive oil preparation preheat oven to 400°. veggie choppers will leave squash cut up and salted in a colander to drain over a bowl. lunch cook should thoroughly rinse salt off the squash. using white towel(s), pat dry in batches and put into a large bowl. add in slivered red onion if using. toss with olive oil. spread out on baking sheets (no parchment). if making along with cornbread, cook in two batches to free up half the oven for later, and serve with half at room temp, half hot. put tray in oven, check & stir every 20 minutes. probably takes about 40 minutes. done when soft and nicely browning.

title: Roasted Butternut Squash
text: all recipes / side roasted butternut squash tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment large baking trays ingredients butternut squash, peel left on, chunked ~6-8 pieces per squash olive oil (optional) mixed herbs (optional — good to keep this plain for diets, and maybe make herbal or maple butters instead) preparation optional: rub large pieces of squash with olive oil and sprinkle tops with mixed herbs (avoid garlic for diets — good to keep this plain and make maple butter instead, as below). place pieces on large baking trays. bake at 375° for 1 ½ to 2 hours total (allow for even more). done when quite soft and slightly brown. okay to turn off the oven and leave them in there if done early. serve with regular and non-dairy butter. or, for an extra treat, make maple butter: in the robo-coupe or mini-cuisinart, mix butter, maple syrup, and maybe nutmeg to taste; make a version with vegan butter too.

title: Roasted Cabbage with Fennel
text: all recipes / side roasted cabbage with fennel tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings with supper leftovers (or ~36 servings with supper leftovers) equipment large bowl 4 large baking sheets ingredients 8 heads (6 heads alt) cabbage (regular white/green), cored and cut into wedges olive oil, as needed 4 tbls (3 tbls alt) fennel seed 2 oranges, juiced and zested preparation preheat oven to 400°. toss cabbage wedges with olive oil in a large bowl. we aren't trying to keep the wedges together — let it all fall apart and get covered in oil. spread onto large baking sheets with parchment. sprinkle with fennel. put in oven about 11:00 and start checking about 11:45. done when lightly browning on the edges. transfer to a large bowl to serve. toss with orange juice and zest. lightly salt to taste.

title: Roasted Cubed Tofu
text: all recipes / entree roasted cubed tofu tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × note: sauce quantities are approximate — use your judgement. yield: ~48 servings (or ~36 servings) equipment huge salad bowl to toss (maybe a smaller one to serve) ingredients 9 lbs (7 lbs alt) cubed extra firm (or firm) tofu light olive oil, as needed ~⅓ cup rice vinegar ~½ cup tamari small amount sesame oil ~½ cup white sesame seeds (optional) preparation mix oil, vinegar, tamari, and sesame oil. toss cubed tofu in the mixture. spread on parchment on large baking trays. roast at 350° for ~40 minutes. check every 15 minutes or so, turning when brown on the bottom. sprinkle with sesame seeds & serve in a large bowl.

title: Roasted Root Vegetables
text: all recipes / side roasted root vegetables tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~50 servings equipment large baking sheets large mixing bowl ingredients note: any mix of these vegetables works — the weights below are a suggestion; total should be about 22 lbs. 10 lbs beets, 1" cubed 10 lbs yams, 1" cubed 2 lbs carrots, 1" chunked (sometimes more of the above and no carrots) olive oil, to lightly coat (either toss in a bowl or use spray) preparation preheat (probably both) ovens to 400°. toss each kind of vegetable separately with enough olive oil to lightly coat. consider chopping up and adding some rosemary from the garden. line as many baking sheets as needed with parchment paper (probably already set up by veggie choppers). spread the oiled vegetables among the number of sheets needed to keep them only 1 level deep, keeping vegetable types separate in case they finish at different times. veggies go in ~10:45. stir and turn every half hour. done when tender and starting to caramelize. as they finish, transfer to a metal bowl and serve.

title: Roasted Zucchini Carrots and Corn
text: all recipes / side roasted zucchini carrots and corn tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~50 servings with supper leftovers (or ~35–50 servings using the smaller quantities, without leftovers) equipment 3 full-sized baking sheets, or a mix of large and small to fit ingredients 17 lbs (12 lbs for the smaller batch) zucchini, ½ case = 11 lbs + 6 (or 1) extra lbs 12 lbs (10 lbs for the smaller batch) carrots olive oil spray 3 lbs (2 lbs for the smaller batch) frozen corn preparation note: you may not be able to fit all the zucchini on sheets — if not, steam the extras and save them for the supper casserole. preheat both ovens to 375°. line the pans used for the carrots with parchment paper. don't line the pans for the zucchini. if the veggie choppers have already put the vegetables on trays, spray with olive oil spray; otherwise hand-mix with oil in bowls and then spread on trays. the carrots benefit from extra long cooking, and the corn gets added last, so try this timing (with help from a timer): (10:40) put the carrots in. (11:00) put the zucchini in and stir the carrots. (11:30) stir both and pour the corn over the top of all the pans, return to oven. (~11:40) you'll be putting tortillas in the oven about here — you may have to combine veggies into fewer pans to make room, and lower the oven temp for the tortillas once the veggies are done. (11:45) check for doneness. the zucchini and carrots should be softened (not mushy but easy to fork through) and beginning to brown slightly. when done, empty them all into a 4” hotel pan and mix.

title: Slaw Salad
text: all recipes / salad slaw salad tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (or ~36 servings using the smaller quantities) equipment huge salad bowl to toss, maybe a smaller one to serve ingredients 4 lg heads (3 lg heads for 36 servings) white cabbage and/or napa cabbage 1 med head (¾ med head for 36 servings) red cabbage 1½ lb (1¼ lb for 36 servings) carrot, shredded ~2 cups (~1½ cups for 36 servings) chopped mint (try left side kitchen garden, or bought) baby spinach, if needed (to fill the bowl and lighten it up) 1 recipe slaw dressing: consult km — options that work from the salad dressings file: peanut lime is best if no peanut allergies, or save some out undressed, or use sesame ginger (good with the lime version), or ginger miso 3 lbs? (2 lbs for 36 servings) peanuts, for serving on the side (~1 lg white serving bowl worth) preparation thinly shred all the cabbage (napa by hand; white and purple using the wider blade in the robo). this does get eaten up and shrinks if pre-dressed, so pile it up and use all 5 cabbages even if it's looking like a lot in the smaller salad bowl. use shredded carrots we have, or shred some more. wash and chop the mint. toss it all together with the spinach if using it to fill a salad bowl. maybe save some out undressed, and dress the rest. tip: mix in the huge salad bowl over the pan rack, then move to the smaller bowl to serve. serve with a bowl of peanuts on the side.

title: Soup Cornbread Sides
