text: all recipes / side soup cornbread sides tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment medium and small bowls ingredients 3 16 oz containers sour cream, in 2 white oval bowls ~3 lbs shredded cheddar, in 2 white oval bowls or one large serving bowl (e.g. the blue one) 4 bunches cilantro, chopped (if on hand), in a small/medium bowl butter and earth balance, for the cornbread

title: Steamed Broccoli W2
text: all recipes / side steamed broccoli w2 tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment 2 6” hotel pans, 2 steamer pans, 2 lids ingredients 1 case broccoli preparation we're doing a whole case, so you may need to do 2 rounds — it can all be finished a bit early, anytime from 11:30 onward or so, and be served room temperature if needed. setup 2 steamer assemblies: get the two 6” deep (deepest) solid pans and fill them with 2” of water. set the water-filled pans across 2 burners each. divide as much broccoli as will fit (with the lid fully closed) into the 2 perforated pans. set the perforated pans in the water-filled pans and put a lid on each. turn on both burners. let the broccoli steam for about 5 minutes after the water comes to a boil. carefully lift the lid and check on it. when it looks done, remove the perforated pans from the base pans and empty the broccoli into a large metal serving bowl. refill one or both pans with any remaining broccoli and steam for just 2–3 minutes (we may use some of these for further baking, so leave it barely done). leave the pans on the counter (out of the water) so we can serve more if needed.

title: Steamed Broccoli
text: all recipes / side steamed broccoli tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment 2 6” hotel pans, 2 steamer pans, 2 lids ingredients 1 case broccoli preparation you may need to wash the steamer pans used for the tempeh to reuse for the broccoli, or maybe the veggie choppers have already set it up. we're doing a whole case, so you may need to do 2 rounds — it can all be finished a bit early, anytime from 11:30 onward or so, and be served room temperature if needed. setup 2 steamer assemblies: get the two 6” deep (deepest) solid pans and fill them with 2” of water. set the water-filled pans across 2 burners each. divide as much broccoli as will fit (with the lid fully closed) into the 2 perforated pans. set the perforated pans in the water-filled pans and put a lid on each. turn on both burners. let the broccoli steam for about 5 minutes after the water comes to a boil. carefully lift the lid and check on it. when it looks done, remove the perforated pans from the base pans and empty the broccoli into a large metal serving bowl. refill one or both pans with any remaining broccoli and steam for just 2–3 minutes (we may use some of these for further baking, so leave it barely done). leave the pans on the counter (out of the water) so we can serve more if needed.

title: Steamed or Roasted Green Beans
text: all recipes / side steamed or roasted green beans tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~13 lbs green beans (if there's a lot more on hand, the extra is meant for another upcoming meal, e.g. chicken tofu) equipment roasted method: 2 large baking trays, foil steamed method: steamer pan setup (either 1 pan re-used for 2 batches, or 2 setups) ingredients 13 lbs green beans olive oil, for tossing salt, and maybe pepper preparation roasted (actually steamed a bit first): toss the beans in olive oil, sprinkle with salt and maybe pepper. heat oven to 350°. these will need to be done early to have time for the tempeh to use the oven. they can be served room temp. we found it best to "steam" them for 20–30 minutes first by covering the trays of beans with foil; when almost soft enough to eat, remove the foil and roast for another ~10 minutes until slightly browning. or simple steamed: you may need to wash the steamer pans used for the tempeh to reuse for the beans. these can be done anytime and served either warm or room temp. steam the beans for ~20 minutes until they are as soft as you like them. be sure to check that the water doesn't all boil off.

title: Supper Bean Casserole Or Soup
text: all recipes / entree supper bean casserole or soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × improvise casseroles or soup out of leftover tortilla bar ingredients — the ingredients below are potential ingredients, use what we have and be creative. yield: casserole fills 2 2” full-sized hotel pans; soup aims for ~14–18 quarts, depending on the size, age, and appetite of the group equipment large mixing bowl 2 2” full-sized hotel pans with lids, or a 20 qt soup pot ingredients for casserole: leftover rice (and maybe quinoa and/or corn tortillas, torn up) — need only a thin layer of grain (maybe 3 qts total) leftover pinto beans (if less than 4 qts, open some cans of black beans to have this much) leftover veggies of any kind (add more frozen corn or frozen green beans to make at least 3 qts veggies) leftover salsa, or open another jar if needed to make it moist and tasty salt, pepper, ground cumin, garlic powder, etc., to spice up if needed (usually only needed if you used a lot of new plain ingredients) for soup: any/all of the above, but very light on the rice or quinoa and tortillas bouillon, to bring to a soup consistency more canned tomatoes, if needed (probably not needed) preparation casserole: layer the casseroles with a light layer of rice and tortillas on the bottom, then mix together the beans, veggies, and rest. a layer of torn-up tortillas works well as a topping (we don't put cheese on top anymore, only serve it on the side). soup: add all the beans and veg to the soup pot, thin with bouillon (1 tsp better than bouillon to 1 cup water), and thicken with a little rice or torn-up tortillas if wanted. serve either version with cheese and vegan cheese, and cilantro if we have enough.

title: Supper Black Bean Soup with Veg
text: all recipes / soup supper black bean soup with veg tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~16 quarts equipment largest soup pot (to stay warm) ingredients leftover black bean soup with corn and tomato canned tomatoes, as needed frozen corn, up to 5 packs (makes it interesting), as needed better than bouillon, as needed preparation add your leftovers to the soup pot. augment as needed to make ~16 quarts total. always put thick soups on a flame disperser and stir often but lightly if the bottom is getting burned — don't scrape it up. bring to a full boil (or 180°), turn off the fire, and put the lid on; the big pots will stay warm until 5:00. probably best to save any leftover chips for the final snack.

title: Supper Dal Soup or Casserole
text: all recipes / soup supper dal soup or casserole tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: soup ~15–16 quarts; casserole fills two 2” deep hotel pans at least half full (for ~48) equipment soup: largest 32 qt stock pot casserole: two 2” deep hotel pans ingredients soup: leftover curried cauliflower — what you have (if you made plain steamed, look at the curry recipe and add some of those spices and some frozen peas) ~4 qts leftover dal ~3 med cans tomatoes with juice 1 lg can coconut milk water + bouillon paste, as needed to make a total of ~15–16 qts of soup 1–2 qts leftover rice casserole (for ~48): leftover dal (~4–5 quarts; if less than this, add a can of white or garbanzo beans) leftover cauliflower and peas (add more frozen peas if short) 2 small cans coconut milk, to mix with the veggies leftover rice (~4–5 quarts; if short, make some more on the stove) 1–2 tsp curry powder, if you added a lot of new unseasoned stuff preparation soup: mix it all up, bring to a boil, taste, turn off, and cover — it should keep hot for the afternoon. serve with sides of leftover raita or yogurt, and leftover chutney or raisins. casserole: layer the food into the 2 pans: rice, veggies, dal. serve with sides of leftover raita or yogurt, and leftover chutney or raisins.

title: Supper Miso Soup
text: all recipes / soup supper miso soup tags: vegan, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings equipment 20 qt stock pot (or 32 qt, if the 20 qt will be used for noodles) ingredients 1 sheet kombu (if we have any) 10 sheet pack nori, cut into ~2” squares 3 lbs tofu, diced small (½”) (if no extra in fridge, use aseptic if any) 3.5 cups miso, ideally red or whatever we have (3.5 cups = ~1¾ tubs) ⅓ cup tamari 13 quarts water 3 lbs carrots, small dice 8 bunches chopped scallions, including ~⅔ of the green part 5 lbs mushrooms, thick slices (maybe pre-sautéed if time) preparation (in the morning) add all but 1 quart of the water, plus the kombu sheet, and simmer for about an hour; remove the kombu. add the nori, mushrooms, and carrots. mix the miso with another quart of water, and prep the scallions and tofu — put these in the fridge for later. (at 5:00) add in the tofu, tamari, and miso/water. (~5:25) just before serving, add the scallions.

title: Supper Moroccan Soup
text: all recipes / soup supper moroccan soup tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × extend leftover moroccan chickpea stew (and any leftover quinoa pilaf) into a soup. if there's almost nothing left to start with, see the recipe for moroccan red lentil soup in the simple soups file instead. yield: ~14–16 quarts equipment 2 soup warmers 32 qt stock pot ingredients leftover moroccan chickpea stew, and any leftover quinoa pilaf red lentils, up to ~6 cups, as needed water mixed with some bouillon paste, as needed more of the spices from the moroccan stew recipe, as needed greek or regular yogurt, for serving on the side preparation extend the leftovers to make ~14–16 quarts, adding red lentils, water mixed with bouillon paste, and more of the moroccan stew spices as needed. make the soup on the stove in the large stock pot. if it's thick and at 175° by lunchtime, it should stay warm all afternoon with the fire off and the lid on. if very watery, it might not — in that case, transfer it to soup warmers (under the toasters). set up a large bowl of greek or regular yogurt for a side.

title: Supper Peanut Casserole
text: all recipes / entree supper peanut casserole tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × the idea: improvise a casserole out of leftover african peanut stew, roasted cabbage (if any), and rice — use what we have and be creative with the ingredients below. yield: for ~48 servings, fills 2 2” hotel pans equipment 2 2” hotel pans with domed lids (on top of pan rack) ingredients min ~3–4 qts leftover rice (make some on the stovetop if not enough) min ~6–8 qts leftover african peanut stew (add some canned chickpeas if not enough) any leftover roasted cabbage (optional) preparation you may want to layer the casseroles with grain on the bottom, then the stew and cabbage, or mix it all up. fill the 2 pans evenly with the mix and cover them with domed lids, label them, and put them in the fridge. check that the serving signs list the ingredients you wind up using.

title: Supper Rata Minestrone Soup
text: all recipes / soup supper rata minestrone soup tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~18 quarts soup (using ~8 qts leftover ratatouille as a base) equipment 2nd largest stock pot (the one with the pasta insert?) soup warmers? ingredients leftover ratatouille and extras better than bouillon broth, as needed more canned tomatoes (1–2 28 oz cans?), as needed extra zucchini prepped for the ratatouille, if any on hand more garlic, as needed leftover white beans, and/or ~2 28 oz cans white beans or garbanzos frozen green beans (1–2 packs), optional more "italian" herbs from the ratatouille recipe, as needed gf pasta, if available (pre-make it, rinse, and cool it) parmesan and "white" vegan cheese, for serving on the side preparation casseroles: first, if andrea fella is teaching and there are leftovers for her, maybe make a medium glass bowl of leftover polenta plus her no-bell-pepper ratatouille for her to microwave (don't put it in the oven). if enough leftovers: make ~18 quarts of soup with the leftover ratatouille (hopefully ~8 qts left), adding better than bouillon broth and any/all of the ingredients above as needed. when hot: when it's done, or just before lunch, transfer to soup warmers for the afternoon. at 5:00pm: if prepared, add the pre-cooked and cooled gluten-free pasta. setup cheese: set up a bowl of parmesan and "white" vegan cheese on the side.

title: Supper Shepards Pie
text: all recipes / entree supper shepards pie tags: vegetarian, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment 2 2” deep full-sized hotel pans with lids ingredients leftover mashed potatoes leftover chicken-fried tofu leftover green beans leftover gravy optional: frozen or other leftover veggies, if needed optional: bouillon, if needed optional: rice optional: canned white beans, to supplement the tofu preparation if there isn't enough left to make something tasty, first check the freezer for suitable leftovers to use, or make a simple soup out of what we have (or run out and get ingredients for). spray the pans. layer "as you like it." simple suggestion: crumble the tofu and mix with the veggies and gravy, then top with mashed potatoes. option: make a smaller dish with no cheese, sprinkling maybe parmesan on top to give it some browning and more flavor.

title: Supper Tofu Spread
text: all recipes / side supper tofu spread tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × ingredients tofu, 6 lbs veganaise, 2 cups celery, fine dice, 4 cups turmeric, 2 t dijon mustard, ½ cup … more to taste tamari, ½ cup … more to taste nutritional yeast, 6 t parsley, 1 bunch dill and/or tarragon, 1 bunch each scallions, chopped, 3 bunches salt, 1 t (start with less, add more to taste) pepper, 1 t (start with less, add more to taste) cayenne, ½ t (start with less, add more to taste) corn cakes, 8 packs preparation crumble the tofu to the texture of crumbled eggs. chop the celery and scallions. wash and chop the parsley, dill, and tarragon. add the other ingredients and mix. taste for salt, pepper, and seasoning. refrigerate until serving time. serve with corn cakes in a towel-lined basket.

title: SW Black Bean Stew Soup
text: all recipes / soup sw black bean stew soup tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~50 servings, enough for 2 meals (or use the smaller quantities, ¼ less, for ~36 servings) equipment 32 qt (largest) stock pot, maybe a 2nd stock pot for excess mini cuisinart ingredients olive oil, as needed, for sauté 6 lbs (4.5 lbs for the smaller batch) chopped yellow onion, medium dice 12 stalks (9 stalks for the smaller batch) celery, small dice 2 6 lb cans (1 large + 2 medium cans for the smaller batch) tomatoes with liquid ½ cup (4.5 t for the smaller batch) cumin (either whole, lightly toasted and ground, or preground) ½ cup (4.5 t for the smaller batch) oregano 2 t (1¾ t for the smaller batch) paprika 1 t (¾ t for the smaller batch) chili powder 5 lbs (4 lbs for the smaller batch) green bell peppers, small dice 5 lbs (4 lbs for the smaller batch) mixed red/yellow/orange bell peppers, small dice 7 lbs (5–6 lbs for the smaller batch) zucchini, ½” dice (quartered — sixths if huge — lengthwise, then cut into ½” chunks) 5 28 oz cans (4 cans for the smaller batch) black beans (use the liquid) 4 bags (3 bags for the smaller batch) frozen corn 9 4 oz cans (7 4 oz cans for the smaller batch) hatch green chilies ~4–6 qts (~4.5 qts for the smaller batch) water, as needed (should be a fairly dense soup) preparation sauté: heat olive oil in the stock pot and add the onions. sauté until translucent. add ingredients: add the celery, chili powder, oregano, cumin, and paprika to the sauté mixture and cook for a few minutes. add the tomatoes, bring to a boil, and lower to a simmer. simmer for at least half an hour. add the peppers, zucchini, beans, and water as needed to make the quantity desired. bring to a boil, and simmer until time for the last step. consider separating out some into a smaller stock pot as a guarantee of leftovers, and because this gets very full. finish: add the corn and green chilies about 20 minutes before serving. add salt as needed. serve with cheddar, cilantro, and sour cream.

title: Tempeh Ruebens and Fixings
text: all recipes / entree tempeh ruebens and fixings tags: vegetarian, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment 2 large baking sheets for tempeh pitcher or bowl to mix sauce ingredients tempeh: 15 8oz packs tempeh, sliced 4 per pack (see km instructions, am yogi does this) — note: case = 12 packs, so case + 3 extra ¾ c light olive oil ¼ c sesame oil 2 c tamari 2 c rice vinegar 4 c water 3 packs swiss cheese, pieces cut in half sunshine burgers for no-soy people, optional (put out a sign pointing to the freezer, they can microwave them) fixings: rye bread — 3 loaves (= 60 slices, usually serves a full house); for a smaller group, figure ~1½ slices per wheat-eater gf bread — ~1½ slices per non-wheat eater 4 24oz jars sauerkraut, drained russian dressing (mix together): veganaise, 32 oz ketchup, 6 t horseradish, 2 t 1 jar dijon mustard 3 packs swiss cheese, sliced in half, arranged on a dinner plate ~6 bags chips (assuming 5oz terra chip bags) preparation note (10/2025): the steaming step was removed — experiments showed it's not needed. set-up and prep: preheat both ovens to 350°. slice each package in half across the center, then each half piece through the thickness dimension to make two thin patties. that is, if the half-piece is ~½" thick, the resulting patties will be ¼" thick rectangles. tip: maybe use 2 white scrapers to hold the piece safely on its side (the km will demonstrate, probably the morning yogi will do it). mix marinade & start on prepping sides: mix the marinade — lite olive oil, sesame oil, rice vinegar, tamari, and water. handy to use a large plastic pitcher. layout the slices flat on the baking sheets, not overlapping. pour the marinade over the slices. (~10:45) put the pans in the ovens. continue working on sides & the veg. (~11:15) after about half an hour, turn over all the tempehs. add water or more marinade if it is getting dry. we are now serving the cheese on the side, see "fixings" below. set-up sides: make the russian dressing (just mix the veganaise, ketchup, and horseradish — see ingredients list). set up sauerkraut (drain), mustard (serve in the jar), chips, and cheese. layout the rye bread on the large baking sheets, overlapping the pieces so it fits on maybe 1 full and 1 half-sized baking sheet. don't cover it so that it more toasts than steams. put it in about 11:30 and check it frequently.

title: Thai Yellow Curry W2
text: all recipes / entree thai yellow curry w2 tags: neither, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (or ~36 if not doing a supper leftover batch) equipment rondo 10-12 qt stockpot ingredients ¼ cup canola or coconut oil (as needed) 4 lbs (3 lbs for 36) onion, thinly sliced ½ cup (6 tbls for 36) ginger, minced 20 cloves (15 cloves for 36) garlic, minced ¾ cup (9 tbls for 36) thai curry paste (maeploy brand yellow is what we use) 2 t (1½ t for 36) turmeric mixed vegetables , ~30-35 lbs total (~23-28 lbs for 36), for example (but use whatever you have): 5 lbs (4 lbs for 36) yams, cubed 7 ea (5 ea for 36) cauliflower 7 ea (5-6 ea for 36) eggplant, cubed 6 lbs (5 lbs for 36) zucchini, cubed 5 lbs (3 lbs for 36) yukon potatoes note: avoid using bell peppers if andrea is teaching 9 lbs (7 lbs for 36) extra firm tofu, cut into ¾" cubes, cooked & served separately (see other recipe) 3 6-lb cans (2 large + 1 small for 36) coconut milk preparation ***note: this full recipe is enough for a full rondo plus ~8-10 qts in one of the smaller stockpots. it works to get down to the *** step below in the rondo, then separate out the 2 quantities and proportionally divide up any additional vegetables. then you can set aside the other pot to use for the leftover supper. pre-roast (eggplant & maybe others): if using eggplant, pre-roast it to lose bitterness & help it absorb sauce better. if there's room in the oven, it's tasty to pre-roast some other hard veggies like cauliflower, carrots, zucchini, yams (not broccoli). roast tofu: see separate recipe — we usually serve this separately, both for diets and for table interest. sauté spices: add oil to the rondo, heat to medium/high, and add onions; sauté until translucent. add garlic, ginger, curry paste, and turmeric, and cook for a minute or two until fragrant. taste the sauce & adjust spices if needed. add veggies: once onions and spice mix are ready, add coconut milk. try not to let it fully boil once you add the coconut — it will separate (still edible if it does, but not ideal). add veggies hardest first, tenderest last, something like: (~10:30) raw carrots, yams, squash, potatoes, peppers, zucchini, roasted eggplant (*** see above); (~11:40) raw cauliflower and/or other pre-roasted veggies; (~11:50) raw broccoli if having any. note from thina (for a possibly better version): use only 1 big coconut milk and maybe 2 small cans, plus 1 jar of better than bouillon. use 1 small can of coconut milk as the oil to melt the curry paste (don't worry about oil separating). then add all the hard veggies, including onions, and add the rest of the coconut milk and better than bouillon, then the rest of the softer veggies. she only roasted the eggplants, and you can use whatever veggies you wish. when the veggies are cooked, it's good to go!

title: Tortilla Bar Fixings
text: all recipes / side tortilla bar fixings tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment foil hotel pan ingredients 2½ lbs (~½ large pack) cheddar cheese, set up in a large bowl ~1 pack vegan cheddar cheese, set up in a small bowl 3 bunches cilantro, washed & chopped (use stems), 1 bowl is ok 2 large jars salsa (usually pace or kirkland), set up in 2 medium bowls ~80-100 corn tortillas (should be set up by yogi helper)

title: Vegan Cornbread
text: all recipes / side vegan cornbread tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48-50 servings equipment 4 half-sized 2" hotel pans (cooks more evenly than 2 full-size) 2 large mixing bowls 2 small mixing bowls ingredients 1⅓ cup vegan egg replacer (in pantry baking box) — note: bob's v-egg has soy, the "ener-g" box brand doesn't — or ground flax seed (in freezer) 4 cups warm water, for the flax or vegan egg 7½ cups rice milk (or alternative milk of choice, check allergies) ¾ cup + 1 t apple cider vinegar 10⅔ cups gluten-free flour 10⅔ cups bob's medium grind cornmeal (check pantries for ~32oz bags; can use polenta if none — the medium grind makes it lighter) 3 t + 1½ tsp salt ½ cup + 1½ t baking powder 4¾ tsp baking soda 2⅔ cups canola oil 2⅔ cups pumpkin pulp (canned/boxed) 2⅔ cups sweetener: maple syrup, honey, or sugar (check with km to accommodate any dietary restrictions) preparation heat oven to 375°. grease pans. mix v-egg or ground flax and warm water separately, and let set for 5-10 minutes to thicken (will need to whisk the v-egg). mix the alternative milk of choice and vinegar and let set while preparing the other ingredients. in a large mixing bowl, mix the dry ingredients: cornmeal, gf flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in one bowl. in a separate mixing bowl, mix together the oil, pumpkin, sweetener, "milk" mixture, and flax mixture. leave wets and drys separate until just ready to go in the oven. mix just until combined, being careful not to overmix. place mixture into 4 half-sized 2-inch-deep hotel pans (stored on the island near the pantry door). bake for 40-50 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked in the center. test by patting for firmness & checking that a toothpick or knife comes out clean. start checking after 30 minutes.

title: Vegan Ricotta
text: all recipes / side vegan ricotta tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × this vegan ricotta cheese tastes just as rich and creamy as the real thing! it's a delicious dairy-free, nut-free, and gluten-free substitute for the ricotta in lasagna, stuffed shells, and more. yield: 1x: about 2½ cups · 3x (full pan, generous): about 7½ cups equipment food processor ingredients 1x: 14 ounces · 3x: 3 lbs extra-firm tofu, drained 1x: 3 tablespoons · 3x: ½ cup + 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice 1x: 2 tablespoons · 3x: 6 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil 1x: 2 tablespoons · 3x: 6 tablespoons nutritional yeast 1x: 1 tablespoon · 3x: 3 tablespoons lemon zest 1x: 2 · 3x: 6 garlic cloves 1x: 1 teaspoon · 3x: 3 teaspoons sea salt 1x: ¼ teaspoon · 3x: ¾ teaspoon dried oregano 1x: ¼ teaspoon · 3x: amount not clearly specified in source ("? some") red pepper flakes preparation in a food processor, place the tofu, lemon juice, olive oil, nutritional yeast, lemon zest, garlic, salt, oregano, and red pepper flakes, and pulse until creamy. use in a vegetarian lasagna recipe or a stuffed shells recipe.

title: White Bean Side
text: all recipes / side white bean side tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × assume the kitchen manager soaked the dry beans; if not, either try the quick-soak method during veggie chop/first sit period, or use canned beans (or instant pot if you know how). this is meant to be offered as a vegan "condiment" to add to the ratatouille, then mix any leftovers into the supper casserole. yield: ~50 servings (or ~36 if not doing a leftover batch) equipment 12 or 16 qt stock pot ingredients 2.5 qts dry (1¾ qts dry for ~36) cannellini beans 4 fresh rosemary sprigs from the garden — 2 to cook with, 2 for garnish (same for both batch sizes) ~¼ cup olive oil 1 t (2 tsp for ~36) salt preparation for dry beans: (~9:30) start first thing — strain off the soaking water, cover with fresh water. toss in 2 rosemary stalks. bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer. cook until soft. strain into a serving bowl. remove rosemary, toss with olive oil. garnish with a fresh rosemary stalk. for canned beans: same as above, but only cook long enough to reheat — don't overcook. could start about 11:00. for instant pot (not tested): cover with water, add oil & rosemary. if pre-soaked, pressure cook on high for ~7 mins; if not, ~50 mins.

title: Red Pepper Dressing Notes from Max Swanger
text: all recipes / salad red pepper dressing notes from max swanger tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × informal dressing notes as dictated by max swanger. ingredients jarred roasted red peppers, drained (quantity as available — split into two batches) red wine vinegar (~¾ cup per batch) olive oil (~2¼ cups per batch — roughly a 1:3 vinegar-to-oil ratio) salt (start with ~1 tsp, to taste) black pepper (start with ~1 tsp, to taste) preparation put the roasted peppers in the vitamix (drained, split into two batches). add red wine vinegar and drizzle in the olive oil — usually about 1:3 vinegar to oil, e.g. try ~¾ cup vinegar to 2¼ cups oil per batch. should work. season to taste with salt and pepper, starting with about 1 tsp each. blend. you can probably put it all in at once and it will likely still emulsify.

title: Rosemary-Chocolate Chip Cookies
text: all recipes / dessert rosemary-chocolate chip cookies tags: vegan, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: 15 cookies ingredients ½ c refined coconut oil, softened (not melted) 2 t loosely packed fresh rosemary, chopped ⅓ c brown sugar ¼ c sugar ¼ c non-dairy mylk 1 t ground flaxseed 2 tsp vanilla 1⅓ c flour ½ tsp salt ½ tsp baking soda ½ c chocolate chips preparation heat oven to 350°. beat together coconut oil and rosemary, then add sugars and beat well. add mylk and flaxseed and beat again for 30 seconds or so. add about half of the flour and the remaining dry ingredients, and mix well. scoop about 2 t portions of cookie dough and gently flatten on a cookie sheet. bake 10-12 minutes until bottoms are golden brown.

title: Saag Paneer
text: all recipes / entree saag paneer tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × saag refers to an indian vegetable dish in which spinach or other dark greens are stewed with ginger, garlic, fresh chiles and spices until meltingly soft. as the name suggests, saag paneer includes paneer, a mild indian cheese that is firm enough to cook without melting. the heat of the serrano chiles balances the creamy richness, but for a milder dish, remove the seeds before mincing the chiles. the fresh greens are finely chopped before cooking, to help them break down faster into a silky gravy. thawed chopped frozen spinach can be used to save time, but make sure to drain well and squeeze out the excess liquid first. finish the dish with a little heavy cream (or plain yogurt) to lend body and richness. serve with steamed rice and/or indian flatbread (such as naan). any leftovers can be refrigerated for up to 2 days. yield: 4 servings ingredients 1 pound fresh baby spinach (about 8 packed cups) 2 tablespoons ghee 8 ounces paneer, cut into 1-by-½-inch pieces ½ cup finely chopped yellow onion kosher salt and black pepper 1 tablespoon freshly grated peeled ginger (from a 2-inch piece) 2 teaspoons grated garlic (from about 3 cloves) 1 serrano chile, stemmed and minced ½ teaspoon ground coriander ¼ teaspoon ground cumin ½ cup heavy cream steamed rice and/or indian flatbread, for serving preparation in a food processor, working in batches, pulse spinach until minced but not puréed. do not pack the spinach too tightly or it won't get evenly chopped. you should have about 3 packed cups of minced spinach. heat 1 tablespoon ghee over medium in a large nonstick skillet. when it shimmers, add paneer and cook, turning occasionally, until golden all over, 5 to 7 minutes. using tongs or a fish spatula, transfer cheese to a plate, leaving as much ghee as possible in the skillet. reduce heat to medium-low, add the remaining 1 tablespoon ghee and the onion, and season with salt and pepper. cook, stirring occasionally, until softened but not browned, about 5 minutes. add ginger, garlic and chile, and cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant and well incorporated, 1 minute. stir in coriander and cumin until well blended. add minced spinach and ½ cup water, and increase the heat to medium. season with salt and pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until spinach is completely soft and most of the liquid is absorbed, about 8 minutes. stir in heavy cream and paneer until well incorporated. season with salt and pepper. transfer to a serving bowl. divide rice and/or flatbread among 4 shallow bowls or plates. pass the saag paneer to spoon on top.

title: Salad Dressings(1)
text: all recipes / salad salad dressings(1) tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × balsamic salad dressing yield: ~1.5 qts (enough for a full house of 44 for one meal), or ~3 qts for 2 meals ingredients 1¾ cups (3½ cups for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) balsamic vinegar 6 (12 for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) cloves peeled garlic ½ cup (1 cup for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) water 1 t (2 t for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) dijon mustard 1 t (2 t for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) sherry vinegar ¾ t (1½ t for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) black pepper 1½ t (2½ t for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) salt (add gradually and taste) 1½ t (2½ t for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) sugar (add gradually and taste) 3½ cups (7 cups for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) olive oil preparation poach the whole peeled garlic cloves in one cup of the oil (one cup out of the amount called for) in a small saucepan or skillet on medium heat for ~5 minutes to make them more mild. add everything except the rest of the oil to the blender (poached garlic cloves and their oil can be added unchopped). blend. if there's room in the vitamix, drizzle in the oil as you keep blending; if not, transfer to a larger container and whisk in the oil. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper, or other seasonings. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with the smallest ladles. herb vinaigrette (also used for "tarragon" in menus) yield: ~1½ qts, or ~3 qts for 2 meals ingredients 2 cups (4 cups for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) rice vinegar ¼ cup (½ cup for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) honey ¼ cup (½ cup for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) dijon mustard 6 (12 for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) cloves garlic 1 cup (2 cups for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) fresh herbs (two versions used: ½ basil/½ parsley, or all tarragon; note: for a quick basic vinaigrette, instead of fresh herbs, gradually add ~1-2 t of any mix of dried herbs — e.g. parsley, basil, tarragon, thyme, dried onion — to taste) 4 cups (8 cups for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) canola oil salt to taste preparation rinse the herbs and pick the leaves off the stems. poach the whole peeled garlic cloves in one cup of the oil (one cup out of the amount called for) in a small saucepan or skillet on medium heat for ~5 minutes to make them more mild. add everything except the rest of the oil to the blender (poached garlic cloves and their oil can be added unchopped). blend. if there's room in the vitamix, drizzle in the oil as you keep blending; if not, transfer to a larger container and whisk in the oil. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper, or other seasonings. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with the smallest ladles. orange ginger salad dressing yield: ~1.5 qts ingredients ~1 t zest of 2 limes ~2 t zest of 2 oranges ~1-2 t juice of the 2 limes 3 cups juice of about 4 oranges, topped off with apple cider vinegar 2 t chopped ginger (about a 2" piece — coarse-chop it and let the vitamix chop it fine with the rest) 1½ t ground cumin (pre-ground is fine) 1 cup olive oil 2½ cups canola oil preparation using a microplane zester or box grater, scrape off just the colored layer of rind from the limes and oranges, trying not to get much of the white pith (it's more bitter). be careful with your fingers and knuckles — this tool is very sharp! using the electric juicer, juice the limes and oranges. add everything except the oil to the blender. blend. if there's room in the vitamix, drizzle in the oil as you keep blending; if not, transfer to a larger container and whisk in the oil. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper, or other seasonings. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with the smallest ladles. artichoke salad dressing yield: ~1.5 qts (double all ingredients for ~3 qts) ingredients 1 cup white wine vinegar (or rice vinegar) 25 oz marinated artichoke hearts (probably fine to add a whole 33oz jar — blend and see) 2 t tamari (omit if no-soy people are on the retreat; probably need more salt at the end) 1 t dijon mustard ½ t honey 1 t white pepper (or more, to taste) 2.5 cups canola or other non-olive oil 1 cup olive oil salt to taste preparation add everything except the oil to the blender. blend. if there's room in the vitamix, drizzle in the oil as you keep blending; if not, transfer to a larger container and whisk in the oil. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper, or other seasonings. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with the smallest ladles. greek lemon salad dressing yield: ~1.5 qts ingredients 1½ cups rice vinegar ½ t lemon zest ½ cup lemon juice (~4 lemons) ¼ cup honey 2 t dijon mustard 6 cloves garlic 1 t oregano 2 cups olive oil 2 cups canola oil preparation using a microplane zester or box grater, scrape off just the colored layer of rind from a lemon, trying not to get much of the white pith (it's more bitter). be careful with your fingers and knuckles — this tool is very sharp! using the electric juicer, juice the lemons. add everything except the oil to the blender. blend. if there's room in the vitamix, drizzle in the oil as you keep blending; if not, transfer to a larger container and whisk in the oil. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper, or other seasonings. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with the smallest ladles. lemon tahini salad dressing yield: ~1.5 qts ingredients 2½ cups tahini 1 cup lemon juice (about 4 fresh lemons) 2½ cups water 5 cloves garlic ¾ cup parsley 1½ t tamari (omit for no-soy yogis, and probably use more salt) 2 t ground cumin 1 t white pepper (start with half and add to taste) maybe more salt or tamari, to taste preparation using the electric juicer, juice at least 4 fresh lemons. wash the parsley and cut off the stems (fine to keep some of the upper stems). add all ingredients to the blender and blend. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper, or other seasonings. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with the smallest ladles. hollyhock yield: ~1.5 qts, or ~3 qts ingredients 1 cup (2 cups for a 3qt batch) nutritional yeast ½ cup + 2 t (1⅓ cup for a 3qt batch) water ½ cup + 2 t (1⅓ cup for a 3qt batch) tamari ½ cup + 2 t (1⅓ cup for a 3qt batch) apple cider vinegar 6 cloves (12 cloves for a 3qt batch) garlic 3 cups (6 cups for a 3qt batch) canola or other non-olive oil preparation add everything except the oil to the blender. blend. if there's room in the vitamix, drizzle in the oil as you keep blending; if not, transfer to a larger container and whisk in the oil. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper, or other seasonings. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with the smallest ladles. honey mustard yield: ~1.5 qts, or ~3 qts for 2 meals ingredients 1¼ cups (2½ cups for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) apple cider vinegar ½ cup + 2 t (1¼ cups for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) dijon mustard ½ cup + 2 t (1¼ cups for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) honey (hint: coat the cup with oil first, honey slides right out) 3½ cups (7 cups for a 3-qt/2-meal batch) canola oil preparation add everything except the oil to the blender. blend. if there's room in the vitamix, drizzle in the oil as you keep blending; if not, transfer to a larger container and whisk in the oil. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper, or other seasonings. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with the smallest ladles. creamy avocado yield: ~1.5 qts ingredients 2½ cups canola oil 1 cup lime/lemon juice 1 cup yogurt 2 avocados ⅓ cup cilantro 1-2 garlic cloves ½ tsp cumin ½ tsp white pepper salt, to taste sugar, if needed, to taste preparation add everything except the oil to the blender. blend. if there's room in the vitamix, drizzle in the oil as you keep blending; if not, transfer to a larger container and whisk in the oil. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper, or other seasonings. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with the smallest ladles. ginger miso yield: ~1.5 qts+, or ~3 qts+ ingredients ½ cup (1 cup for a 3qt+ batch) red wine vinegar (or rice vinegar) ½ cup (1 cup for a 3qt+ batch) tamari ½ cup (1 cup for a 3qt+ batch) honey ½ cup finely diced medium onion ¾ cup (1½ cups for a 3qt+ batch) miso ¼ cup (½ cup for a 3qt+ batch) grated ginger 4 cups (8 cups for a 3qt+ batch) safflower oil 1 t (2 t for a 3qt+ batch) toasted sesame oil (to taste) preparation add everything except the oil to the blender. blend. if there's room in the vitamix, drizzle in the oil as you keep blending; if not, transfer to a larger container and whisk in the oil. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust seasonings. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with the smallest ladles.
