title: Salad to go with Thai Cauliflower Soup
text: all recipes / salad salad to go with thai cauliflower soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × option for the first full day's supper, instead of a greek salad bar. ingredients 1 red cabbage (or ~½ of a large one), shredded or manually thinly sliced 1 napa cabbage, thinly sliced 2 lbs frozen green beans, steamed until thawed 2 cups chopped mint leaves (either bought or from the garden outside the kitchen door) ~2 cups shredded carrots optional: mung bean sprouts (the fat white kind), if we bought some optional: extra bell peppers, if we bought some (make sure to leave 15 for the ratatouille meal) baby kale, enough to fill the medium salad bowl sides: 2 bunches cilantro, 2 lbs peanuts peanut lime dressing: 2¼ cups peanut butter 2 cups water (more if needed, if too thick) 1¾ cups lime juice (10-12 limes) & zest of 4 limes (ok to top off with lemon juice if you can't get enough lime juice from the limes) ¾ cup rice vinegar 3 t sesame oil ½ cup agave (maybe more, taste at the end) ½ cup tamari (maybe less if not low-sodium) 6 cloves garlic (the vitamix will mince it) 1 t roughly chopped ginger (the vitamix will mince it) 1½ cups light olive oil preparation mix the cabbages, green beans, mint, carrots, and any optional sprouts/peppers with enough baby kale to fill the medium salad bowl. maybe mix it in the giant bowl and serve in the medium one. make 1 batch of peanut lime dressing (below), set up in 2 small pitchers. set up and serve as sides: 2 bunches cilantro, 2 lbs peanuts. for the peanut lime dressing: mix the peanut butter & water in a bowl to thin it. add that and everything except the oil to the vitamix; mix. drizzle in the oil while mixing.

title: Salted Choc Chip Cookies Vegan GF
text: all recipes / dessert salted choc chip cookies vegan gf tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × note: for best texture, make the dough the day before and fridge overnight. yield: approximately 60 cookies at this batch size (18 cookies at the original 1x recipe size — this batch is scaled 3.5x; usually get 5x6 per sheet on 2 large baking sheets = 60) ingredients 7 cups (2 cups at 1x) bob's (or trader joe's) 1-to-1 gf flour, preferred brand 3½ tsp (1 tsp at 1x) baking powder 2½ tsp (¾ tsp at 1x) baking soda 1¾ tsp (½ tsp at 1x) salt 4¼ cups (1¼ cups at 1x) dark chocolate chips (= 2 bags at this batch size; more is fine too) 1¾ cups (½ cup at 1x) sugar 1¾ cups (½ cup at 1x) packed light brown sugar 2 cups (½ cup + 1 t at 1x) canola or lite olive oil 1 cup + ½ t (¼ cup + 1 t at 1x) water sea salt, for garnish preparation in a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. add the chocolate chips to the flour mixture and toss to coat. in a separate large bowl, whisk (best with an electric hand mixer) the sugars briskly with the oil and water until smooth and incorporated, about 2 minutes. note: use fresh, soft light brown sugar; if there are clumps, break them up with the back of a spoon or your hand before whisking. add the flour mixture to the sugar mixture, then stir with a wooden spoon or rubber spatula until just combined and no flour is visible. do not overmix. cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate the dough for at least 12 hours and up to a day or two. preheat the oven to 350°. line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment paper. remove the dough from the refrigerator and use clean bare or gloved hands to portion it into 2-inch mounds. size guide: aim for 8x5 = 40 per full-sized sheet pan, or 4x5 = 20 per half pan. partially flatten each ball with fingers or a fork (they don't spread out much at all). tip: use a white plastic scraper to make clear rows between cookies. sprinkle the dough balls very lightly with coarse-grained sea salt, and bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the edges are golden. best to use only the top rack of the oven, or watch the bottom rack very carefully — it burns easily. check starting at about 12 minutes, since ovens vary. let cool completely before lifting off the pans to serve. from vogue.com. excerpted from ovenly by agatha kulaga and erin patinkin (harlequin). copyright © 2014. photographs by winona barton-ballentine. variations: this dough is versatile and easy to work with — try adding fresh herbs or spices, substituting flavored oils, or dressing them up with buttercream sandwiched between two cookies. a few favorites: substitute the chocolate chips with flaked coconut and toasted almonds, and add ¼ teaspoon almond extract to the oil/water mixture. instead of canola oil, use half hazelnut oil and half safflower oil, and use dark chocolate pieces instead of chocolate chips. mix one tablespoon of ground cinnamon into the flour mixture, and add milk chocolate chips and currants. prepare your favorite buttercream recipe and add in ¼ cup bourbon (or even champagne); mix until smooth and sandwich between two cookies to make cookie sandwiches.

title: Sesame Ginger Dressing
text: all recipes / salad sesame ginger dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: for a pre-tossed salad, ~48 servings (double the quantities for a self-serve dressing). as a pre-tossed salad, use on either the supper noodle or rice dish, or a slaw. equipment vitamix bowl ingredients 1¼ cups lime juice + zest of 2-3 limes, or rice vinegar, or a mixture 1 tbls grated ginger (good to use the microplane) ½ cup ginger, chopped in mini-cuisinart 6 tbls tamari 3 tbls agave 3 tbls sesame oil 6 cloves garlic, minced in mini-cuisinart, or 1½ tsp garlic powder 2 tbls sriracha sauce ¼ cup toasted white sesame seeds (& more in the salad, see above) ½ to 1 tbls salt (add ½ t and see... probably need more in the final salad) 2 cups light olive oil preparation blend all but the oil in the vitamix. drizzle in the oil & blend again.

title: Sherry Shallot Vinaigrette FOG
text: all recipes / salad sherry shallot vinaigrette fog tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~1.5 qts ingredients 1½ cups sherry vinegar 12 shallots 1 t dijon mustard 2¼ cups olive oil 2¼ cups canola oil 1 t salt ½ t white pepper preparation thinly slice the shallots. sauté the shallots in some of the olive oil. put the vinegar, mustard, and seasonings in the blender and blend. add the shallots with their oil and just pulse it a couple of times (we don't want the shallots totally liquified). transfer to a larger container and whisk in the rest of the oils. taste (drizzle a little into a separate spoon) and adjust salt, pepper, or mustard. for one meal: fill 2 small pitchers. serve with the smallest ladles.

title: Sherry Shallot Vinaigrette Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad sherry shallot vinaigrette salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: 1 batch (~48 servings) equipment vitamix ~4 qt plastic container & whisk 2 pitchers ingredients 1½ cups sherry vinegar 2 very large shallots (like small onions — check the onion area if we have any) 2 t dijon mustard 2¼ cups olive oil 2¼ cups light olive oil 1 tsp salt ½ tsp white pepper preparation remove the outer papery skin & thinly slice the shallots. sauté the shallots in some of the olive oil. put the vinegar, mustard, and seasonings in the blender and blend. drizzle the rest of the oil into the running vitamix and blend well. add the shallots with their oil and just pulse it a couple of times (we don't want the shallots totally liquified). taste and adjust salt & pepper if needed. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover & store in the fridge (if not for today, label and date also).

title: Simple Miso Soup
text: all recipes / soup simple miso soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × maybe offer on the last night with noodle salad. from rachel. ingredients 15 sheets nori, cut in large squares 3.5 cups miso 3.5 cups cubed tofu 7 cups chopped scallions preparation heat 15 quarts of water to a low simmer. add 15 sheets of nori cut into large squares. simmer for 5 minutes. add 3.5 cups of white miso (blended with some hot water to avoid clumping). add 3.5 cups of extra firm tofu. (i used the silken tofu from the yogi fridge, so there should have been 11 left in the main fridge for the next retreat.) simmer for another 5 minutes. before serving, add finely chopped scallions. the recipe says 7 cups; i used what we had left from the produce order, which was probably about half that.

title: Smoked Paprika Dressing
text: all recipes / salad smoked paprika dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (1 batch) equipment vitamix juicer 2 pitchers ingredients 2 ½ cups red wine vinegar 1 cup agave ¼ cup dijon mustard ¼ cup lime juice 2 t smoked paprika 2 t oregano 2 cloves garlic ½ cup chopped shallot 3 cups olive oil 1 t pepper 1 t salt preparation juice limes in the juicer next to the rice cooker. add all ingredients except the oil to the vitamix container and mix on low. drizzle the oil into the vitamix while mixing. gradually increase speed until fully emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. cover and store in the fridge (if not for today, label and date it too).

title: Spiced Chickpea Stew Turmeric Coconut
text: all recipes / entree spiced chickpea stew turmeric coconut tags: vegetarian, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × spiced chickpeas are crisped in olive oil, then simmered in a garlicky coconut milk for an insanely creamy, basically-good-for-you stew that evokes stews found in south india and parts of the caribbean. while the chickpeas alone would be good as a side dish, they are further simmered with stock, bolstered with dark, leafy greens of your choosing, and finished with a handful of fresh mint. when shopping, be sure to avoid low-fat coconut milk, coconut milk meant for drinking, or cream of coconut — all are very different and would not be suitable here. (by alison roman, nyt cooking.) yield: 4 to 6 servings as originally written. kitchen notes on this copy say there was very little left over for 48 people, and suggest scaling up 8–9x for a retreat batch (~32–48 servings) — with a bit more chickpeas and broth, and optionally picking up 2 quarts of greek yogurt for serving. ingredients ¼ cup olive oil, plus more for serving 4 garlic cloves, chopped 1 large yellow onion, chopped 1 (2-inch) piece ginger, finely chopped kosher salt and black pepper 1½ teaspoons ground turmeric, plus more for serving 1 teaspoon red-pepper flakes, plus more for serving 2 (15-ounce) cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed 2 (15-ounce) cans full-fat coconut milk 2 cups vegetable or chicken stock 1 bunch swiss chard, kale, or collard greens, stems removed, torn into bite-size pieces 1 cup mint leaves, for serving yogurt, for serving (optional) toasted pita, lavash, or other flatbread, for serving (optional) preparation heat ¼ cup oil in a large pot over medium heat. add garlic, onion, and ginger. season with salt and pepper, and cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is translucent and starts to brown a little at the edges, 3 to 5 minutes. add 1½ teaspoons turmeric, 1 teaspoon red-pepper flakes, and the chickpeas, and season with salt and pepper. cook, stirring frequently, so the chickpeas sizzle and fry a bit in the spices and oil, until they've started to break down and get a little browned and crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. remove about a cup of chickpeas and set aside for garnish. using a wooden spoon or spatula, further crush the remaining chickpeas slightly to release their starchy insides (this helps thicken the stew). add the coconut milk and stock, and season with salt and pepper. bring to a simmer, scraping up any bits that have formed on the bottom of the pot. cook, stirring occasionally, until the stew has thickened, 30 to 35 minutes. taste a chickpea or two, not just the liquid, to make sure they've simmered long enough. if you want the stew thicker after 30 to 35 minutes, keep simmering until you've reached your desired consistency. add the greens and stir, making sure they're submerged in the liquid. cook until they wilt and soften, 3 to 7 minutes depending on what you're using (swiss chard and spinach wilt much faster than kale or collard greens). season again with salt and pepper. divide among bowls and top with mint, the reserved chickpeas, a sprinkle of red-pepper flakes, and a good drizzle of olive oil. serve alongside yogurt and toasted pita if using; dust the yogurt with turmeric if you'd like.

title: Spinach Mushroom Lasagna
text: all recipes / entree spinach mushroom lasagna tags: vegetarian, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (2 hotel pans, ~24 servings each), plus a smaller 8x8 pan (~6–7 servings) for the no-dairy, gluten-free alt version equipment 2 hotel pans (~24 servings each, cut 6x4) 1 8x8 pan for the no-dairy, gf alt version ingredients 5 lbs (half case) mushrooms, cut chunky 4 lbs onions, medium dice 20cl garlic, chopped in chopper as needed, bottled pasta sauce (note how much we use) — enough to make 8 qts sauce (3 cups reserved for the alt version) 10 x 10oz frozen spinach bags (2 bags reserved for the alt version) 5 x 32oz ricotta 4 tubs trader joe's goat cheese (= 2 cups) 8 eggs, beaten 2 t nutmeg 4 cups bread crumbs (2 cups for topping, maybe 2 cups for the cheese mix) 8 cups shredded mozzarella 4 cups parmesan for alt version: soy cheese (maybe) 2 lemons 1 t nutmeg 1 box gf noodles 3 lbs firm tofu (will reuse some of the sauce & spinach reserved above) preparation be sure the spinach is out to thaw early. sauté onions, garlic, and mushrooms with 2 tsp salt. cook until the liquid is mostly gone. mix with bottled pasta sauce to total about 7.5 qts (put the mushroom mix in an 8 qt container and add sauce to fill). note: may want to use some plain pasta sauce for the bottom layers. strain and press the spinach (maybe with gloves, wring it out). set aside 1 cup for the alt version. make cheese mix: ricotta + goat cheese + nutmeg + beaten eggs + squeezed-dry spinach; maybe add 1-2 cups breadcrumbs (leave 2 cups total for the topping). make alt filling: blend tofu, lemon juice, and nutmeg, then mix with spinach. mix 4 cups parmesan, 2 cups mozzarella, and 2 cups bread crumbs for the topping. preboil the gf noodles? maybe set up a ramekin of cheese and sauce for the no-soy, no-gluten person. layers for 1 hotel pan (consider using a 4" deep pan just to avoid spillover): 2 cups sauce (maybe plain, without chunky mushrooms), 7½ sheets tj's lasagna noodles, 5 cups cheese/spinach mix, 3 cups sauce, 3 cups mozzarella, 7½ sheets tj's lasagna noodles, 5 cups cheese/spinach mix, 3 cups sauce, 7½ sheets tj's lasagna noodles, 3 cups sauce, and topping (~4 cups per pan). layers for alt version (need 6-7 servings?): ½ cup sauce, sheets of gf noodles, ½ the alt filling, 1 cup sauce, a soy cheese layer(?), more noodles, the remaining ½ alt filling, 1 cup sauce, another soy cheese layer(?).

title: Split Pea Soup
text: all recipes / soup split pea soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48-52 servings equipment largest 32 qt soup pot ingredients olive oil, for sauté 8 cups onions, chopped 7 cups celery, diced (~½" dice) 9 cups carrots, diced (~½" dice) 2 tsp salt 4 bay leaves 1½ t smoked paprika (maybe more later, but start easy on this) 3 t marjoram 3 t turmeric 2 t ground cumin ¾ tsp cayenne pepper (maybe more later, but start easy on this) 12 cups yellow or green split peas, rinsed 11 quarts water (mixed with a jar of better than bouillon) 1¼ cup lemon juice 1 bunch parsley, chopped preparation sauté: sauté onions over medium heat until softened. add carrots and celery, and sauté over medium heat (~30 mins). add turmeric, cayenne, marjoram, smoked paprika, and salt. sauté ~5 more minutes. mix 2 qts hot water (use tea water) with a jar of better than bouillon vegan "chicken" broth. add the peas, the bouillon mix, and the other 9 qts of water. bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. simmer an hour or more until the peas are soft and creamy. taste and adjust seasonings as needed. if needed, puree partially with an immersion blender (leave some chunks of carrot and celery). around 12:00: leave the soup at ~180°f with the burner turned off — it should stay hot. finish (~5:15): stir in the lemon juice and parsley, and adjust seasonings (especially — probably add more salt). adapted from vegetarian times, december 2013.

title: Steamed Broccoli
text: all recipes / side steamed broccoli tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × you may need to wash the steamer pans used for the tempeh to reuse for the broccoli, or the veggie choppers may have set it up already. we're doing a whole case, so you may need to do 2 rounds — it can all be finished a bit early, anytime from 11:30 onward or so, and served room temperature if needed. equipment 2 6" hotel pans 2 steamer pans 2 lids ingredients 1 case broccoli preparation setup two steamer assemblies: get the two 6" deep (deepest) solid pans and fill them with 2" of water. set the water-filled pans across 2 burners each. divide as much broccoli as will fit (with the lid fully closing) between the 2 perforated pans. set the perforated pans into the water-filled pans and put a lid on each. turn on both burners. let the broccoli steam for about 5 minutes after the water comes to a boil, then carefully lift the lid and check on it. when it looks done, remove the perforated pans from the base pans and empty the broccoli into a large metal serving bowl. refill one or both pans with any remaining broccoli and steam for just 2-3 minutes (some of this may be used for further baking, so leave it barely done). leave the pans on the counter (out of the water) so more can be served if needed.

title: Artichoke Hummus
text: all recipes / side artichoke hummus tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~16 cups (for a supper with leftovers), or ~8 cups (typical last-day snack only, blue bowl) equipment large bowl robo coupe large ceramic serving bowl leftover container if making the double (16-cup) size ingredients artichoke hearts, drained: 2 large (~48oz) jars for 16 cups, or 1 large (48oz) jar for 8 cups — maybe save 2-3 small pieces for garnish lemon juice: 1 cup (~8 lemons) for 16 cups, or ½ cup (~4 lemons) for 8 cups water: 2 cups for 16 cups, or 1 cup for 8 cups tahini: 1½ cups for 16 cups, or ¾ cup for 8 cups ev olive oil: 1 cup for 16 cups, or ½ cup for 8 cups cans of chickpeas: 4 x 28oz for 16 cups, or 2 x 28oz for 8 cups garlic: 16 cloves for 16 cups, or 8 cloves for 8 cups cayenne: ½ tsp for 16 cups, or ¼ tsp for 8 cups salt to taste: ~4-6 tsp for 16 cups, or ~2-3 tsp for 8 cups for garnish, as needed: artichoke pieces, parsley, or nasturtium preparation you will need to make this in 2 batches (for 8 cups) or 4 batches (for 16 cups) to fit in the robo coupe, so add some of each ingredient to each batch as you go, then hand-mix the batches together. assemble the robo coupe with the clear bowl and blade, adding roughly proportional parts of each ingredient to each batch. blend using pulse at first, then leave it running for a full minute or so to get a smooth consistency. mix all the batches together. serve in a large ceramic bowl with garnish.

title: Beans, greens and mushrrom soup
text: all recipes / soup beans, greens and mushrrom soup tags: vegetarian source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings equipment largest pot ingredients leftover bean dish from the previous day 10-12 quarts veggie broth herbs? (unspecified) additions? (unspecified) preparation empty the ingredients into a large pot and bring to a boil. place into soup warmers and keep at 165°f until dinner.

title: Black Bean Soup Supper
text: all recipes / soup black bean soup supper tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~16 qts (or less if lots of 8 precepts) equipment largest soup pot (to stay warm) ingredients leftover black bean soup with corn & tomato canned tomatoes, as needed frozen corn, up to 5 packs (makes it interesting) better than bouillon, as needed sour cream, for serving cheddar cheese, for serving cilantro, for serving preparation add your leftovers to the soup pot. augment as needed to reach ~16 qts (or less if lots of 8 precepts) by adding canned tomatoes, frozen corn (up to 5 packs), and better than bouillon. always put thick soups on a flame disperser and stir often but lightly if the bottom is getting burned — don't scrape it up. bring to a full boil (or 180°f), turn off the fire, and put the lid on — the big pots will stay warm until 5:00. do not serve with chips — they are reserved for other meals. sides: set up whatever's available of sour cream, cheddar cheese, and cilantro.

title: Butternut Soup
text: all recipes / soup butternut soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (or ~36 for the smaller batch) equipment ~20 qt soup pot (largest is ideal, but it's probably being used for lunch) ingredients leftover roasted butternut squash, peeled — however much you have pre-cubed butternut squash: 15-20 lbs (or 12-15 lbs for 36) — whatever was ordered white or gold potatoes, cubed: ~4 lbs (or 3 lbs for 36) olive oil, for sauté onions, chopped: 3 lbs (or 2¼ lbs for 36) garlic, chopped: 10 cloves (or 8 cloves for 36) better than bouillon vegan chicken broth: 1 jar in ~8 qts water (or ¾ jar in ~6 qts water for 36) — mix up and add as needed to reach the desired amount of soup (maybe 14 qts, or 11 qts for the smaller batch) dried thyme: 3 tbls (or 2½ tbls for 36) chopped parsley: 1 cup (or ¾ cup for 36) lemon juice & zest, to taste: 2 lemons (or 1½ lemons for 36) black pepper, to taste: 2 tsp (or 1½ tsp for 36) salt, to taste (probably need more!): 2 tsp (or 1½ tsp for 36) preparation sauté: sauté onions until transparent, then add garlic and cook briefly. simmer: add the butternut squash, potatoes, thyme, and stock; bring to a boil and reduce to a simmer. when partly done, add the parsley. finish: add lemon, salt, and pepper to taste. about noon: cover and turn off the fire. test that it is 165°f — it should hold at ~145-165°f until supper. check it again at 5:00 and reheat if needed, or transfer to the soup warmers and keep those on low all afternoon.

title: Carrot Ginger Soup
text: all recipes / soup carrot ginger soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings ingredients ½ cup olive oil 4 cups onions, chopped 15 lbs carrot 1 large can coconut milk 6-8 quarts vegetable broth 4-6 inches ginger, minced in cuisinart (more if desired) preparation sauté onions: in a large pot, sauté onions in olive oil until tender. add remaining ingredients, bring to a boil, then down to a simmer, and cook until the butternut squash is easily pierced with a fork, 20-30 minutes. emulsify: using an immersion blender, blend until smooth. season with salt and pepper.

title: Cauliflower Soup
text: all recipes / soup cauliflower soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × this is usually prepped on opening day but served at first-full-day supper. best idea is to get it all prepped on opening day, then cook it on opening day when the big 32 qt pot is available — it will keep hot all afternoon. note: there are 2 flavors of this — original (rather plain) and thai. we usually serve the original with a spinach/greek salad bar and the thai with a slaw (see those recipes), though we rarely do the thai/slaw version now since we don't usually have the extra ingredients unless pre-arranged with the produce orderer. yield: ~48 servings ingredients 1 case minus 2 heads cauliflower, cut into pieces (save the extra 2 heads for the dal day later in the week) — use 8 large or 10 medium heads, depending on how many are in a case 4 lbs yellow potatoes, cubed (optional if you don't have them) 18 cloves garlic (chopped in the mini cuisinart) 4 lbs onions, chopped 8 quarts water 1 jar veggie bouillon do one or the other of these: for original: 2 lemons, zest of one and juice of one (maybe more) 3 tbls dijon mustard ½ bunch parsley ½ cup olive oil for thai version (check we have the extra ingredients): 1 cup chopped ginger (chopped in the mini-cuisinart; leave 1 lb for later) ⅓ cup thai yellow curry paste (mae ploy tub — look in top of kitchen fridge for an open one, or the pantry for a new one) 4 limes, juice and zest (optional if you don't have them; leave ¼ for later) 3 bunches cilantro, roughly chopped including stems (served on the side) preparation sauté: sauté onions until soft, add garlic, and sauté a minute or so with ~2 tsp salt. if doing the thai version, add the ginger here. add the cauliflower, (potatoes), water, and bouillon, and cook until tender. season with salt and pepper to taste. finish: blend with an immersion blender, then finish with the rest of the flavors of your choice (original or thai, above). set up the cilantro as a side.

title: Leftover Lentil Salad
text: all recipes / salad leftover lentil salad tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings (about 16 cups of leftovers) equipment large bowl ingredients leftover lentil grape salad (consider making a no-nut supper version if you have a no-nut version of the leftovers) leftover roasted yams, beets, carrots leftover quinoa spinach kalamata olives pumpkin seeds tomatoes feta cheese cucumbers (maybe) dressing, whatever is left — greek lemon or balsamic are good preparation serve the leftovers (lentil grape salad, roasted yams/beets/carrots, quinoa) combined or separately, however you like. set up elements of the greek salad bar from week 1 day 1: spinach, kalamata olives, pumpkin seeds, tomatoes, feta cheese, and maybe cucumbers. probably skip the chickpeas if you have lentil salad left. serve with whatever dressing is left — greek lemon or balsamic are good.

title: Loaded Nachos
text: all recipes / entree loaded nachos tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~50 servings (or ~36) — typically 2 large sheets dairy + ½ sheet vegan for 50, or 1½ sheets dairy + ½ sheet vegan for 36 equipment 2 large baking sheets 1 half-sheet, for the no-cheese version ingredients tortilla chips: 1½ bags for 50 (or 1 bag for 36) — costco's giant 48-serving bags canned black beans, or leftover burgers etc.: 6 qts for 50 (or 4 qts for 36) shredded cheddar, or vegan cheddar (1 bag): ~2.5 lbs for 50 (or ~2 lbs for 36) sliced black olives, strained (= 1 red bag of costco): ~2 qts for 50 (or 1½ qts for 36) green chilies, strained: 8 small cans for 50 (or 6 small cans for 36) salsa (no need to open early, just set out jars): ~2 jars for 50 (or ~1½ jars for 36) scallions, chopped: 8 bunches for 50 (or 6 bunches for 36) bottled jalapenos, as a side if available (optional): 1 jar sour cream, as a side: 2 pints preparation (during the morning we just get ready — the dish is assembled at 5:00) set up for later use (storage containers are fine, don't need to be pretty): beans, cheddar, black olives, green chilies, scallions. set up nicely for serving on the side: jalapenos, sour cream. (at 3:50, km) set up pans with a thick layer of chips; stage the rest of the ingredients nearby. (at 5:00, km) turn both ovens on to 400°f. sprinkle the chips with beans, scallions, olives, chilies, salsa, and cheese. (~5:15) put into the hot ovens for ~10-15 minutes, until warm and the cheese is melted.

title: Moroccan Soup
text: all recipes / soup moroccan soup tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × if you have almost nothing left over, there is a recipe for a moroccan red lentil soup that may be printed in the soups folder, or online under "other recipes." yield: ~48 servings equipment largest soup pot, filled to ~15-16 qts ingredients ~2 qts leftover rice pilaf (or make more) ~7 qts or more leftover moroccan stew as needed: more canned tomatoes, better than bouillon mixed per jar instructions, any leftover veggies that fit, maybe some raisins or dried apricots up to 2-4 qts dry red lentils, if very short preparation if you've added so much that it's bland, sauté some more onions — see the original recipe for ideas on spices to add. bring to a full boil, turn off the fire, and put the lid on — it will stay hot until 5:00. serve with yogurt if you have some, and cilantro if you have some.

title: Peanut Casserole
text: all recipes / entree peanut casserole tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment 2 2" hotel pans, or largest soup pot (for the ~16 qt soup version, to stay warm) ingredients leftover peanut stew leftover roasted cabbage leftover rice canned tomatoes, as needed (for soup version) any not-needed zucchini, kale, or cabbage — check with km (for soup version) frozen green beans, maybe (for soup version) better than bouillon, as needed (for soup version) more peanut butter, salt, or lemon, to adjust flavor if needed preparation for either version: chop the leftover cabbage into bite-sized pieces. for casseroles: mix or layer whatever rice, cabbage, and peanut stew you have leftover. if there's not enough to make 2 (2") casseroles (or 1-1½ if lots of 8 precepts), a soup is probably easier to pad out. cover and refrigerate. for soup: add your leftovers to the soup pot (using no more than ~2 qts rice, so it's not too thick). augment as needed to reach ~16 qts (or less if lots of 8 precepts) using canned tomatoes, any not-needed zucchini/kale/cabbage (check with km), maybe frozen green beans, and better than bouillon. consult on flavor if it's not enough — maybe more peanut butter, salt, or lemon. bring to a rapid boil, turn off the fire, and put the lid on — the big pots will stay warm until 5:00. about 3:50: reheat the casseroles during the talk; they're done when they reach 165°f.

title: Sesame Noodle or Rice Salad
text: all recipes / salad sesame noodle or rice salad tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × km has 2 choices here: rice or noodles, peanut or sesame/ginger dressing. (consider nut allergies.) yield: ~48 servings equipment rice cooker or 20qt w/ pasta insert large sauce pan large skillet vitamix huge salad bowl to mix 2nd-largest bowl to serve ingredients either: 6 cups raw short grain brown rice (assume cooked the day before) or: 5 boxes annie chun brown-rice noodles 3 lbs asparagus, cut into 1” pieces, blanched ~2 lbs snap peas or snow peas, cut in half or thirds, raw 3 lbs carrots, small dice, blanched (or can use 2-3 cups shredded) saved broccoli stems, small dice, blanched 1 pack frozen peas (use raw, or could sub chopped green beans if no peas) 2 whole cucumbers, small dice 4 bunches scallions, sliced small ¾ cup toasted white sesame seeds (& more in dressing, see below) dressing: choose either sesame ginger or peanut sesame (filed under salad dressings) optional side: 2 little jars pickled ginger optional side: bowl of chopped cilantro & mint mixed with a little oil preparation make rice or noodles: easiest to do the day before if not using a rice cooker. if using noodles, do it on the day in the 20qt pasta cooker insert — add some sesame oil to the boiling water, then drain & rinse with cold water. make dressing: also easy to do the day before. choose either sesame peanut dressing or sesame ginger dressing. consider peanut allergies — maybe save some undressed salad & toss with simple oil, rice vinegar & ginger. prep veggies: cut up veggies as specified in the ingredients list. steam just a little, still slightly crunchy: carrots, broccoli stems, asparagus. leave raw: snap or snow peas, frozen peas, cucumber. prep seeds: using a large skillet, spread out a total of 1 cup white sesame seeds. put on a low flame and watch carefully. remove when just lightly brown. some go in the dressing, some in the salad. toss: toss all veggies, grain, and (setting aside a nut-allergy portion?) dressing in one of the super-huge salad bowls. transfer to the next-largest bowl to serve. cover, refrigerate & re-toss before serving. ideal to take out of the fridge at 3:50 & let it come nearer to room temp.

title: Shepherds Pie
text: all recipes / entree shepherds pie tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment 2 2” hotel pans, or ~16 qts soup in the largest soup pot (to stay warm) ingredients leftover peanut stew leftover roasted cabbage leftover rice preparation for either: chop up the leftover cabbage into bite-sized pieces. for casseroles: mix or layer whatever you have leftover of rice, cabbage and peanut stew. if not enough to make 2 2” casseroles (or 1-1½ if a lot of 8 precepts), a soup is probably easier to pad out. cover & fridge. for soup: add your leftovers to the soup pot (using no more than ~2 qts rice, i.e. not too thick). augment as needed to have ~16 qts (or less if lots of 8 precepts) using: canned tomatoes any not-needed zucchini or kale or cabbage? (check with km) maybe frozen green beans? better than bouillon consult on flavor if not enough (maybe more peanut butter? salt? lemon?) bring to a rapid boil, turn off the fire, put the lid on — the big pots will stay warm until 5:00. at 3:50: reheat casseroles during the talk, done when 165 degrees.

title: Spinach Salad
text: all recipes / salad spinach salad tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings equipment serving bowls large baking sheet ingredients 3 ½ cups pumpkin seeds (roasted, see below) 3 lbs (¾ of the bucket) feta cheese, crumbled (save leftover & rest for lentil salad day) 2 (29oz) cans garbanzo beans, drained ~4-5 cups kalamata olives, drained (check if leftovers in fridge) 4 pints cherry tomatoes, rinsed (may be located in pantry), halved if time 1 case baby spinach (supper yogi will prep this) 2 small pitchers balsamic dressing (should be leftover from before) preparation toast pumpkin seeds: do this first thing to finish using the oven early. turn on oven to 350 (can put seeds in before preheated). spread seeds on a baking sheet and roast for 15-20 mins until they start lightly browning. check and stir at 10 mins. setup rest: set up leftover balsamic dressing in 2 small pitchers, cover with plastic and put in fridge. set up all other sides (except spinach). cover and label. put tomatoes and seeds in the pantry, rest in fridge together on the "supper" shelf.

title: Thai Casserole
text: all recipes / entree thai casserole tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48 servings equipment 2 2” hotel pans ingredients ~6 qts leftover rice, or make more ~7 qts leftover thai veggies (or add more from freezer) maybe more other leftover veggies if any, or more frozen veg, or canned tomatoes, or more tofu, extra spinach if not needed for salad, or more coconut milk as needed preparation mix or layer whatever you have of the above into the 2 casseroles. cover & fridge. at 3:50: reheat during the talk, done when 165 degrees.

title: Thai Cauliflower Soup
text: all recipes / soup thai cauliflower soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × this is usually prepped on opening day but served at first full day's supper. best idea is to get it all made except for the "final touches" on opening day or even the day before (as soon as you have the produce), then reheat it on the first full day when the big 32 qt pot is available — it will keep hot all afternoon. yield: ~48 servings ingredients 10 hds (1 case minus 2) cauliflower: 2 heads cut into edible-size flowerets, 8 heads rough chopped for later blending (set aside the other 2 from the case of 12 for another recipe later) 5 lbs yellow onions, diced medium 1 ½ cups ginger, minced in small cuisinart 30 cloves garlic, minced in small cuisinart 2-3 fresh jalapeno peppers, seeded, chopped fine (optional) ~¾ cup fresh lime juice (maybe ~10 limes), and zest of ~5 of them ⅔ cup yellow thai curry paste ⅔ of a large can coconut milk simple stock: 1 jar bouillon, mixed with ~3 qts hot tea machine water to dissolve, plus more water or lemongrass stock (see below) to a total of ~16 quarts of soup (of soup, not just of stock — maybe ~6 qts stock total) 1 bu optional scallions, chopped white & light green parts 2 bags frozen peas salt, to taste at the end optional, for ambitious cooks with extra time — make stock with ~20 lemon grass stalks, ?galangal, kaffir lime leaves preparation sauté: sauté onions until, add ginger, garlic, jalapenos & sauté a minute or so. add ingredients and cook: add the rough-chopped cauliflower and stock (either diluted bouillon or fancy) to not quite cover the cauliflower, and let cook until the cauliflower is soft. blend with an immersion blender until smooth. add curry paste & blend that in. add the florets. this should now be about noon: insure it's over 170°, put a lid on it, turn off the gas, and it will stay hot all afternoon (or cool and save to reheat when needed). final touches (at 5:00pm): test temp, put it on a flame disperser and turn the gas back on to low/med. if time: heat the coconut milk in a sauce pan enough to melt the fat, but not to boil, then add it in. make sure it is ~165° but try not to let it come back to a boil (it separates the coconut milk). add lime zest and juice to taste. add salt to taste if needed. ~5 mins before serving: add the peas (probably thawing in the fridge). serve with cilantro (listed under the salad prep — they both call for it) and optionally the chopped scallions.

title: Thai Salad
text: all recipes / salad thai salad tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × this is to be served with 1 batch of peanut lime dressing (see salad dressings). yield: ~48 servings equipment serving bowls ingredients ½ large or 1 small red cabbage, shredded in robocoupe or by hand 1 napa cabbage, shredded (easiest by hand) 2 lbs frozen green beans, steamed until thawed and edible 2 cups mint leaves, chopped (check garden if not ordered) 2 cups shredded carrots (take from salad bar supply) mung bean sprouts (optional, if we bought some) baby kale — add to the above to make a full medium-sized salad bowl 2 lbs peanuts, served whole on the side 3 bu chopped cilantro, on the side (optional — also good with the soup, so may be offered there instead) preparation mix all except cilantro & peanuts. serve those and the dressing on the side.

title: Vegan Cheesy Broccoli Soup
text: all recipes / soup vegan cheesy broccoli soup tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × ideally put the cashews to soak at breakfast so they're ready to use by 9:30 — the soup is fine but just grittier if not pre-soaked. yield: ~48 servings equipment largest 32 quart stock pot vitamix immersion blender ingredients 5 cups cashews, soaked in water to cover by about 2” 1 case broccoli, rough chop heads into florets/chunks (optional: could trim some stems and chop — trim very deeply, be sure to get all the tough stringy stuff off) 4 lbs yukon-type potatoes, 1” cubed (or a bit larger is ok) 4 lbs onions, medium diced ¾ cup minced garlic (use mini cuisinart) 2 cups nutritional yeast 1 lemon, juice and zest 1 jar better than bouillon ~6 quarts water — use ~3 quarts from the hot tea urn into a metal pitcher to dissolve the bouillon, then add the other 3 qts cold salt & pepper, to taste (maybe white pepper?) optional: cheddar and vegan cheddar, served on the side preparation prep: blend cashews in their water in the vitamix until smooth. mix bouillon with 3 quarts hot tea urn water. chop garlic in the mini-cuisinart. put a heat-deflector under the pot. sauté onions in olive oil, add garlic when onions are soft, watch so it doesn't burn. add liquids: add broth, yeast & cashew blend to the onions. mix. add rest: add potatoes, (most of the) broccoli, & the rest of the water. you may need to cook down the broccoli a bit to fit it all in (it all reduces down a lot when done & blended). use the big wooden paddle to turn the ingredients so all the broccoli gets cooked. cook until the broccoli and potatoes are soft enough to eat and the temp is ≥ 180°. blend: using the large immersion blender, blend the soup. maybe put the pot on the floor or on a step stool — easier to hold the big blender. season: add lemon juice and zest, salt and pepper to taste. get back to ~180°, turn off the burner, put on the lid, and leave on the stove for supper.

title: Vegan Cornbread
text: all recipes / side vegan cornbread tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: ~48-50 servings (4 half-pans), or ~36 servings if using 3 half-pans (quantities were recently upped to fill 4 half-pans) equipment 4 half-sized 2” hotel pans (cooks more evenly than 2 full-size) 2 large mixing bowls 2 small mixing bowls ingredients 1 ⅓ cup (1 cup for 36) vegan egg replacer, in pantry baking box (note: bob's v-egg has soy, the "ener-g" box brand doesn't — prefer that one) or ground flax seed, in freezer 4 cups (3 cups for 36) warm water, for the flax or vegan egg 7 ½ cups (5 ½ cups + 2 tbls for 36) rice milk (or alternative milk of choice, check allergies) ¾ cup + 1 t (½ cup + 1 tbls + 2 tsp for 36) apple cider vinegar 10 ⅔ cups (8 cups for 36) gluten-free flour 10 ⅔ cups (8 cups for 36) bob's medium grind cornmeal (check pantries for ~32oz bags; can use polenta if none — the medium grind makes it lighter) 3 t + 1 ½ tsp (2 t + 2 t for 36) salt ½ cup + 1 ½ t (¼ cup + 3 tbls + ¼ tsp for 36) baking powder 4 ¾ tsp (3 ½ tsp for 36) baking soda 2 ⅔ cups (2 cups for 36) canola oil 2 ⅔ cups (2 cups for 36) pumpkin pulp (canned/boxed) 2 ⅔ cups (2 cups for 36) brown sugar (not honey, to keep it vegan) preparation heat oven to 375 degrees. grease pans. mix v-egg or ground flax and warm water separately, let set for 5-10 minutes to thicken (will need to whisk the v-egg). mix alternative milk of choice and vinegar and let set while preparing other ingredients. in a large mixing bowl, mix dry ingredients: cornmeal, gf flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt in one bowl. in a separate mixing bowl, mix together oil, pumpkin, sweetener, "milk" mixture, and flax mixture. leave wets and drys separate until just ready to go in the oven. mix just until combined, being careful not to overmix. place mixture into 3 or 4 half-sized 2-inch-deep hotel pans (stored on the island near the pantry door). bake for 40-50 min, or until golden brown and cooked in the center — test by patting for firmness or checking that a toothpick/knife comes out clean. start checking after 30 mins.

title: Sweet Potato Hummus
text: all recipes / side sweet potato hummus tags: vegan, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × adapted from martha stewart on the web. yield: ~4 cups ingredients 1 pound sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces (if starting from leftover baked ones: just peel and mash, try about 2 cups) 1 can (19.5 ounces) chickpeas, drained and rinsed 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice (from 1 lemon) 1/4 cup tahini 2 tablespoons olive oil 2 teaspoons ground cumin 1 garlic clove, chopped coarse salt and ground pepper whole-wheat pita and crudites such as red pepper and broccoli, for serving

title: Tarragon Dressing
text: all recipes / salad tarragon dressing tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × instructions below are for making a double batch. equipment two vitamix containers smallest skillet, for poaching garlic ingredients 1 cup water 6 cloves garlic (12 total for both containers — poached first, see preparation) 3 1/2 cup canola oil, plus additional oil to cover the garlic for poaching 2 cup rice vinegar ¼ cup honey ¼ cup dijon mustard 1 box tarragon (approx. ½ cup) preparation gather all ingredients below and two vitamix containers. you will double this recipe: add the ingredients to the first vitamix container, then repeat with the second container. add 1 cup water to each vitamix container. add 3 1/2 cup canola oil to each vitamix container. poach garlic: place 12 whole garlic cloves in the smallest skillet and cover with canola oil. simmer on medium heat for about 5 minutes — watch closely. add 6 cloves and half the oil to each vitamix container (adding it to the cool oil/water prevents the garlic from further cooking). rinse the tarragon and pick the leaves off the stems. add remaining ingredients to the first vitamix container. repeat with the second vitamix container. blend all ingredients. fill 2 small pitchers with each salad dressing made.

title: Tarragon Dressing
text: all recipes / salad tarragon dressing tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × instructions below are for making a double batch. equipment vitamix container a second 2 or 4 quart container with lid ingredients 1 cup water 1 tsp garlic powder (on spice shelf far left) 3 ¾ cup canola oil 2 cup rice vinegar ¼ cup honey ¼ cup dijon mustard 1 box tarragon (approx. ½ cup, fine to use the whole box) preparation gather all ingredients below, the vitamix container, and a second 2 or 4 quart container with lid. you will double this recipe by putting a set of the ingredients in each container — it's easiest to add each ingredient to both containers, then move on to the next ingredient. rinse 2 boxes of tarragon and pick the leaves off the stems, then divide the pile back in half. add the ingredients list (above) to each container. blend the contents of the vitamix container using the vitamix. fill 2 small pitchers with it. pour the second set of ingredients into the vitamix container and mix it. pour the mixed dressing back into the container, cover, label, and put in the fridge.

title: Tarragon Salad Dressing
text: all recipes / salad tarragon salad dressing tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × note: you may be asked to make 2 batches — read the instructions below before starting. the quantities here are for one batch. yield: ~48 servings per batch equipment vitamix 2 pitchers extra 2 qt square container with green lid, for a second batch ingredients 1 ½ cup rice vinegar 1 ½ cup water 1 tsp garlic powder ¼ cup dijon mustard ¼ cup agave ½ tsp salt ½ clamshell fresh tarragon leaves, picked off from stems (could use ~1 ½ tsp dry if no fresh — taste for quantity) ½ bunch fresh parsley, cut off the main trunk of stems, ok to use the rest (=~½ cup packed down) 3 ½ cups light olive oil preparation rinse herbs — no need to chop, the vitamix will do it. add all ingredients except the oils to the vitamix container and mix on low. if making 2 batches, measure a second batch (except oils) into the square container. drizzle the oils into the vitamix while mixing. gradually increase speed until all emulsified. divide between 2 small pitchers. for a second batch: pour the measured container ingredients into the vitamix and blend. add the second batch of oils as above. pour back into the container, label, date, and store in the fridge for later.

title: Tarragonl Dressing
text: all recipes / salad tarragonl dressing tags: vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × updated by chris 7/30/2015 for a bit milder & less. instructions below are for making a double batch. equipment vitamix container a second 2 quart (smallest square) container with lid ingredients 1 ½ cups rice vinegar 1 ½ cups water 1 tsp garlic powder (on spice shelf far left) ¼ cup honey (tip: coat the cup with oil, honey slides right out) ¼ cup dijon mustard ½ tsp salt ½ clamshell fresh tarragon (could use ~1 ½ tsp dry if no fresh) ½ bunch fresh parsley (approx. ½ cup packed down) 3 ½ cups canola oil preparation gather all ingredients below, the vitamix container, and a second 2 quart (smallest square) container with lid. you will double this recipe by putting a set of the ingredients in each container — it's easiest to add each ingredient to both containers, then move on to the next ingredient. rinse the tarragon. add the ingredients list (above) to each container. blend the contents of the vitamix container using the vitamix. fill 2 small pitchers with it. pour the second set of ingredients into the vitamix container and mix it. pour the mixed dressing back into the container, cover, label, and put in the fridge.

title: Thai Noodle Salad Recipe Feasting At Home
text: all recipes / salad thai noodle salad recipe feasting at home tags: vegetarian, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × recipe by sylvia fountaine of feasting at home. a simple delicious recipe for thai noodle salad with peanut sauce, loaded up with healthy veggies. vegan and gluten free, this make-ahead salad is perfect for midweek lunches or large gatherings. add sesame ginger tofu for added protein. yield: 6-8 servings (prep 15 min, cook 15 min, total 30 min) ingredients 6 ounces dry noodles (brown rice noodles, pad thai style rice noodles, soba noodles, or linguine) 4 cups mix of red cabbage, carrots, and radish, shredded or grated 1 red bell pepper, finely sliced 3 scallions, sliced 1/2 bunch cilantro, chopped (or sub basil and mint) 1 tablespoon (or less, or more) jalapeño, finely chopped 1/4-1/2 cup roasted, crushed peanuts (optional garnish) thai peanut sauce (you may not need all of it — save extras for another use): 5 thin slices ginger, cut across the grain, about the size of a quarter 2 cloves garlic 1/2 cup peanut butter (or sub almond butter) 1/2 cup fresh orange juice (roughly 1 large orange) 1/3 cup fresh lime juice (roughly 2 limes) 1/4 cup soy sauce or gf braggs liquid amino acids (note: tamari will turn this unpleasantly dark) 1/3 cup honey, agave, or maple syrup 1/4 cup toasted sesame oil 1-1 1/2 teaspoons cayenne pepper (or a squirt of sriracha sauce) 1 teaspoon salt optional: baked sesame ginger tofu, added for extra protein preparation cook noodles: (see notes for rice noodles) cook pasta according to package directions. drain and chill under cold running water, then drain again. peanut sauce: while the noodles are cooking, add all the peanut sauce ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth. (can be done up to 3 days ahead and refrigerated.) prep your veggies: slice, grate, and chop. combine: place shredded veggies, bell pepper, scallions, cilantro, and jalapeño into a serving bowl. toss. add the cold noodles to the bowl and toss again. pour some peanut sauce over top and toss well to combine — no need to use all of it, just enough to coat it well, generously. (save any extra sauce for leftover salad, as it can soak up the sauce overnight.) taste: adjust the salt to your liking, add chili flakes if you want, or more lime, and serve, garnishing with roasted peanuts, cilantro, and a lime wedge. notes rice noodles: if cooking pad-thai-style rice noodles, pour boiling water over the noodles in a baking dish, let soak until softened, then drain. salad will keep 4 days in the fridge. nutrition (per serving) serving size: 1 cup calories: 214 sugar: 10 g sodium: 280.5 mg fat: 9.8 g saturated fat: 1.6 g carbohydrates: 29.9 g fiber: 2 g protein: 2.9 g cholesterol: 0 mg source: feastingathome.com/thai-noodle-salad-with-peanut-sauce

title: Thai Noodle Salad with Peanut Sauce
text: all recipes / salad thai noodle salad with peanut sauce tags: vegetarian, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × recipe by sylvia fountaine of feasting at home. a simple delicious recipe for thai noodle salad with peanut sauce, loaded up with healthy veggies. vegan and gluten free, this make-ahead salad is perfect for midweek lunches or large gatherings. add sesame ginger tofu for added protein. yield: 6-8 servings per the original recipe (prep 15 min, cook 15 min, total 30 min); ingredient quantities below are scaled ×6 for irc, with the original single-batch amount noted in parentheses ingredients 36 oz dry noodles (6 oz in original recipe) — brown rice noodles, pad thai style rice noodles, soba noodles, or linguine 24 cups mix of red cabbage, carrots, and radish, shredded or grated (4 cups in original) 6 red bell peppers, finely sliced (1 in original) 18 scallions, sliced (3 in original) 3 bu cilantro, chopped (1/2 bunch in original) (or sub basil and mint) 6 tbsp jalapeño, finely chopped (1 tbsp in original, or less, or more) 3 cups roasted, crushed peanuts, optional garnish (1/4-1/2 cup in original) thai peanut sauce (you may not need all of it — save extras for another use): 30 thin slices ginger, cut across the grain, about the size of a quarter (5 slices in original) 12 cloves garlic (2 in original) 3 cups peanut butter, or sub almond butter (1/2 cup in original) 3 cups fresh orange juice, roughly 1 large orange each (1/2 cup in original) 1 cup fresh lime juice, roughly 2 limes (1/3 cup in original) 1 ½ cups soy sauce or gf braggs liquid amino acids — tamari will turn this unpleasantly dark (1/4 cup in original) 2 cups honey, agave, or maple syrup (1/3 cup in original) 1 ½ cups toasted sesame oil (1/4 cup in original) cayenne pepper, to taste (1-1 ½ teaspoons in original, or a squirt of sriracha sauce) salt, to taste (1 teaspoon in original) preparation cook noodles: (see notes for rice noodles) cook pasta according to package directions. drain and chill under cold running water, then drain again. peanut sauce: while the noodles are cooking, add all the peanut sauce ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth. (can be done up to 3 days ahead and refrigerated.) prep your veggies: slice, grate, and chop. combine: place shredded veggies, bell pepper, scallions, cilantro, and jalapeño into a serving bowl. toss. add the cold noodles to the bowl and toss again. pour some peanut sauce over top and toss well to combine — no need to use all of it, just enough to coat it well, generously. (save any extra sauce for leftover salad, as it can soak up the sauce overnight.) taste: adjust the salt to your liking, add chili flakes if you want, or more lime, and serve, garnishing with roasted peanuts, cilantro, and a lime wedge. optional: add baked sesame ginger tofu — made with soy sauce (or coconut aminos or tamari), sesame oil, miso, ginger, garlic, and chili paste; marinate, then bake at 400°f for 30-35 minutes. notes rice noodles: if cooking pad-thai-style rice noodles, pour boiling water over the noodles in a baking dish, let soak until softened, then drain. salad will keep 4 days in the fridge. nutrition (per serving, original recipe) serving size: 1 cup calories: 214 sugar: 10 g sodium: 280.5 mg fat: 9.8 g saturated fat: 1.6 g carbohydrates: 29.9 g fiber: 2 g protein: 2.9 g cholesterol: 0 mg

title: Thin Mint Cookies
text: all recipes / dessert thin mint cookies tags: vegan, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: makes 65 cookies ingredients 1 ¼ cups all-purpose flour (or gluten-free all-purpose flour) 1 cup sugar ½ cup cocoa powder ¼ teaspoon salt ¼ teaspoon baking soda ¾ cup vegan margarine 3 tablespoons soy, almond, or rice milk 1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract ½ teaspoon pure peppermint extract chocolate coating (coats about half the cookies, ~32): 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips (dairy-free) 1 tablespoon vegan margarine ½ teaspoon peppermint extract preparation cookies: in a food processor, pulse flour, sugar, cocoa powder, salt, and baking soda until combined. add margarine, milk, vanilla, and mint extract. pulse a few more times until the mixture comes together. transfer the mixture to a large bowl and knead it with your hands until it comes together and all the flour is incorporated. chill the dough in the refrigerator for 1 hour. preheat the oven to 350°f and line two large baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone baking mats. remove the dough from the refrigerator. roll a heaping teaspoon of cookie dough into a ball and place onto the prepared baking sheets, leaving about 3 inches between each ball. evenly flatten the dough with your fingertips so that it is about ¼ inch thick and bake for 12-14 minutes. let cool completely. chocolate coating: melt the chocolate chips and margarine in a double boiler or microwave. stir in the mint extract and mix until smooth. dip the completely cooled cookies into the chocolate.

title: Thin Mint Cookies
text: all recipes / dessert thin mint cookies tags: vegan, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: makes 65 cookies ingredients 1¼ cups all-purpose flour (or gluten-free all-purpose flour) 1 cup sugar ½ cup cocoa powder ¼ teaspoon salt ¼ teaspoon baking soda ¾ cup vegan margarine 3 tablespoons soy, almond, or rice milk 1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract ½ teaspoon pure peppermint extract chocolate coating (coats about half the cookies, ~32): 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips (dairy-free) 1 tablespoon vegan margarine ½ teaspoon peppermint extract preparation to make the cookies: in a food processor, pulse flour, sugar, cocoa powder, salt, and baking soda until combined. add margarine, milk, vanilla, and mint extract. pulse a few more times until the mixture comes together. transfer the mixture to a large bowl and knead it with your hands until it comes together and all the flour is incorporated. chill the dough in the refrigerator for 1 hour. preheat the oven to 350 degrees f and line two large baking sheets with parchment paper or silpats. remove dough from refrigerator. roll a heaping teaspoon of cookie dough into a ball and place onto prepared baking sheets, leaving about 3 inches in between each ball. evenly flatten the dough with your fingertips so that it is about ¼ inch thick and bake for 12-14 minutes. let cool completely. to make the chocolate coating: melt chocolate chips and margarine in a double boiler or microwave. stir in the mint extract and mix until smooth. dip completely cooled cookies into the chocolate.

title: TOFU scramble for no
text: all recipes / entree tofu scramble for no tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × yield: 2 servings ingredients 1 teaspoon nutritional yeast 1/4 teaspoon turmeric 1/4 teaspoon ground cumin 1/4 teaspoon paprika 1 tablespoon water pinch sea salt 1/8 teaspoon black pepper olive oil spray 1 scallion, finely diced 1 clove garlic, minced 1/2 package firm tofu, very well drained 1 tablespoon very finely chopped parsley preparation in a small bowl, mix together nutritional yeast, turmeric, cumin, paprika, water, salt, and pepper. set aside. mist a frying pan with olive oil and place it over medium heat. once hot, add scallion and garlic, and saute until fragrant, about 2 minutes. crumble tofu into the pan, breaking it up with your fingers. pour seasoning over tofu and mix well, trying to color as much tofu as possible. cook for 2 minutes or until tofu is hot throughout. toss in parsley and continue to stir for another 1 to 2 minutes. once cooked, serve with favorite sides and toppings, such as sliced avocado, whole-grain crackers or toast, sliced tomato, bacon (regular or meat-free), salsa, and/or hot sauce.

title: Vegan Bacon for Potato Bar
text: all recipes / side vegan bacon for potato bar tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × equipment 3-4 large baking sheets ingredients 6 lbs tofu (amount not specified in original for the no-supper-leftovers batch), thinly sliced 1 cup liquid smoke ½ - ¾ cup nutritional yeast 3 cups tamari olive oil spray preparation arrange tofu: preheat ovens to 400 degrees. arrange tofu in one layer on baking sheets. mix marinade and bake: mix tamari and liquid smoke and spread evenly over the tofu. place tofu in oven and bake for 45-60 minutes until tofu is crispyish but not burned. remove from oven when you reach desired texture. chop and finish: once tofu is cooled, chop into small pieces to put on potatoes and add the nutritional yeast and mix.

title: Vegan (GF) Banana Choc Chip Cupcakes
text: all recipes / dessert vegan (gf) banana choc chip cupcakes tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × from vegan cupcakes take over the world . yield: ~48 cupcakes (4 dozen) — fine made all gluten-free, or make 4 dozen regular plus 1 dozen gluten-free. recipe also scales down to 1 dozen or up to 5 dozen (see ingredient notes). ingredients 2 cups mashed very ripe bananas (5 dz batch: 2½ cups; 1 dz batch: ½ cup) 5 cups flour, all-purpose or bob's 1-1 gluten free (5 dz batch: 6¼ cups; 1 dz batch: 1¼ cups) 1 tsp baking soda (5 dz batch: 1¼ tsp; 1 dz batch: ¼ tsp) 4 tsp baking powder (5 dz batch: 5 tsp; 1 dz batch: 1 tsp) 2 tsp salt (5 dz batch: 2½ tsp; 1 dz batch: ½ tsp) 3 cups granulated (regular white) sugar (5 dz batch: 3¾ cups; 1 dz batch: ¾ cup) 1⅓ cup canola oil (5 dz batch: 1⅔ cups; 1 dz batch: ¼ cup + 1½ tbsp) 2⅔ cups rice milk (5 dz batch: 3⅓ cups; 1 dz batch: ½ cup + 3 tbsp) 6 tsp vanilla extract (5 dz batch: 8 tsp; 1 dz batch: 2 tsp) optional: almond extract — 2 tsp for the 5 dz batch, ½ tsp for the 1 dz batch (not typically used for the 4 dz batch, but good with it) 3 cups dark or semi-sweet chocolate chips (5 dz batch: 3¾ cups; 1 dz batch: ¾ cup) optional chocolate icing: 2½ cups confectioners' (powdered) sugar 1½ tablespoons cocoa ½ teaspoon ground cinnamon 7 tablespoons earth balance, melted (~40 secs in microwave) 3 tablespoons soy or rice milk (check diets) 1½ teaspoons vanilla extract preparation preheat oven to 350. line 4 muffin tins with paper cupcake liners. mash bananas until quite smooth. sift/mix flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and sugar in a large bowl and mix (or just mix — we never sift). in a separate bowl, whisk together the oil, rice milk, vanilla, (almond), and mashed banana. fold wet ingredients into dry ingredients, mixing to just combine (don't over mix). fold in chocolate chips. fill liners ⅔ full. you could add a couple of choc chips to top each one. bake for 20-22 minutes (maybe more in our right oven) until inserted knife or toothpick comes out clean. cool completely on wire rack. (if not for today, store in a lidded ant-proof container!) optional chocolate icing: place sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl. add the melted earth balance, soy milk, and vanilla and stir with a fork until smooth. let it come back to room temp to judge consistency — the mixture should look opaque; if it looks too liquid, add a little extra powdered sugar. best kept at room temp unless overnight, then refrigerate and bring back to room temp before using. pipe on with a sandwich-type plastic bag with one tip-end cut off a small bit. enough for a squiggle on each of 5 dozen.

title: Vegan (GF) Pumpkin Choc Chip Cupcakes
text: all recipes / dessert vegan (gf) pumpkin choc chip cupcakes tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × adapted from vegan cupcakes take over the world , by isa chandra moskowitz et al. yield: ~48 cupcakes (4 dozen); recipe author notes getting 5 dozen out of this batch ingredients 4 cups canned pumpkin (hint: 2 cans ≈ 3½ cups, so if you have leftover baked yams, mash some of those to save opening a third can) 1⅓ cup canola oil 4 cups granulated (regular white) sugar 1 cup rice milk 4 tsp vanilla extract 5 cups all-purpose flour or bob's "1-1" gluten free flour 2 tsp baking powder 2 tsp baking soda 2 tsp cinnamon 1 tsp salt 3 cups chocolate chips (about 1½ bags; use a few more to put 1-2 on top of each one) optional cinnamon icing: 2½ cups confectioners' (powdered) sugar 1½ teaspoons ground cinnamon 7 tablespoons earth balance, melted (~40 secs in microwave) 3 tablespoons soy or rice milk (check diets) 1½ teaspoons vanilla extract preparation preheat oven to 350. line 4-5 muffin tins with paper cupcake liners. in a bowl, mix well the flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon and salt. in a separate bowl, stir together pumpkin, oil, sugar, rice milk and vanilla. mix well, then stir in chocolate chips. add dry to wet and stir with a fork. fill liners ⅔ full. you could add a couple of choc chips to top each one, especially if not icing. bake for 20-25 minutes (maybe more in our right oven) until they are looking lightly browned and an inserted knife or toothpick comes out clean. cool completely on wire rack. (if not for today, store in a lidded ant-proof container!) optional cinnamon icing: place sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl. add the melted earth balance, soy milk, and vanilla and stir with a fork until smooth. let it come back to room temp to judge consistency — the mixture should look opaque; if it looks too liquid, add a little extra powdered sugar. best kept at room temp unless overnight, then refrigerate and bring back to room temp before using. pipe on with a sandwich-type plastic bag with one tip-end cut off a small bit. enough for a squiggle on each of 5 dozen.

title: Vegan GF Cornbread
text: all recipes / side vegan gf cornbread tags: vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, soy-free source: insight retreat center scale recipe: ½× 1× 2× 3× or × adapted from nisha vora, rainbowplantlife.com. this fits nicely in two 2" deep hotel pans, each cut 6x8. this can take a couple of hours of off-and-on attention from someone (km?), so plan for that — approximate times are noted below. measurements given in grams need a precision scale (there's one, or more, above the spice shelf that looks like an ipad). yield: two 2" deep hotel pans, each cut 6x8 ingredients ½ gallon oatly full fat oat milk (from whole foods) 4 tbls apple cider vinegar 1170g stone-ground medium corn meal (not the polenta, that's too coarse) 564g gluten free all-purpose flour 8 tbls (½ cup) baking powder 3 tsp salt 336g vegan butter, melted 336g extra virgin olive oil 240g brown sugar 504g agave 24g (6 tbls) finely chopped rosemary (use spice grinder), from the kitchen garden preparation (timing below aims for the cornbread to still be warm when served.) preheat oven to 400 (with the vulcan, try 450 and watch it). (~10:15) stir vinegar and oat milk and set aside at least 10-20 minutes to curdle. in a large bowl combine flour, cornmeal, baking powder and salt. whisk well. (~10:30) pour in the melted vegan butter, oil, brown sugar, agave, and curdled oat milk. careful not to overmix, some lumps ok. should look like pancake mix. fold in the rosemary. allow batter to rest 10 min to 1 hour. (~11:10) heat the empty pans in the oven while the batter is resting, about 10 minutes. remove from oven, add more lumps of vegan butter to melt and coat the pan. sprinkle pan bottom with cornmeal. pour in batter, dividing between the 2 pans. (~11:20) bake 25-35 minutes (in the vulcan, rotate front/back and top/bottom halfway through; might take longer than 25). test with a toothpick or knife. cool for 15 minutes before slicing, 5x8 per pan.
